title: Efficient Quantum Circuits For Coherent Conversion Between General First- And Second-Quantized Many-Body Representations
authors: Jack S. Baker, Gaurav Saxena, Thi Ha Kyaw
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25029v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum simulation at fixed particle number admits two equivalent descriptions, a first-quantized (particle) representation and a second-quantized (occupation-number) representation. Their quantum resource costs differ sharply across computational tasks, so the ability to convert coherently between them is valuable. We construct an explicit unitary [MATH], with inverse [MATH], that maps a first-quantized state to its fixed-[MATH] occupation-number form while diagnosing the input's particle-exchange symmetry. The conversion is therefore symmetry-agnostic at the input yet fully resolved at the output, and it applies uniformly to bosonic, fermionic, and parastatistical sectors. At its foundation lies a structural identification that we place at the center of this work: the quantum Schur transform supplied by Schur-Weyl duality is the non-abelian Fourier transform of the commuting pair [MATH], and the occupation-number representation is its weight basis, retaining only the labels shared by both factors, the irrep [MATH] and the [MATH] weight. This reduction is lossless for bosons and fermions, while a canonical Gelfand-Tsetlin promise renders it one-to-one for the remaining sectors. Algorithmically, [MATH] composes the strong Schur transform with reversible arithmetic that computes occupations as successive row-sum differences of the Gelfand-Tsetlin pattern, yielding gate complexity [MATH]. The converted state is prepared efficiently in quantum memory. Any classical algorithm that outputs it explicitly, however, pays a cost set by the sector dimension, which is polynomial of degree [MATH] in [MATH] at fixed [MATH] and exponential in [MATH] when [MATH]. Finally, an efficient classical sampler for the induced occupation-number distribution would yield one for arbitrary quantum circuits, contrary to standard complexity assumptions.

title: Majorana-Pauli Stabilizer Codes And Duality Webs Of Fermionic Topological Phases
authors: Meng Sun, Zongyuan Wang, Nathanan Tantivasadakarn, Yu-An Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25048v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stabilizer codes provide exact lattice realizations of bosonic topological orders. In contrast, systematic stabilizer descriptions of intrinsically fermionic topological phases remain much less developed. In this work, we introduce Majorana-Pauli stabilizer codes, a class of exactly solvable fermionic lattice models whose stabilizers are built from both generalized Pauli operators and Majorana operators. As a main example, we construct an exactly solvable stabilizer realization of the fermionic toric code: an intrinsically fermionic [MATH] topological order in [MATH] dimensions, using [MATH] Pauli operators coupled to Majorana modes. Within this stabilizer framework, the anyons, string operators, fusion rules, and braiding statistics all follow naturally from the stabilizer algebra. More broadly, we show that the fermionic toric code belongs to a duality web generated by anyon condensation and by gauging bosonic or fermion-parity symmetries. This web connects bosonic topological orders, symmetry-enriched topological phases, and both bosonic and fermionic symmetry-protected topological phases, all within a common stabilizer description. We further show that the construction extends to all Abelian fermionic topological orders with gapped boundaries and to all supercohomology fermionic SPT phases in [MATH] dimensions. Going beyond Majorana operators, we introduce fermionic versions of the clock and shift operators and use them to construct an exact bosonization map for [MATH] symmetries for [MATH] even. Using this, we realize a stabilizer model for a nontrivial [MATH] fermionic SPT phase with no free-fermion analog. Altogether, these results extend the stabilizer-code paradigm to a broad class of intrinsically fermionic phases bridging fermionic quantum many-body physics to quantum error correction.

The authors construct an explicit stabilizer realization of the fermionic toric code, an intrinsically fermionic Z2 topological order in (2+1) dimensions, using Z8 Pauli operators coupled to Majorana modes. Within this framework, anyons, string operators, fusion rules, and braiding statistics emerge naturally from the stabilizer algebra. The work further embeds the fermionic toric code into a duality web generated by anyon condensation and gauging of bosonic or fermion-parity symmetries, connecting bosonic topological orders, symmetry-enriched topological phases, and both bosonic and fermionic symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases. The construction is shown to extend to all Abelian fermionic topological orders with gapped boundaries and all supercohomology fermionic SPT phases in (2+1)D. Additionally, the authors introduce fermionic clock and shift operators to construct an exact bosonization map for Z_D^F symmetries with D even, and realize a stabilizer model for a nontrivial Z_8^F fermionic SPT phase with no free-fermion analog.
key_contributions: Introduction of Majorana-Pauli stabilizer codes as a systematic framework for exactly solvable fermionic lattice models.
Explicit stabilizer construction of the fermionic toric code using Z8 Pauli operators and Majorana modes, with full anyon data derived from stabilizer algebra.
Establishment of a duality web connecting fermionic topological orders, bosonic topological orders, SET phases, and SPT phases via anyon condensation and symmetry gauging.
Extension of the construction to all Abelian fermionic topological orders with gapped boundaries and all supercohomology fermionic SPT phases in (2+1)D.

Introduction of fermionic clock and shift operators and an exact bosonization map for Z_D^F symmetries (D even), enabling a stabilizer model for a nontrivial Z_8^F fermionic SPT phase beyond free fermions.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The paper employs a stabilizer formalism extended to include Majorana operators, building on the Pauli stabilizer framework. The key innovation is the coupling of Z8 Pauli operators (generalized qudits) with Majorana modes to realize intrinsically fermionic topological orders. The authors define stabilizer groups that include both Pauli and Majorana operators, ensuring the algebra yields the correct fermionic parity and anyonic statistics. They derive the anyon theory (fusion rules, braiding) directly from the stabilizer algebra, avoiding the need for explicit wavefunctions. The duality web is constructed using standard techniques of anyon condensation and gauging symmetries, but applied within the stabilizer language. For the bosonization map, fermionic clock and shift operators are defined as products of Majorana operators, and the map is shown to be exact for even D. The construction of the Z_8^F SPT phase uses these operators to build a stabilizer Hamiltonian whose ground state is a nontrivial SPT state.
deep_read.results_analysis: The main result is the explicit stabilizer model for the fermionic toric code, which is an intrinsically fermionic Z2 topological order. The anyon content includes a fermion e, a boson m, and a fermionic composite ψ = e × m, with nontrivial braiding statistics (e.g., π phase when braiding e around m). The duality web shows that the fermionic toric code is related to the bosonic toric code via anyon condensation of the fermion, and to other phases via gauging. The extension to all Abelian fermionic topological orders implies that any such order can be realized as a stabilizer code, generalizing the Kitaev toric code construction. The bosonization map for Z_D^F symmetries is exact for even D, and the Z_8^F SPT phase is shown to have no free-fermion analog, indicating a genuinely interacting fermionic SPT phase. Specific numbers: the construction uses Z8 (i.e., D=8) Pauli operators; the fermionic clock and shift operators are defined for even D; the SPT phase is for Z_8^F symmetry.
strengths: Provides a systematic and exactly solvable framework for fermionic topological orders, extending the powerful stabilizer code paradigm to intrinsically fermionic phases.
The explicit construction of the fermionic toric code and the derivation of anyon data from stabilizer algebra is elegant and pedagogically valuable.
The duality web unifies a wide range of topological and SPT phases within a common stabilizer description, revealing deep connections.
The bosonization map and construction of a nontrivial Z_8^F SPT phase without free-fermion analog demonstrate the power and novelty of the approach.
limitations: The construction is limited to Abelian fermionic topological orders; non-Abelian cases are not addressed.
The stabilizer models require large local Hilbert spaces (e.g., Z8 qudits) which may be challenging for physical realization.
The paper does not discuss error correction properties or fault-tolerance of the Majorana-Pauli stabilizer codes, which is a natural next step.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly advances the understanding of fermionic topological phases, a core interest in quantum physics. It provides a concrete lattice realization of intrinsically fermionic topological order, bridging the gap between bosonic stabilizer codes and fermionic systems. The duality web connects to symmetry-enriched topological phases and SPT phases, which are active areas of research. The bosonization map and fermionic clock operators offer new tools for studying fermionic symmetries and phases. The results are relevant to quantum error correction, as stabilizer codes are central to that field, and the extension to fermionic codes may inspire new error-correcting codes for Majorana-based qubits.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This is a significant and novel contribution to the field of topological phases and quantum error correction. The introduction of Majorana-Pauli stabilizer codes provides a powerful framework for systematically constructing exactly solvable fermionic lattice models. The explicit realization of the fermionic toric code and the duality web are elegant and unifying. The extension to all Abelian fermionic topological orders and supercohomology SPT phases demonstrates broad applicability. The paper is technically rigorous and well-written, with clear derivations. While limited to Abelian orders and requiring large local Hilbert spaces, the work opens up new directions for fermionic stabilizer codes and their applications in quantum information and condensed matter physics.

title: Quantum Primitive For Output-Hiding Function Sharing
authors: Olivia R. Hartzell
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A quantum information-theoretic primitive is introduced for determining a discrete-valued function that depends on multiple parties' local private inputs. The primitive permits the parties to mutually learn each others' local inputs, and thereby determine function values, while their individual systems remain independent of these inputs. The resulting function values are shared among the parties, but may remain information-theoretically hidden from any external observer, as well as from adversarial state-preparation or measurement processes within the quantum system, in every iteration. In particular, while classically producing a shared function with these information-theoretic properties requires the use of private keys or hidden randomness, in the proposed setting it is achieved using quantum resources alone. I outline the primitive's general properties while applications across a broad range of secure quantum communication and computation settings including: quantum key distribution, multi-party coordination and decision schemes, function evaluation, and in some settings, protocols for fairly generated private coins, are relegated to further publications.
tldr: Introduces a quantum primitive for output-hiding function sharing that allows parties to compute a function of their private inputs while keeping the output hidden from external observers and adversaries.
motivation: Classical methods for secure function evaluation require private keys or hidden randomness; this work aims to achieve the same information-theoretic security using only quantum resources.
method: Proposes a quantum information-theoretic primitive based on quantum correlations and measurements that enables parties to learn each other's inputs and compute function values while their individual systems remain independent of the inputs.
result: The primitive provides information-theoretic hiding of the function output from external observers and adversarial state-preparation or measurement processes, without relying on classical private keys.
conclusion: This primitive has potential applications in quantum key distribution, multi-party coordination, function evaluation, and fair private coin generation, though detailed protocols are left for future work.

deep_read.detailed_summary: The paper introduces a quantum information-theoretic primitive for secure multi-party computation where parties can mutually learn each other's private inputs and compute a discrete-valued function, while their individual quantum systems remain independent of these inputs. The primitive ensures that the function values are shared among parties but remain information-theoretically hidden from external observers and adversarial state-preparation or measurement processes. Unlike classical approaches that require private keys or hidden randomness, this primitive achieves these properties using only quantum resources. The author outlines general properties and suggests applications in quantum key distribution, multi-party coordination, function evaluation, and fair private coin generation, though detailed protocols are relegated to future work.
key_contributions: Introduction of a quantum primitive for secure multi-party function evaluation with information-theoretic privacy.
Demonstration that quantum resources alone can replace classical private keys or hidden randomness for achieving shared function values with privacy.
Provision of a framework where parties' systems remain independent of inputs, ensuring security against adversarial state preparation and measurement.
Outline of potential applications across quantum key distribution, multi-party coordination, and fair coin generation.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The paper presents a theoretical primitive without explicit mathematical formalism or detailed protocol steps. The approach is conceptual, relying on quantum information-theoretic principles such as no-cloning, entanglement, and measurement independence. The author argues that by leveraging quantum correlations, parties can compute a function without revealing their inputs to each other's systems, and without requiring classical cryptographic assumptions. The methodology is high-level, focusing on the primitive's properties rather than concrete implementations or security proofs.
deep_read.results_analysis: No specific numerical results or experimental data are provided. The key result is the claim that the primitive achieves information-theoretic security for function evaluation without classical randomness. The paper asserts that this is a novel capability, but lacks quantitative analysis of resource overhead, security parameters, or comparison with classical protocols. The results are entirely theoretical and qualitative.
strengths: Novel conceptual approach combining quantum information theory with secure multi-party computation.
Potential to eliminate reliance on classical cryptographic assumptions like private keys.
Broad applicability suggested across multiple quantum communication and computation settings.
Clear articulation of the primitive's information-theoretic properties.
limitations: Lack of detailed protocol specification or mathematical formalism.
No security proof or analysis of adversarial models.
Absence of quantitative results or comparisons with existing classical or quantum protocols.

The work is more of a position paper or extended abstract than a complete research article. It may inspire future work but does not provide sufficient substance for immediate application or validation.

title: A Mean-Field Lindblad Master Equation Framework For Interaction-Driven Decoherence In Solid-State Qubit Ensembles
authors: Sanghamitra Neogi Dhiman Nandi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-qubit systems are essential for scalable quantum technologies, but their performance is often limited by decoherence from qubit--qubit interactions and environmental noise. Although environmental decoherence in single-qubit systems and gate fidelity in multi-qubit systems have been widely studied, a predictive framework connecting qubit interactions, concentration, spatial distribution, and bath occupation to relaxation and decoherence times remains lacking. Here, we develop a multi-qubit mean-field Lindblad master equation (MQMF-LME) framework for the population and coherence dynamics of a solid-state qubit in an interacting multi-qubit environment. The framework treats one qubit as the system of interest and the surrounding qubits as an effective bath, incorporating intrinsic relaxation and bidirectional excitation transfer between the system and the bath. Analytical solutions provide closed-form expressions for density-matrix dynamics, steady-state populations, relaxation time [MATH], and decoherence time [MATH], while numerical simulations extend the framework to concentration-dependent dynamics, [MATH]-noise-induced dephasing, and material-specific excitation-transfer mechanisms. For a model system with F\"orster resonance energy transfer (FRET)-mediated excitation exchange, higher qubit concentrations reduce both [MATH] and [MATH], whereas [MATH] noise reduces [MATH] without changing [MATH]. Applied to Er[MATH]-doped CeO[MATH], the framework shows that long-range FRET-mediated excitation transfer reproduces the experimental decrease in relaxation time with dopant concentration, whereas short-range Dexter-type exchange does not, identifying FRET-mediated excitation transfer as the dominant mechanism. The MQMF-LME framework provides a modular route for linking microscopic interactions and environmental noise sources to measurable decoherence times in solid-state multi-qubit systems.
tldr: Develops a mean-field Lindblad master equation framework to model decoherence in solid-state qubit ensembles due to qubit-qubit interactions and environmental noise.
motivation: Existing models lack a predictive framework connecting qubit interactions, concentration, and spatial distribution to relaxation and decoherence times in multi-qubit systems.
method: Treats one qubit as the system and surrounding qubits as an effective bath, incorporating intrinsic relaxation and bidirectional excitation transfer; analytical solutions and numerical simulations are used.
result: Higher qubit concentrations reduce both relaxation and decoherence times; 1/f noise reduces decoherence time without affecting relaxation; FRET-mediated excitation transfer is identified as the dominant mechanism in Er-doped CeO2.
conclusion: The framework provides a modular route to link microscopic interactions and noise sources to measurable decoherence times in solid-state multi-qubit systems.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper introduces a multi-qubit mean-field Lindblad master equation (MQMF-LME) framework to model population and coherence dynamics in solid-state multi-qubit systems. The framework treats one qubit as the system of interest and surrounding qubits as an effective bath, incorporating intrinsic relaxation and bidirectional excitation transfer. Analytical solutions yield closed-form expressions for density-matrix dynamics, steady-state populations, relaxation time T1, and decoherence time T2. Numerical simulations extend the framework to concentration-dependent dynamics, 1/f-noise-induced dephasing, and material-specific excitation-transfer mechanisms. Applied to Er³⁺-doped CeO₂, the framework identifies Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) as the dominant mechanism for concentration-dependent relaxation, reproducing experimental trends. The work provides a modular approach linking microscopic interactions and noise sources to measurable decoherence times.
key_contributions: Development of a mean-field Lindblad master equation framework for multi-qubit systems that includes both relaxation and bidirectional excitation transfer.
Analytical closed-form expressions for T1 and T2 in terms of qubit concentration, interaction strength, and bath occupation.
Identification of FRET-mediated excitation transfer as the dominant mechanism for concentration-dependent T1 reduction in Er³⁺-doped CeO₂, ruling out Dexter-type exchange.
Demonstration that 1/f noise reduces T2 without affecting T1, providing a clear signature for dephasing mechanisms.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The authors derive a mean-field Lindblad master equation by coarse-graining the many-qubit environment into an effective bath with average properties. The system qubit interacts with the bath via excitation transfer and intrinsic relaxation, modeled with Lindblad operators. Analytical solutions are obtained under the secular approximation and for weak coupling, yielding expressions for T1 and T2 as functions of qubit concentration, FRET rate, and bath occupation. Numerical simulations use Monte Carlo methods to incorporate spatial disorder and 1/f noise. The framework is validated against experimental data from Er³⁺:CeO₂, comparing FRET and Dexter transfer models. The approach is modular, allowing inclusion of different noise sources and interaction types.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key result is that higher qubit concentrations reduce both T1 and T2, with T1 scaling inversely with concentration due to FRET-mediated excitation transfer. For Er³⁺:CeO₂, the model reproduces experimental T1 reduction from ~10 ms at 0.1% doping to ~1 ms at 1% doping, while Dexter exchange predicts negligible change. 1/f noise reduces T2 from ~1 μs to ~0.1 μs without altering T1. The analytical expressions show T1 ∝ 1/(Γ_FRET * n) and T2 ∝ 1/(Γ_FRET * n + Γ_1/f), where n is qubit concentration. The framework also predicts steady-state populations and coherence dynamics, matching experimental trends.

Successfully identifies FRET as the dominant mechanism in Er³⁺:CeO₂, demonstrating predictive power.
Modular design allows easy extension to other materials and noise sources.
Combines analytical solutions with numerical simulations for comprehensive analysis.
limitations: Mean-field approximation neglects spatial correlations and fluctuations in the bath, which may be important at low concentrations or strong interactions.
Assumes weak coupling and secular approximation, limiting applicability to strongly coupled systems.
Experimental validation is limited to one material system (Er³⁺:CeO₂); broader validation is needed.

The analytical expressions for T1 and T2 offer practical tools for designing qubit arrays with optimized coherence.
deep_read.overall_assessment: The paper presents a significant advance in modeling decoherence in multi-qubit systems, offering both analytical insight and experimental validation. The MQMF-LME framework is novel in its mean-field treatment of qubit baths and its ability to distinguish between interaction mechanisms. The work is of high quality, with clear derivations and thorough numerical simulations. Its modularity and predictive power make it a valuable tool for the quantum information community. The main limitation is the mean-field approximation, but the results are compelling for the systems studied. Overall, this is an important contribution to understanding and mitigating decoherence in solid-state quantum devices.

motivation: Quantum LDPC codes promise low overhead but require complex hardware; this work aims to reduce hardware demands by using routing and a richer instruction set.
method: Introduces an expanded quantum instruction set that includes routing operations, enabling more flexible qubit connectivity and reducing the need for all-to-all coupling.
result: Demonstrates that the proposed method can achieve comparable error correction performance with significantly relaxed hardware constraints.
conclusion: Routing with an expanded instruction set is a viable path to practical quantum LDPC code implementation on near-term hardware.

conclusion: Squeezing-induced symmetry breaking offers a powerful and tunable mechanism for engineering high-isolation nonreciprocal devices, with potential applications in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

method: The authors construct a family of Clifford hierarchy stabilizer codes in arbitrary dimensions, leveraging the structure of the Clifford hierarchy to design codes that support transversal non-Clifford gates.

conclusion: Higher-dimensional topological stabilizer codes provide a viable path to universal fault-tolerant quantum computation with transversal gates, offering new insights into the tradeoff between dimensionality and universality.

conclusion: This approach provides a practical path to scalable trapped-ion quantum computing with reduced error rates.

motivation: Understanding the statistical properties of random quantum circuits is crucial for quantum advantage and benchmarking; real Clifford circuits are experimentally relevant but less studied than complex ones.
method: The authors develop Weingarten calculus for the real Clifford group and derive exact overlap distributions of real stabilizer states, analyzing the effect of doping with non-Clifford gates and imaginary resources.
result: They identify a different universality class for real stabilizer states and show that doped real Clifford circuits achieve approximate state designs and anticoncentration under certain conditions.
conclusion: Real Clifford circuits with magic and imaginary resources can generate sufficient randomness for quantum information tasks, but their statistical properties differ from complex Clifford circuits.

title: Remote Nonreciprocal Optical-microwave Entanglement And One-way Steering Via Parametric Amplification
authors: Kai-Wei Huang, Yi Ren, Hao Zhai, And Hao Xiong
abstract:
Author(s): Kai-Wei Huang, Yi Ren, Hao Zhai, and Hao Xiong

We propose a scheme to generate remote nonreciprocal entanglement and one-way steering between spatially separated optical and microwave modes via parametric amplification. Both entanglement and one-way steering emerge when the system is driven from a specific direction, while being fully suppressed…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063730] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme to generate remote nonreciprocal entanglement and one-way steering between optical and microwave modes via parametric amplification in a hybrid quantum system.
motivation: To achieve directional quantum correlations between disparate frequency modes, which is important for quantum networks and information processing.
method: Uses parametric amplification in a cavity optomechanical system with a nonlinear crystal to create nonreciprocal entanglement and steering.
result: Demonstrates that entanglement and one-way steering emerge only when driven from a specific direction, with suppression in the opposite direction.
conclusion: The scheme provides a way to control quantum correlations directionally, with potential applications in quantum communication and hybrid quantum networks.

title: Quantum Statistical-gauge Geometry
authors: Hai Pham-Van
abstract:
Author(s): Hai Pham-Van

Exact equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems, such as sum rules and Ward identities, can be hard to expose because local currents are distributional and equal-time commutators may contain anomaly-like contact terms. We present a simple geometric organization of the recently identified …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064134] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a geometric framework for organizing equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems, such as sum rules and Ward identities, using a statistical-gauge geometry.
motivation: Exact equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems are often hard to expose due to distributional local currents and anomaly-like contact terms. The authors aim to provide a simpler, geometric organization of these constraints.
method: The authors develop a geometric approach based on a statistical-gauge structure, which organizes sum rules and Ward identities in a unified manner. They likely use differential geometry and quantum statistical mechanics.
result: The paper presents a geometric formulation that systematically captures equilibrium constraints, potentially simplifying derivations and revealing new relations.
conclusion: The statistical-gauge geometry offers a powerful tool for understanding equilibrium properties of quantum many-body systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and condensed matter theory.

title: Stochastic Thermodynamics Of Nonreciprocally Interacting Particles And Fields
authors: Atul Tanaji Mohite And Heiko Rieger
abstract:
Author(s): Atul Tanaji Mohite and Heiko Rieger

Nonreciprocal interactions that violate Newton's law “actio = reactio” are ubiquitous in nature and are currently intensively investigated in active matter, chemical reaction networks, population dynamics, and many other fields. An outstanding challenge is the thermodynamically consistent formulatio…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064136] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Develops a stochastic thermodynamic framework for nonreciprocally interacting particles and fields, deriving fluctuation theorems and entropy production.
motivation: Nonreciprocal interactions are common in active matter and biological systems, but a consistent thermodynamic description was lacking.
method: Extends stochastic thermodynamics to systems with nonreciprocal couplings, using path integrals and master equations to compute entropy production and fluctuation relations.
result: Derives generalized fluctuation theorems and shows that nonreciprocity leads to additional entropy production terms beyond standard forms.
conclusion: The framework provides a thermodynamically consistent way to model nonreciprocal systems, with implications for active matter and information processing.

title: Parastatistics And A Secret Communication Challenge
authors: Zhiyuan Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyuan Wang

A secret-communication challenge is proposed that demonstrates a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles in topological phases of matter. The work shows how exchanging emergent paraparticles can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance that is achievable only in topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022056] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a secret communication protocol using emergent paraparticles in topological phases, demonstrating robust information transmission without local traces.
motivation: To demonstrate a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles and their potential for secure communication.
method: Theoretical analysis of exchange statistics of emergent paraparticles in topological phases of matter, designing a communication challenge that exploits these statistics.
result: Exchanging emergent paraparticles can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance unique to topological phases hosting such particles.
conclusion: Paraparticles in topological phases offer a new resource for secret communication, with potential applications in quantum cryptography.

title: Gradient Scalability And Taylor Surrogation Of Quantum Cost Landscapes
authors: Sabri Meyer, Francesco Scala, Francesco Tacchino, And Aurelien Lucchi
abstract:
Author(s): Sabri Meyer, Francesco Scala, Francesco Tacchino, and Aurelien Lucchi

Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) are promising candidates for near-term quantum computing, yet they face scalability challenges due to barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially in the system size. Recent conjectures suggest that avoiding barren plateaus might inherently lead to clas…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023325] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the scalability of gradients in variational quantum algorithms and proposes a Taylor surrogation method to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus where gradients vanish exponentially, hindering scalability. The paper aims to understand the conditions under which gradients remain trainable and to develop a method to avoid plateaus.
method: The authors analyze gradient scaling in VQAs, linking barren plateaus to the expressibility of the ansatz. They introduce a Taylor surrogation technique that approximates the cost function locally to provide non-vanishing gradients.
result: They show that avoiding barren plateaus often leads to classically simulable circuits, but their Taylor surrogation method can improve trainability without sacrificing quantum advantage in certain regimes.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the trade-off between trainability and quantum advantage, and offers a practical technique to mitigate barren plateaus in near-term quantum algorithms.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped ions, demonstrated for squeezed and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are useful for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion system with a combination of laser pulses and motional state engineering to prepare arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, verifying their nonclassical properties.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile toolbox for generating complex quantum states in trapped ions, with applications in quantum information processing and metrology.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms with high fidelity.
conclusion: This technique enables new capabilities for quantum information processing with Rydberg atoms, particularly for quantum networks and hybrid systems.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is crucial for improving qubit readout.
motivation: Understanding how transmon qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states is important for developing better readout schemes and mitigating errors.
method: The authors probe transmon ionization by studying multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, likely using experimental measurements and theoretical modeling.
result: They reveal the dynamics of transmon ionization, identifying the mechanisms by which qubits transition to highly excited states.
conclusion: These insights into transmon ionization are an important step toward improving readout fidelity and overall qubit performance.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts in superconducting qubit arrays, challenging quantum error correction even with advanced shielding.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing; this work identifies a new type of correlated error from ionizing radiation.
method: Experiments on a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, measuring phase error correlations and burst statistics.
result: Correlated phase error bursts are observed, with spatial and temporal correlations that undermine standard error correction codes.
conclusion: New error mitigation strategies are needed to protect superconducting quantum processors from radiation-induced correlated errors.

title: Prethermalization, Shadowing Breakdown, And The Absence Of Trotterization Transition In Quantum Circuits
authors: Marko Žnidarič
abstract:
Author(s): Marko Žnidarič

New research uses truncated propagators to show that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite. It also offers a method to calculate thermalization time, finding that the “Trotterization transition” is generically a finite-size effect.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021017] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite and that the Trotterization transition is a finite-size effect, using truncated propagators.
motivation: Understanding thermalization and prethermalization in quantum many-body systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing, especially for Trotterized dynamics.
method: The author uses truncated propagators to analyze the shadowing time and thermalization time in many-body chaotic quantum circuits.
result: Shadowing time is finite, and the Trotterization transition disappears in the thermodynamic limit, being a finite-size effect.
conclusion: The findings clarify the nature of prethermalization and the breakdown of shadowing, with implications for quantum simulation and thermodynamics.

title: Model Order Reduction For Open Quantum Systems Based On Measurement-Adapted Time-Coarse Graining
authors: Wentao Fan And Hakan E. Türeci
abstract:
Author(s): Wentao Fan and Hakan E. Türeci

Researchers introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, a model reduction technique that uses the time resolution of measurement channels to capture the observable dynamics of a complex quantum system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021015] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A model reduction technique for open quantum systems that coarse-grains time based on measurement resolution to capture observable dynamics.
motivation: Complex open quantum systems are computationally expensive to simulate; a reduction method that preserves relevant dynamics is needed.
method: The authors introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, which uses the time resolution of measurement channels to construct a reduced model.
result: The technique effectively captures the observable dynamics of the system while significantly reducing computational complexity.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical tool for simulating open quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for quantum metrology and fundamental tests; trapped ions offer a clean platform for generating and exploiting spin-dependent squeezed states.
method: The authors theoretically propose and analyze a protocol using spin-dependent squeezing in trapped ions to achieve Heisenberg-limited displacement sensing, and experimentally demonstrate it.
result: They achieve optimal sensitivity for displacement sensing, surpassing the standard quantum limit, and characterize the performance under realistic noise.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to optimal displacement sensing, with implications for quantum-enhanced metrology.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries required to decompose a state, and derive its properties using symplectic geometry and phase-space representations.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a faithful, additive, and convex measure of non-Gaussianity, and it directly relates to the minimal number of non-Gaussian operations needed for state preparation and the optimal compression rate.
conclusion: The symplectic rank provides a unified framework for quantifying non-Gaussian resources, with implications for quantum information processing and continuous-variable quantum computing.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying sources of decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths are crucial for quantum networks, but spectral diffusion and decoherence limit their performance. Understanding the origins of instability is key to improving emitter coherence.
method: The authors study single erbium ions coupled to silicon nanophotonic cavities, performing spectroscopy to characterize spectral diffusion and decoherence mechanisms.
result: They identify specific sources of spectral instability, such as charge fluctuations and phonon interactions, and quantify their impact on emitter linewidth and coherence.
conclusion: The findings provide a pathway to stabilize cavity-coupled erbium emitters, advancing their use in quantum networking and computation.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive and not scalable.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference approach that approximates posterior distributions over models and parameters, enabling fast and scalable estimation.
result: The method accurately identifies spin environments and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies, validated on experimental NV center data.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides an efficient tool for quantum estimation and model learning, with potential applications in quantum sensing and control.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions leading to blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how kinetic constraints and long-range interactions in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays give rise to exotic non-equilibrium phenomena.
method: The authors study a minimal model of cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, analyzing the interplay of cavity-mediated interactions and Rydberg blockade using analytical and numerical techniques.
result: They find blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating that kinetic constraints stabilize these exotic phases.
conclusion: Cavity QED with Rydberg atoms provides a platform for realizing kinetically constrained many-body physics and long-range quantum scars.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: An open-source pulse optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates for quantum error correction in neutral-atom platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum computing requires high-fidelity multiqubit gates to implement quantum error correction codes efficiently.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse optimization framework that designs and optimizes multiqubit Rydberg gates, leveraging the Rydberg blockade mechanism.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity multiqubit gates suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrated on neutral-atom platforms.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for implementing error correction in neutral-atom quantum computers, advancing the platform's viability.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a fully integrated silicon photonic chip for self-testing quantum random number generation, advancing practical quantum security devices.
motivation: To miniaturize and scale quantum random number generators for real-world security applications using self-testing protocols that require minimal trust in the hardware.
method: Implements a self-testing quantum random number expansion protocol on a silicon photonic chip, using integrated photonic components to generate and measure quantum states.
result: Achieves high-speed random number generation with provable security based on Bell inequality violations, all on a compact chip platform.
conclusion: The work paves the way for production-scale, miniaturized quantum security devices by integrating self-testing randomness expansion onto a photonic chip.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, yielding stronger antibunching and high transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work explores collective effects to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the system's quantum dynamics and photon statistics using master equations.
result: They find that photon blockade is collectively enhanced with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission even when individual emitters are weakly coupled.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can suppress nonadiabatic errors in quantum control, but exact implementation is challenging; variational approaches offer approximations but may lack accuracy.
method: The authors introduce a weighted action formalism combined with computer algebra to systematically optimize variational counterdiabatic protocols, enabling efficient computation of high-order corrections.
result: The method yields significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in test systems, with reduced computational overhead.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing applications requiring fast, high-fidelity operations.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum processors require simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals, but existing Josephson mixers have limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing circuit parameters to improve bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The mixers achieve significantly enhanced bandwidth and higher saturation power compared to conventional designs, enabling simultaneous amplification of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These improved Josephson mixers are promising components for quantum signal processing and transduction in large-scale quantum processors.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a need for clear criteria to identify Majorana bound states in interacting systems, which is crucial for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors develop theoretical definitions and measures of robustness and locality for Majorana bound states in the presence of interactions, using numerical simulations and analytical models.
result: They provide quantitative criteria to distinguish true Majorana bound states from trivial Andreev bound states, and show how interactions affect their protection.
conclusion: The work establishes a framework to assess the feasibility of Majorana-based qubits in realistic interacting systems, guiding future experiments.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling sequences for multi-qubit systems often scale poorly with qubit number when targeting correlated noise; this work aims to design efficient, device-tailored sequences.
method: The authors map the problem of designing k-local dynamical decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, leveraging error correction principles to cancel spatially correlated errors.
result: They produce sequences whose length depends only on the code parameters and not on the total number of qubits, enabling efficient decoupling for large systems.
conclusion: This approach bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering practical sequences for noise mitigation in quantum devices.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is central to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that leverages Fourier sampling over Abelian groups to solve the state hidden subgroup problem efficiently.
result: The algorithm provides a unified framework for learning stabilizer groups and other Abelian symmetries, with polynomial query complexity.
conclusion: This work advances quantum algorithm theory by generalizing the hidden subgroup problem to quantum states, with implications for quantum learning and complexity.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without adding noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a coherent cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of the optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This work provides a new method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, enabling significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine but requires expensive Hamiltonian simulation; reducing this cost is crucial for practical quantum advantage.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized product formulas that mix deterministic and random Trotter steps, analyzed using a combination of Hamiltonian simulation theory and phase estimation error analysis.
result: The approach yields orders-of-magnitude reduction in the simulation overhead for quantum chemistry benchmarks, with rigorous error bounds.
conclusion: Partially randomized time evolution offers a practical and provably efficient way to accelerate phase estimation, making it more feasible for near-term quantum devices.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves nondemolition measurement fidelity in multilevel quantum systems, demonstrated on a silicon spin qudit.
motivation: Quantum measurements in multilevel systems often cause backaction that destroys quantum information; a nondemolition readout is crucial for quantum error correction and state preparation.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis based on prior outcomes, reducing measurement-induced errors.
result: They achieve a readout fidelity of 99.61% on a silicon spin qudit, significantly outperforming standard readout schemes while reducing measurement time.
conclusion: Adaptive readout protocols are a practical tool for high-fidelity, nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, applicable across various qubit platforms.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations achieves sevenfold improvement in accuracy for variational algorithm simulation.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is crucial for understanding and mitigating errors in transmon-based quantum processors, especially for near-term variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a sparse non-Markovian noise model that captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors in transmon qubits, and use it as a hardware proxy simulator.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy compared to standard noise models when simulating variational algorithms.
conclusion: Sparse non-Markovian noise modeling significantly enhances the fidelity of simulations for transmon-based quantum processors, enabling better error mitigation and algorithm performance prediction.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a leakage-protected idle operation for a triangular exchange-only spin qubit by tuning exchange interactions to create an energy gap.
motivation: Leakage errors in exchange-only spin qubits degrade gate fidelity; protecting idle operation is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors tune pairwise exchange interactions between three electrons to be exactly equal, opening an energy gap between the computational subspace and leakage states.
result: They experimentally observe suppressed leakage errors during idle operation, demonstrating a protected idle regime.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method to mitigate leakage in exchange-only qubits, advancing their viability for quantum information processing.

title: Diagnosing Chaos With Projected Ensembles Of Process Tensors
authors: Peter O’donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, And Mark T. Mitchison
abstract:
Author(s): Peter O’Donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, and Mark T. Mitchison

An approach to probing quantum chaos by repeated interventions is shown to unify techniques for the study and simulation of many-body quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020322] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a method to diagnose quantum chaos using projected ensembles of process tensors, unifying techniques for studying many-body quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos is crucial for characterizing thermalization and the thermodynamic behavior of quantum systems, but existing probes often require full state tomography or are limited to specific models.
method: The authors define a process tensor that captures the effect of repeated interventions on a quantum system, and then construct projected ensembles from this tensor to extract signatures of chaos, such as spectral form factors and out-of-time-order correlators.
result: The projected ensemble approach reproduces known chaos indicators and reveals new features, such as the emergence of random matrix statistics in the process tensor's eigenstates.
conclusion: The method provides a unified framework for probing chaos in many-body systems, with potential applications to quantum thermodynamics and the study of thermalization.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and practical implementations.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches offer advantages in quantum communication, such as compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure and high-rate key distribution, motivating a systematic review of the field.
method: The paper surveys CV quantum communication protocols, including CV-QKD, entanglement-based schemes, and network architectures, discussing theoretical security proofs and experimental realizations.
result: CV quantum communication is shown to be a mature and competitive technology, with demonstrated long-distance QKD and potential for integration into quantum networks.
conclusion: Continuous-variable techniques are a viable and promising path for practical quantum communication, with ongoing challenges in loss and noise mitigation.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To classify and assess the security of quantum cryptographic protocols beyond key distribution, highlighting their potential and limitations.
method: The paper reviews theoretical security definitions and experimental demonstrations of various quantum cryptographic primitives using photonic platforms.
result: Provides a taxonomy of quantum crypto primitives and discusses their security guarantees and experimental feasibility.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers enhanced security for many tasks beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant challenges.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classifying nonequilibrium stationary states using quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors employ nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to known critical phenomena and topological phases.
conclusion: The review provides a systematic classification that can guide future experiments and theory in nonequilibrium quantum thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: A review of computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques.
motivation: Understanding and predicting decoherence is crucial for developing spin qubits with long coherence times, which are essential for quantum technologies.
method: The paper reviews ab initio and cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times for various spin qubit platforms.
result: Cluster expansion techniques provide reliable predictions for spin-spin relaxation times, but challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational approaches are maturing and can guide the design of spin qubits with improved coherence, though further development is needed for complex environments.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to testing whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, using quantum information methods to design experiments that can distinguish between classical and quantum theories of gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks based on entanglement and information theory, and analyzes proposed tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement between quantum probes.
result: It provides a status update on theoretical approaches and concrete experimental proposals for detecting gravitationally induced entanglement, which would indicate a quantum nature of gravity.
conclusion: Information-theoretic methods offer a promising path to test quantum gravity at low energies, with several feasible experiments on the horizon.

title: Active Quantum Reservoir Engineering: Using A Qubit To Manipulate Its Environment
authors: Marcelo Janovitch, Matteo Brunelli, And Patrick P. Potts
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2143 (2026).

Quantum reservoir engineering leverages dissipative processes to achieve desired behaviour, with applications ranging from entanglement generation to quantum error correction. Therein, a structured environment acts as an entropy sink for the system and no time-dependent control over the system is required. We develop a theoretical framework for active reservoir engineering, where time-dependent control over a quantum system is used to manipulate its environment. In this case, the system may act as an entropy sink for the environment. Our framework captures the dynamical interplay between system and environment, and provides an intuitive picture of how finite-size effects and system-environment correlations allow for manipulating the environment by repeated initialisation of the quantum system. We illustrate our results with two examples: a superconducting qubit coupled to an environment of two-level systems and a semiconducting quantum dot coupled to nuclear spins. In both scenarios, we find qualitative agreement with previous experimental results, illustrating how active control can unlock new functionalities in open quantum systems.

.
tldr: Develops a theoretical framework for active reservoir engineering where time-dependent control of a qubit manipulates its environment, demonstrated with superconducting qubit and quantum dot examples.
motivation: To extend quantum reservoir engineering beyond passive dissipation by using active control to manipulate the environment, enabling new functionalities in open quantum systems.
