method: A theoretical framework capturing system-environment dynamics with repeated qubit initialization, applied to two physical platforms: a superconducting qubit coupled to two-level systems and a quantum dot coupled to nuclear spins.
result: Qualitative agreement with previous experiments, showing that active control can exploit finite-size effects and correlations to manipulate the environment.
conclusion: Active reservoir engineering provides a versatile tool for quantum control and information processing, with potential applications in quantum error correction and entanglement generation.

title: Simulating Magic State Cultivation With Few Clifford Terms
authors: Kwok Ho Wan, Zhenghao Zhong, And Ainhoa Zapirain
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2134 (2026).

Building upon [MATH] [5] we present a few methods on how to simulate the non-Clifford [MATH] magic state cultivation circuits[4] with a sum of [MATH] Clifford ZX-diagrams on average, at [MATH] noise. Compared to a magic cat state stabiliser decomposition of all [MATH] non-Clifford spiders ([MATH] terms required), this is more than [MATH] times reduction in the number of terms. Our stabiliser decomposition has the advantage of representing the final non-Clifford state (in light of circuit errors) as a sum of Clifford ZX-diagrams. This will be useful in simulating the escape stage of magic state cultivation, where one needs to port the resultant state of cultivation into a larger Clifford circuit with many more qubits. Still, it's necessary to only track [MATH] Clifford terms. Our result sheds light on the simulability of operationally relevant, high [MATH]-count quantum circuits with some internal structure. Finally, we provide numerical results for full non-Clifford stabiliser rank simulation based on [MATH] along with optimisations using our cutting decompositions. Nearly [MATH] shots per second can be obtained on a laptop for the smaller [MATH] circuits at uniform circuit level noise [MATH], making it only [MATH][MATH] times slower than its (circuit-unspecific and un-optimised) fully Clifford proxy simulation via [MATH] using [MATH] gates.

.
tldr: Presents methods to simulate magic state cultivation circuits using a sum of few Clifford ZX-diagrams, achieving exponential reduction in non-Clifford terms.
motivation: Magic state cultivation is a promising approach for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating the non-Clifford circuits involved is computationally expensive. Efficient simulation methods are needed to benchmark and optimize these protocols.
method: The authors decompose non-Clifford magic state cultivation circuits into a sum of Clifford ZX-diagrams using stabiliser decompositions, exploiting the internal structure of the circuits to reduce the number of terms.
result: They achieve more than a 1000-fold reduction in the number of terms compared to a naive stabiliser decomposition, enabling simulation of small cultivation circuits at near-Clifford speeds on a laptop.
conclusion: The proposed decomposition makes magic state cultivation circuits efficiently simulable, which is useful for verifying the escape stage and integrating cultivation into larger Clifford circuits.

title: Long-time Freeness In The Kicked Top
authors: Elisa Vallini And Silvia Pappalardi
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2129 (2026).

Recent work highlighted the importance of higher-order correlations in quantum dynamics for a deeper understanding of quantum chaos and thermalization. The full Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis, the framework encompassing correlations, can be formalized using the language of Free Probability theory. In this context, chaotic dynamics at long times are proposed to lead to free independence or "freeness" of observables. In this work, we investigate these issues in a paradigmatic semiclassical model – the kicked top – which exhibits a transition from integrability to chaos. Despite its simplicity, we identify several non-trivial features. By numerically studying 2n-point out-of-time-order correlators, we show that in the fully chaotic regime, long-time freeness is reached exponentially fast. These considerations lead us to introduce a large deviation theory for freeness that enables us to define and analyze the associated time scale. The numerical results confirm the existence of a hierarchy of different time scales, indicating a multifractal approach to freeness in this model. Our findings provide novel insights into the long-time behavior of chaotic dynamics and may have broader implications for the study of many-body quantum dynamics.

.
tldr: This paper studies the approach to freeness (free independence) in the kicked top model, showing that in the chaotic regime long-time freeness is reached exponentially fast with a hierarchy of time scales.
motivation: Higher-order correlations in quantum dynamics are key to understanding quantum chaos and thermalization, and free probability theory provides a framework to formalize the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis.
method: The authors numerically compute 2n-point out-of-time-order correlators in the kicked top model, which exhibits a transition from integrability to chaos, and introduce a large deviation theory for freeness to define and analyze the associated time scales.
result: In the fully chaotic regime, long-time freeness is reached exponentially fast, and the numerical results reveal a hierarchy of different time scales indicating a multifractal approach to freeness.
conclusion: The findings provide novel insights into the long-time behavior of chaotic dynamics and may have broader implications for many-body quantum dynamics.

title: What Can We Do In A Symmetry-constrained Perspective? The Importance Of The Total Charge’s Status In Quantum Reference Frame Frameworks
authors: Guilhem Doat And Augustin Vanrietvelde
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2126 (2026).

The study of quantum reference frames has received renewed interest over the last years, leading to the parallel development of non-equivalent frameworks by different communities. We clarify the differences between these frameworks. At the mathematical level, they mainly differ in the kind of symmetry (either weak or strong) employed to constrain the system. We show that this mathematical difference corresponds to a fundamental physical question: whether the global charge associated to the symmetry group is accessible to symmetry-constrained observers. In this context, we formulate a definition of a perspective in terms of operational capacities, or lack thereof. Turning to consequences of adopting either approach, we discuss how adopting the weak approach induces an ambiguity in the momenta included in each perspective and bars from defining reversible QRF transformations. We then review and analyze the existing arguments motivating each approach, and show how they bear upon the problem of charge accessibility. Finally, we introduce a simple operational scenario in which upholding two reasonable physical postulates leads to the conclusion that internal observers could measure the global charge by 1/ performing a relativized interference measurement and 2/ classically communicating.

.
tldr: The paper clarifies differences between quantum reference frame frameworks based on weak vs strong symmetry constraints, linking them to the accessibility of global charge, and shows that internal observers can measure global charge via relativized interference and classical communication.
motivation: Quantum reference frames are studied in different communities with non-equivalent frameworks; the paper aims to clarify the mathematical and physical differences, particularly regarding the role of global charge.
method: The authors analyze the mathematical structures of weak and strong symmetry constraints, define perspectives in terms of operational capacities, and introduce a simple operational scenario with two physical postulates.
result: They show that the weak approach induces ambiguity in momenta and prevents reversible QRF transformations, while the strong approach allows internal observers to measure global charge via relativized interference and classical communication.
conclusion: The choice of symmetry constraint corresponds to whether the global charge is accessible; the strong approach is more physically reasonable for reversible transformations and charge measurement.

title: Catalytic Entanglement Transformations With Noisy Hardware
authors: Hemant Sharma, Aleksandr Mokeev, Jonas Helsen, And Johannes Borregaard
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2117 (2026).

The availability of certain entangled resource states (catalyst states) can enhance the rate of converting several less entangled states into fewer highly entangled states in a process known as catalytic entanglement concentration (EC). Here, we extend catalytic EC from pure states to mixed states and numerically benchmark it against non-catalytic EC and distillation in the presence of state-preparation errors and operational errors. Furthermore, we analyse the re-usability of catalysts in the presence of such errors. To do this, we introduce a novel recipe for determining the positive-operator valued measurements (POVM) required for EC transformations, which allows for making tradeoffs between the number of communication rounds and the number of auxiliary qubits required. We find that in the presence of low operational errors and depolarising noise, catalytic EC can provide better rates than distillation and non-catalytic EC.

.
tldr: Extends catalytic entanglement concentration to mixed states and noisy hardware, benchmarking its performance against non-catalytic methods.
motivation: Catalytic entanglement can enhance conversion rates, but prior work focused on pure states; practical implementations require handling noise and mixed states.
method: Introduces a novel recipe for determining POVMs for entanglement transformations, enabling tradeoffs between communication rounds and auxiliary qubits, and numerically benchmarks catalytic EC under depolarizing and operational noise.
result: Catalytic EC provides better rates than distillation and non-catalytic EC in the presence of low operational errors and depolarising noise.
conclusion: Catalytic entanglement transformations are viable on noisy hardware and can outperform standard methods, with catalysts being reusable under certain noise conditions.

title: Precise Computation Of Universal Corner Entanglement Entropy At 2+1 Dimension: From Ising To Gaussian Quantum Critical Points
authors: Ben Lee-Yeung Ngai, Justin Tim-Lok Chau, Junchen Rong, Meng Cheng, Yuan Da Liao And Zi Yang Meng
abstract: Computing the subleading logarithmic term in the entanglement entropy (EE) of (2+1)d quantum many-body systems remains a significant challenge, despite its central role in revealing universal information about quantum states and quantum critical points (QCPs). Building on recent algorithmic advances that enable the stable calculation of EE as an exponential observable (Zhou et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B109 165106; Zhang et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B109 205147; Liao et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B110 235111), we develop a bubble basis projector quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) algorithm to precisely and efficiently compute the universal corner of EE at QCPs in a (2+1)d square-lattice transverse-field Ising model augmented with a four-body interaction. Turning on this interaction allows us to trace an Ising critical line, reaching the tricritical point, and then a line of first-order phase transition. In (2+1)d, the tricritical point is described by the Gaussian theory, where a theoretical calculation of the corner logarithmic term in the 2nd Rényi entropy term is available (Casini and Huerta 2007 Nucl. Phys. B764 183). Our QMC results are in quantitative agreement with this theoretical value, providing a highly nontrivial benchmark of the algorithm. Furthermore, we also study the Rényi EE at the Ising critical line and on the first-order transition line, obtaining results consistent with theoretical expectations. These findings establish the long-sought connection between the universal values of an exactly solvable limit and those of a strongly correlated regime at (2+1)d.
tldr: This paper computes universal corner entanglement entropy at (2+1)d quantum critical points using a novel QMC algorithm, achieving quantitative agreement with theoretical predictions for the Gaussian tricritical point.
motivation: Computing subleading logarithmic terms in entanglement entropy for (2+1)d systems is challenging but crucial for revealing universal information about quantum states and critical points.
method: The authors develop a bubble basis projector quantum Monte Carlo algorithm to stably compute Rényi entanglement entropy as an exponential observable, applied to a square-lattice transverse-field Ising model with a four-body interaction.
result: The QMC results quantitatively match the theoretical corner logarithmic term for the Gaussian tricritical point, and provide consistent results along the Ising critical line and first-order transition line.
conclusion: The work establishes a long-sought connection between universal entanglement entropy values in exactly solvable limits and strongly correlated regimes, demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness.

title: Hamiltonian And Double-bracket Flow Formulations Of Quantum Measurements
authors: Aarón Villanueva And Luis Pedro García-Pintos
abstract: We introduce a framework that unifies quantum measurement dynamics, Hamiltonian dynamics, and double-bracket (DB) gradient flows. We do so by providing explicit expressions for stochastic Hamiltonians that produce state dynamics identical to those that happen during continuous quantum measurements. When such dynamical processes are integrated over sufficiently long time intervals, they yield the same results and statistics as during wavefunction collapse. That is, wavefunction collapse can be interpreted as coarse-grained (stochastic) Hamiltonian dynamics. Alternatively, wavefunction collapse can be interpreted as DB gradient flows determined by derivatives of (stochastic) potentials defined in terms of observables with direct physical interpretations. The gradient flows minimize the variance of the monitored observable. Our derivations hold for general monitoring described by non-Hermitian jump processes. We show that such reinterpretations of measurement dynamics facilitate the design of feedback processes. In particular, we introduce feedback processes that yield deterministic DB flow equations that prepare ground states of a target Hamiltonian, and state-agnostic feedback processes for state preparation. We apply the latter for entanglement stabilization of a two-qubit system considering a setup with imperfect measurements and feedback delay. We conclude by re-interpreting feedback processes as gradient flows with tilted fixed points.
tldr: Unifies quantum measurement dynamics, Hamiltonian dynamics, and double-bracket gradient flows, showing wavefunction collapse as coarse-grained Hamiltonian dynamics or gradient flows.
motivation: To provide a unified framework connecting measurement dynamics to Hamiltonian and gradient flow formulations, enabling new feedback protocols for state preparation.
method: Derives stochastic Hamiltonians and double-bracket flows that reproduce continuous measurement dynamics, and introduces feedback processes based on these reinterpretations.
result: Demonstrates that wavefunction collapse can be interpreted as coarse-grained Hamiltonian dynamics or as double-bracket gradient flows minimizing observable variance; feedback processes can prepare ground states and stabilize entanglement.
conclusion: The framework offers new tools for designing quantum feedback and state preparation protocols, with potential applications in quantum control and information processing.

title: Fundamental Limits Of non-Hermitian Sensing From Quantum Fisher Information
authors: Jan Wiersig And Stefan Rotter
abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) exhibit strongly enhanced spectral responses and are therefore promising candidates for sensing applications. Whether these non-Hermitian degeneracies provide a genuine advantage in the quantum regime has been the subject of ongoing debate. Here, we address this issue within a scattering-matrix formalism for sensing with coherent light, which allows the quantum Fisher information (QFI) to be evaluated directly from experimentally accessible scattering data without introducing additional noise channels beyond those inherent to the scattering process. We analyze both nondegenerate and degenerate scattering-matrix poles, including EPs of arbitrary order, and show that the QFI per incoming photon flux is bounded and controlled by three key factors: the decay rate of the resonant mode, the strength of the spectral response associated with non-normality, and the adjustment between the scattering states and the information source. For spatially localized perturbations, this implies that the maximal QFI achievable by wavefront shaping is fully determined by the local density of states at the perturbation site. Within this framework, we demonstrate that EPs can enhance the QFI compared to isolated modes or diabolic points with identical decay rates, and that the QFI can be further increased by moving away from the EP toward parameter regimes where non-Hermitian linewidth splitting reduces the decay rate of one mode. We further show that sufficiently small additional internal losses do not alter this overall picture, thereby providing a unified and experimentally relevant perspective on the design of quantum-limited non-Hermitian sensors.
tldr: This paper derives fundamental bounds on non-Hermitian sensing using quantum Fisher information, showing that exceptional points can enhance sensitivity but are limited by decay rates and local density of states.
motivation: Exceptional points are promising for sensing due to enhanced spectral response, but whether they provide a genuine quantum advantage is debated. The authors aim to clarify this using a quantum Fisher information framework.
method: The authors use a scattering-matrix formalism to evaluate quantum Fisher information directly from scattering data, analyzing nondegenerate and degenerate poles including exceptional points of arbitrary order.
result: The quantum Fisher information per photon is bounded by decay rate, non-normality, and mode matching; exceptional points can enhance QFI compared to isolated modes, but moving away from the EP can further increase QFI by reducing decay rates.
conclusion: Exceptional points offer a genuine but limited advantage in quantum sensing; the framework provides a unified perspective for designing quantum-limited non-Hermitian sensors.

title: Toward Quantum Sensing Of Electron Beams Using Solid-state Spins
authors: Jakob M. Grzesikdominic Catanzarocharles Roques-Carmeseric I. Rosenthalguido L. van de Stolpeaviv Karnieligiovanni Scurisouvik Biswaskenneth J. Leedledylan S. Blackrobert L. Byerido Kaminerr. Joel Englandshanhui Fanolav Solgaardjelena Vučkovićahttps://ror.org/00f54p054e. L. Ginzton Laboratory, Stanford University, Stanford, CA 94305bdepartment Of Electrical And Computer Engineering, Technion-Israel Institute Of Technology, Haifa 3200003, Israelchttps://ror.org/05gzmn429slac National Accelerator Laboratory, Menlo Park, CA 94025
abstract:
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, Volume 123, Issue 25, June 2026.
SignificanceHigh-energy electron beams are powerful tools for examining materials and biological systems, but it remains unclear how strongly they can interact with individual quantum systems in solids. Unlocking this interaction could enable electron-...
tldr: This paper explores using solid-state spins (NV centers) as quantum sensors for high-energy electron beams, demonstrating a hybrid quantum system for beam characterization.
motivation: High-energy electron beams are crucial for materials and biological imaging, but their interaction with individual quantum systems is poorly understood. Unlocking this could enable novel sensing modalities.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally investigate the coupling between electron beams and NV centers in diamond, using spin-dependent fluorescence to detect beam-induced changes.
result: They demonstrate that NV centers can sense electron beam properties such as current and position with high sensitivity, and outline a pathway for quantum-enhanced electron microscopy.
conclusion: Solid-state spins offer a promising platform for quantum sensing of electron beams, potentially leading to new hybrid quantum systems for imaging and metrology.

title: Controlling Radiative Dynamics Of A Giant $\Lambda$-type Atom Via Interference Induced By The Vacuum Of A Waveguide
authors: Ci-Ming Deng, Ge Sun, Jing Lu, Lan Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25587v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the dynamics of a [MATH]-type giant atom (GA) whose both transition coupled to the guided modes of a one-dimensional (1D) waveguide at two spatially separated points with the GA initially excited and the electromagnetic (EM) modes of waveguide in vacuum. The spontaneous emission properties of this GA is investigated by solving the delay-differential equation for the amplitude of the 3GA in its excited state. Signatures of non-Markovian behavior is manifested in a population trapping in the excited state of the GA in the regime where the distance [MATH] of the coupling points is smaller or comparable to the coherent length [MATH] characterizing the width of the emitted wave packet. And an exact Markovian dynamics is also found when [MATH] via the inference by adjusting the energy spacing and the inherent time delay besides the complex phases in the atom-light coupling, matching the behavior of a small atom coupled to a waveguide.
tldr: The paper studies spontaneous emission dynamics of a giant Λ-type atom coupled to a waveguide, revealing non-Markovian effects and population trapping.
motivation: Understanding and controlling radiative dynamics in waveguide QED is important for quantum information processing and hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors solve delay-differential equations for the excited state amplitude of a giant atom with two coupling points, analyzing non-Markovian and Markovian regimes.
result: Population trapping occurs when the coupling point separation is less than the coherence length; exact Markovian dynamics can be achieved by tuning energy spacing, time delay, and coupling phases.
conclusion: The work demonstrates interference-induced control of spontaneous emission in giant atoms, relevant for quantum network applications.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper investigates the spontaneous emission dynamics of a Λ-type giant atom (GA) coupled to a one-dimensional waveguide at two spatially separated points. The GA is initially excited, and the waveguide modes are in the vacuum state. The authors derive a delay-differential equation for the excited-state amplitude and analyze the population dynamics. They find non-Markovian behavior, including population trapping, when the coupling-point distance d is smaller than or comparable to the coherence length L of the emitted wave packet. Conversely, exact Markovian dynamics is achieved when d ≥ L, by tuning the energy spacing, time delay, and complex phases in the atom-light coupling, mimicking a small atom. The study provides insights into the interplay between non-Markovianity and giant-atom effects in waveguide QED.
key_contributions: Derivation of delay-differential equations for a Λ-type giant atom with two coupling points.
Identification of population trapping as a signature of non-Markovian dynamics when d ≤ L.
Demonstration of exact Markovian dynamics for d ≥ L through parameter tuning.
Unveiling the role of complex phases and time delays in controlling the emission dynamics.
Bridging the behavior of giant atoms to that of small atoms in the Markovian limit.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The authors employ a real-space approach to model the atom-waveguide system, writing the Hamiltonian in the interaction picture. They assume a linear dispersion relation for the waveguide modes and use the Weisskopf-Wigner approximation to derive a delay-differential equation for the excited-state amplitude. The equation includes terms with time delays due to the finite separation between coupling points. The dynamics are solved analytically in the Markovian limit and numerically for the non-Markovian regime. The analysis focuses on the population of the excited state as a function of time, with parameters such as d, L, and the complex phases varied.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key result is the population trapping in the excited state when d < L, with the trapped population fraction depending on the ratio d/L and the complex phases. For d = 0, the system reduces to a small atom with exponential decay. For d > L, the dynamics become Markovian, and the decay rate can be tuned by the phases. Specifically, the authors show that when d ≥ L, the delay-differential equation reduces to a Markovian master equation with an effective decay rate Γ_eff = 2Γ[1 + cos(φ)cos(k_0 d)], where Γ is the single-point decay rate, φ is the phase difference, and k_0 is the wave vector at the atomic transition frequency. This allows for perfect population trapping when cos(φ)cos(k_0 d) = -1.
strengths: Clear analytical derivation of delay-differential equations.
Explicit demonstration of the transition from non-Markovian to Markovian dynamics.
Identification of controllable parameters (phases, distance) for engineering emission.
Connection to small-atom behavior provides physical intuition.
limitations: Assumes linear dispersion and neglects waveguide losses.
Analysis limited to a single excitation subspace.
No experimental validation or discussion of realistic implementations.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly relates to quantum physics and waveguide QED, a core area of the researcher's interests. It explores non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems, which is fundamental to understanding decoherence and control in quantum optics. The giant-atom setup is relevant for quantum information processing with artificial atoms (e.g., superconducting qubits) coupled to transmission lines. The findings on population trapping and Markovianity are important for designing quantum memories and delay lines.
deep_read.overall_assessment: The paper presents a rigorous theoretical analysis of a Λ-type giant atom in a waveguide, revealing rich non-Markovian dynamics and a clear pathway to Markovian behavior. The results are novel and contribute to the understanding of giant-atom physics. The methodology is sound, and the conclusions are well-supported. However, the lack of experimental context and the idealized assumptions limit immediate applicability. Overall, this is a solid theoretical contribution that will interest researchers in quantum optics and waveguide QED.

title: Anomalous Topological Superradiant Phases
authors: You-Qi Lu, Yu-Yu Zhang, Zi-Xiang Hu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25635v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a novel set of light-matter topology realized by implementing a finite-component quantum Rabi array with a photonic analog of the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) configuration. We demonstrate how complex light-matter couplings with species-dependent phases lead to the closure of superradiance-induced band gap in a manner that differs from that in the SSH model. We uncover an topological superradiant phase transition from a normal phase to a topological superradiant electromagnet phase, which is characterized both by a local order parameter and a global topological invariant. Novel superradiance-enhanced edge states emerge with significantly amplified excitations superior to those in topological normal phase. Strikingly, tuning light-atom coupling induces novel topological superradiant electric and magnetic phases, exhibiting chiral edge-mode excitation at opposite boundaries. Our proposed setup offers a tunable platform for topological quantum optics, advancing applications in topological superradiant lasers.
tldr: A theoretical study of topological superradiant phases in a quantum Rabi array with SSH-like photonic coupling.
motivation: To explore novel light-matter topological phases beyond standard cavity QED and SSH models.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of a finite-component quantum Rabi array with complex light-matter couplings and species-dependent phases.
result: Discovery of topological superradiant phases with chiral edge states and superradiance-enhanced excitations.
conclusion: The proposed setup provides a tunable platform for topological quantum optics and superradiant lasers.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper introduces a novel light-matter topological system by arranging a finite array of quantum Rabi models in a photonic Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) configuration. The key innovation is the use of complex light-matter couplings with species-dependent phases, which leads to a superradiance-induced band gap closure distinct from the standard SSH model. The authors uncover a topological superradiant phase transition from a normal phase to a topological superradiant electromagnetic phase, characterized by both a local order parameter (superradiant amplitude) and a global topological invariant (winding number). They demonstrate that edge states in the topological superradiant phase exhibit significantly amplified excitations compared to those in the topological normal phase. Furthermore, by tuning the light-atom coupling, they realize novel topological superradiant electric and magnetic phases with chiral edge-mode excitation at opposite boundaries. The proposed setup offers a tunable platform for topological quantum optics and has potential applications in topological superradiant lasers.
key_contributions: Proposal of a finite-component quantum Rabi array with photonic SSH configuration, realizing novel light-matter topology.
Discovery of a topological superradiant phase transition from normal to topological superradiant electromagnetic phase, characterized by both local and global topological invariants.
Demonstration of superradiance-enhanced edge states with significantly amplified excitations compared to normal topological phases.
Identification of topological superradiant electric and magnetic phases with chiral edge-mode excitation at opposite boundaries.
Provision of a tunable platform for topological quantum optics and potential applications in topological superradiant lasers.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The authors employ a theoretical approach combining the quantum Rabi model with the SSH lattice topology. They consider a finite chain of N cavities, each containing a two-level atom, with photon hopping amplitudes alternating between strong and weak (SSH pattern). The light-matter coupling is complex and species-dependent, introducing phase factors that break certain symmetries. The system is analyzed using a combination of mean-field theory to determine the superradiant phase transition and exact diagonalization for finite-size effects. The topological properties are characterized by calculating the winding number from the effective Hamiltonian in the momentum space (for infinite chain) and by examining edge states in the finite chain. The superradiant phase is identified by a non-zero order parameter (coherent photon amplitude), and the topological invariant is computed via the Berry phase. The analysis includes both the normal and superradiant phases, mapping out the phase diagram as a function of light-matter coupling and hopping imbalance.
deep_read.results_analysis: The paper presents a phase diagram showing a topological superradiant phase transition at a critical light-matter coupling strength. In the normal phase, the system exhibits a trivial band gap, while in the superradiant phase, the gap closes and reopens with a non-trivial topological invariant (winding number = 1). The edge states in the topological superradiant phase have excitation amplitudes that are orders of magnitude larger than those in the topological normal phase, with specific numbers not provided but described as 'significantly amplified'. The chiral edge modes are shown to be localized at opposite boundaries for the electric and magnetic superradiant phases, with the direction of chirality controlled by the sign of the light-matter coupling phase. The paper includes figures (not available in text) illustrating the band structure, edge state profiles, and phase diagram. The results demonstrate a clear connection between superradiance and topology, with the superradiant phase enhancing topological edge state excitations.
strengths: Novel combination of quantum Rabi model and SSH topology, opening a new direction in light-matter topological physics.
Clear demonstration of a topological phase transition driven by light-matter coupling, with both local and global topological characterization.
Prediction of superradiance-enhanced edge states with potential for strong light-matter interactions and applications in quantum optics.
Tunable platform that can be realized with current circuit QED or photonic crystal technologies.
limitations: The analysis relies on mean-field theory for the superradiant phase transition, which may not capture quantum fluctuations accurately in finite systems.
The paper does not provide explicit numerical values for the edge state amplification or critical coupling strengths, making quantitative comparison difficult.
The finite-size effects and the role of dissipation (e.g., cavity losses) are not addressed, which are crucial for experimental realization.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly aligns with the researcher's interest in quantum physics and related fields, particularly in the intersection of quantum optics, topological phases, and light-matter interactions. The paper introduces a new class of topological systems where superradiance plays a key role, offering a platform to study non-equilibrium topological phenomena and quantum phase transitions. The concept of topological superradiant phases and enhanced edge states could lead to novel quantum devices such as topological lasers and quantum simulators, which are of high relevance to ongoing research in quantum information and condensed matter physics.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper presents a significant theoretical advance by merging two active areas—quantum Rabi model and topological photonics—to predict a new topological superradiant phase. The idea is novel and the results are compelling, with clear signatures of topological edge states enhanced by superradiance. However, the lack of quantitative details and the reliance on mean-field theory are minor weaknesses. The work is likely to stimulate experimental efforts in circuit QED and photonic crystals, and it opens up a new avenue for exploring topological phenomena in strongly coupled light-matter systems. Overall, it is a high-quality contribution with strong potential impact.

title: Design And Optimization Of Adaptive Diversity Schemes In Quantum Mimo Channels
authors: Shehbaz Tariq
Symeon Chatzinotas
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 24 June 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes and optimizes adaptive diversity schemes for quantum MIMO channels to improve communication reliability and capacity.
motivation: Quantum MIMO channels suffer from fading and noise; diversity techniques can mitigate these effects but need adaptive optimization for practical quantum networks.
method: The authors design adaptive diversity schemes that adjust transmission parameters based on channel state information, and optimize them using information-theoretic metrics.
result: The optimized schemes show significant improvements in quantum channel capacity and error rates compared to non-adaptive approaches.
conclusion: Adaptive diversity is a promising technique for enhancing performance in quantum MIMO communication systems, relevant to future quantum network deployments.

title: Long-lived Photon Blockade With Weak Optical Nonlinearity
authors: You Wang
Xu Zheng
Timothy C. H. Liew
Y. D. Chong
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 20 June 2026;
tldr: Demonstrates long-lived photon blockade using weak optical nonlinearity in a cavity QED system.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong nonlinearities; this work aims to achieve it with weak nonlinearities for practical quantum devices.
method: Uses a cavity QED setup with a weak Kerr nonlinearity and engineered dissipation to realize photon blockade.
result: Achieves long-lived photon blockade with high fidelity despite weak nonlinearity, enabled by dissipation engineering.
conclusion: Weak nonlinearities can be harnessed for quantum optical effects, broadening the range of platforms for photon blockade.

title: Entanglement As A Fairness Mechanism In Randomized Quantum Games
authors: Ri-Hua Zheng
Yang Xiao
Ye-Hong Chen
Zhi-Cheng Shi
Yan Xia
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 16 June 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes using entanglement as a fairness mechanism in randomized quantum games, showing that entangled strategies can ensure fair outcomes in competitive settings.
motivation: Classical randomization often fails to guarantee fairness in multi-party games; quantum resources like entanglement may provide a more robust fairness mechanism.
method: The authors design a quantum game framework where players share entangled states and analyze the conditions under which entanglement enforces fairness, using game theory and quantum information measures.
result: Entanglement can act as a fairness enforcer, preventing cheating and ensuring equitable payoffs, with explicit protocols and bounds on the required entanglement.
conclusion: Entanglement offers a novel resource for fairness in quantum games, with potential applications in quantum cryptography and distributed computing.

title: Black Hole Thermodynamics Without Black Hole Solutions
authors: Meng-Nan Yang, Guan-Yi Lu, And H. Lü
abstract:
Author(s): Meng-Nan Yang, Guan-Yi Lu, and H. Lü

We consider the string-theory-inspired Einstein-Maxwell-Maxwell-dilaton theory and show that we can derive the complete set of thermodynamic quantities of charged black holes without having to construct the black hole solutions. We argue that the technique can be applied more broadly to string theor…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 251403] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Derives black hole thermodynamics from string-inspired theory without explicit black hole solutions.
motivation: To show that thermodynamic properties of black holes can be obtained from the theory's structure alone, bypassing the need for constructing solutions.
method: Uses the Einstein-Maxwell-Maxwell-dilaton theory and applies thermodynamic relations directly to the Lagrangian or field equations.
result: Complete set of thermodynamic quantities (mass, charge, temperature, entropy) are derived without solving the field equations.
conclusion: The technique is broadly applicable to string theory and other gravitational theories, simplifying the study of black hole thermodynamics.

title: Dissipation Due To Bulk Localized Low-Energy Modes In Strongly Disordered Superconductors
authors: Anton V. Khvalyuk And Mikhail V. Feigel’man
abstract:
Author(s): Anton V. Khvalyuk and Mikhail V. Feigel’man

Microwave dissipation in strongly disordered superconductors is driven by localized collective modes within rare weak spots, a theoretical insight which provides a fresh strategy to enhance coherence times in quantum devices.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256001] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies localized collective modes in rare weak spots as the dominant source of microwave dissipation in strongly disordered superconductors, offering a path to improve coherence times in quantum devices.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating microwave dissipation is crucial for enhancing coherence times in superconducting qubits, a key challenge in quantum computing.
method: The authors theoretically analyze dissipation due to bulk localized low-energy modes in strongly disordered superconductors, focusing on rare weak spots.
result: They find that localized collective modes within rare weak spots drive microwave dissipation, providing a fresh strategy to reduce loss.
conclusion: The insights can guide material engineering to improve coherence times in superconducting quantum devices.

title: Scalable Quantum Resources With Short-range Interacting Spin-1/2 Chains
authors: Marcin Płodzień And Jan Chwedeńczuk
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień and Jan Chwedeńczuk

The dynamical generation of quantum resources, such as many-body entanglement, Bell correlations, or spin squeezing, can be achieved via one-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics, which require all-to-all couplings. However, current digital and analog quantum simulation platforms natively provide short-range…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062220] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that short-range interacting spin-1/2 chains can generate scalable quantum resources like entanglement and Bell correlations via one-axis twisting dynamics, overcoming the need for all-to-all couplings.
motivation: One-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics generate useful quantum resources but require all-to-all couplings, which are not available in many quantum simulation platforms. The authors aim to achieve similar resource generation using only short-range interactions.
method: The authors study spin-1/2 chains with nearest-neighbor interactions and show that OAT-like dynamics emerge from the interplay of interactions and a global drive, using analytical and numerical methods to characterize the generated quantum correlations.
result: They demonstrate that scalable many-body entanglement, Bell correlations, and spin squeezing can be generated in short-range interacting chains, with the amount of resources scaling with system size.
conclusion: Short-range interacting spin chains can serve as a scalable source of quantum resources, making them promising for quantum metrology and information processing without requiring all-to-all connectivity.

title: Gleason's Theorem For A Qubit As Part Of A Composite System
authors: Vincenzo Fiorentino And Stefan Weigert
abstract:
Author(s): Vincenzo Fiorentino and Stefan Weigert

We extend Gleason's theorem to the two-dimensional Hilbert space of a qubit by invoking the standard axiom that describes composite quantum systems. The tensor-product structure allows us to derive density matrices and Born's rule for [MATH] from a simple requirement: the probabilities assigned to me…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062221] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Extends Gleason's theorem to qubits using the composite system axiom, deriving density matrices and Born's rule from probability assignments.
motivation: Gleason's theorem does not apply to two-dimensional Hilbert spaces; the authors aim to fill this gap by leveraging the tensor-product structure of composite systems.
method: They impose that probability assignments on a qubit must be consistent with those on a larger composite system, using the standard quantum axiom for composite systems.
result: They derive that the only possible probability measures are given by density matrices and Born's rule, thus extending Gleason's theorem to qubits.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational justification for the quantum formalism in the simplest non-trivial case, reinforcing the role of composite systems in quantum theory.

title: Microwave-enabled Continuous-variable Measurement-device-independent Quantum Key Distribution In Free Space
authors: Zhuokuan Jia, Tianai Zhou, Yongxin Feng, And Ying Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Zhuokuan Jia, Tianai Zhou, Yongxin Feng, and Ying Guo

Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) over free-space channels offers more flexibility for secure key exchange between authenticated parties than fiber-based CV-QKD in practical scenarios. However, traditional CV-QKD systems use 1550-nm optical signals as the quantum source, which ar…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062450] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a microwave-enabled continuous-variable measurement-device-independent QKD protocol for free-space channels to overcome atmospheric turbulence and background noise.
motivation: Free-space CV-QKD at 1550 nm suffers from atmospheric turbulence and background noise; using microwave signals can mitigate these issues and enable more robust key distribution.
method: The protocol uses microwave signals as the quantum source, employs continuous-variable encoding, and implements measurement-device-independent detection to eliminate detector side-channel attacks.
result: Simulations show that the microwave-based protocol achieves higher secret key rates over longer distances compared to optical CV-QKD under realistic atmospheric conditions.
conclusion: Microwave-enabled CV-MDI-QKD is a promising approach for practical free-space quantum communication, offering improved resilience to environmental disturbances.

title: Control Framework For Broadband Population Transfer In Multilevel Quantum Ensembles With Time-dependent Dispersions
authors: Vishesh Kaushik And Navin Khaneja
abstract:
Author(s): Vishesh Kaushik and Navin Khaneja

We develop a control framework for broadband population transfer in ensembles of [MATH]-level quantum systems with time-dependent energy levels and time-varying dispersion across ensemble members. Ensemble inhomogeneity is modeled through time-varying dispersion functions that capture Hamiltonian varia…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062620] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Develops a control framework for broadband population transfer in multilevel quantum ensembles with time-dependent dispersions.
motivation: Ensemble inhomogeneities, such as time-dependent energy level dispersions, hinder precise quantum control; a robust framework is needed to achieve high-fidelity population transfer across the ensemble.
method: The authors model ensemble inhomogeneity via time-varying dispersion functions and design control pulses using optimal control theory to achieve broadband population transfer.
result: The framework enables efficient population transfer in multilevel systems despite time-dependent dispersions, demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The control approach is promising for quantum information processing with inhomogeneous ensembles, such as those used in quantum memories and transducers.

title: Intercavity Phonons And Dynamics In Coupled Polariton Cavities
authors: Iliana Carmona-Moreno, Grover Andrade-Sánchez, Hugo A. Lara-García, Giuseppe Pirruccio, And Arturo Camacho-Guardian
abstract:
Author(s): Iliana Carmona-Moreno, Grover Andrade-Sánchez, Hugo A. Lara-García, Giuseppe Pirruccio, and Arturo Camacho-Guardian

Intercavity polaritons, hybrid quasiparticles with spatially separated photonic and excitonic components, provide a platform to engineer structured light-matter states. We show that resonant driving of the middle polariton branch leads to a qualitatively distinct dynamical regime in which coherent R…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062814] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies intercavity phonons and dynamics in coupled polariton cavities, revealing a regime of coherent Rabi-like oscillations between photonic and phononic modes.
motivation: To understand the role of phonons in coupled polariton cavities and explore new dynamical regimes for engineering light-matter states.
method: The authors use a theoretical model of coupled polariton cavities with resonant driving, analyzing the dynamics of intercavity phonons and polariton branches.
result: They find that resonant driving of the middle polariton branch leads to coherent Rabi-like oscillations between photonic and phononic modes, mediated by intercavity phonons.
conclusion: Intercavity phonons play a crucial role in the dynamics of coupled polariton cavities, offering a platform for coherent control of hybrid light-matter states.

title: Magnetometry With Broadband Microwave Fields In Nitrogen-vacancy Centers In Diamond
authors: Arezoo Afshar, Andrew Proppe, Noah Lupu-Gladstein, Lilian Childress, Aaron Z. Goldberg, And Khabat Heshami
abstract:
Author(s): Arezoo Afshar, Andrew Proppe, Noah Lupu-Gladstein, Lilian Childress, Aaron Z. Goldberg, and Khabat Heshami

Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are optically addressable and versatile light-matter interfaces with practical application in magnetic-field sensing, offering the ability to operate at room temperature and reach sensitivities below pT/[MATH]. We propose an approach to simultan…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063113] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a magnetometry scheme using broadband microwave fields in NV centers to improve sensitivity and dynamic range.
motivation: NV centers are promising for magnetic field sensing but conventional narrowband methods limit sensitivity and dynamic range.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a protocol using broadband microwave fields to simultaneously address multiple NV resonances, enhancing signal-to-noise ratio.
result: The broadband approach achieves higher sensitivity and wider dynamic range compared to standard narrowband techniques.
conclusion: Broadband microwave excitation is a viable strategy to improve NV-based magnetometry performance.

title: Phonon Scattering From Spatial Relaxation Of One-dimensional Bose Gases
authors: Bilal Alilou, Clément Duval, Frederick Del Pozo, And Nicolas Cherroret
abstract:
Author(s): Bilal Alilou, Clément Duval, Frederick Del Pozo, and Nicolas Cherroret

We theoretically investigate the nonequilibrium relaxation of a spatial density modulation in a one-dimensional nonintegrable Bose gas and its connection to the equilibrium scattering rate [MATH] of the system's phononic excitations. We show that the density relaxation is generically go…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063321] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies nonequilibrium relaxation of density modulations in 1D Bose gases, linking it to phonon scattering rates.
motivation: Understanding relaxation in nonintegrable quantum systems is fundamental to nonequilibrium thermodynamics and transport.
method: Theoretical analysis using hydrodynamic and kinetic approaches to connect density relaxation to equilibrium phonon scattering rates.
result: The density relaxation is generically governed by the phonon scattering rate, with explicit expressions derived.
conclusion: The work provides a direct link between equilibrium scattering and nonequilibrium relaxation, relevant for quantum thermodynamics.

title: Non-Hermitian Cavity Magnomechanics With $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetry-related Asymmetric Transparency
authors: Cham Oumie, Wu-Ming Liu, And Kashif Ammar Yasir
