[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063522] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Investigates non-Hermitian cavity magnomechanics with PT-symmetry-related asymmetric transparency.
motivation: To explore magnomechanically induced transparency in a cavity magnomechanical system with non-Hermitian coupling, which is relevant for quantum information processing and sensing.
method: Theoretical analysis of a cavity magnomechanical system with traveling-field-induced non-Hermitian coupling, involving a microwave cavity mode coupled to magnons in a YIG sphere.
result: Observes PT-symmetry-related asymmetric transparency and related phenomena.
conclusion: Provides insights into non-Hermitian physics in hybrid quantum systems, potentially useful for quantum transducers and signal processing.

title: Nonreciprocal Universal Photon Blockade In An Asymmetrical Cavity
authors: Xiuwen Xia, Xinqin Zhang, Xiaobing Luo, Chaofei Liu, Haozhen Li, Jabir Hakami, Jingping Xu, And Yaping Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiuwen Xia, Xinqin Zhang, Xiaobing Luo, Chaofei Liu, Haozhen Li, Jabir Hakami, Jingping Xu, and Yaping Yang

Inspired by the distinctive properties of universal photon blockade (UPB), we propose a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model in an asymmetric cavity to achieve quantum nonreciprocity. Through theoretical analysis, we establish direction-dependent optimal conditions for perfect UPB in weak-driving limita…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063729] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical proposal for achieving nonreciprocal universal photon blockade in an asymmetric cavity using a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model.
motivation: To realize quantum nonreciprocity and photon blockade simultaneously, which is important for quantum information processing and networking.
method: The authors analyze a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model in an asymmetric cavity, deriving direction-dependent optimal conditions for perfect universal photon blockade under weak driving.
result: They establish that nonreciprocal photon blockade can be achieved with high contrast, enabling directional control of single-photon transmission.
conclusion: The proposed system provides a platform for integrated quantum devices that combine nonreciprocity and photon blockade, useful for quantum networks.

title: Universality Of Dissipative Discrete Time Crystal Formation
authors: Jr. And Jayson G. Cosme Roy D. Jara
abstract:
Author(s): Roy D. Jara, Jr. and Jayson G. Cosme

We demonstrate that the Kibble-Zurek mechanism holds for open systems transitioning from a disordered phase to a discrete time crystal (DTC). Specifically, we observe the characteristic power-law scaling with quench time of the number of spatial defects and the transition delay measured from the tim…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214323] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that the Kibble-Zurek mechanism applies to open systems forming discrete time crystals, showing universal scaling of defects and transition delay.
motivation: Understanding defect formation in time crystals is important for characterizing non-equilibrium phases in open quantum systems.
method: The authors study a driven-dissipative model of a discrete time crystal and analyze the scaling of spatial defects and transition delay as a function of quench time using numerical simulations.
result: They observe power-law scaling consistent with the Kibble-Zurek mechanism, indicating universality in the formation of discrete time crystals.
conclusion: The Kibble-Zurek mechanism holds for open systems transitioning to a discrete time crystal phase, providing insights into non-equilibrium critical dynamics.

title: Generalized Stochastic Spin-wave Theory For Open Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Zejian Li, Anna Delmonte, And Rosario Fazio
abstract:
Author(s): Zejian Li, Anna Delmonte, and Rosario Fazio

We propose a semiclassical framework for solving open quantum dynamics in driven-dissipative spin systems. Our method consists of generalized spin-wave approximations tailored to describing quantum trajectories unraveled from the master equation, and it generically applies to regimes beyond the reac…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214324] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: A semiclassical framework for solving open quantum dynamics in driven-dissipative spin systems using generalized spin-wave theory.
motivation: Open quantum spin systems are important for quantum thermodynamics and quantum information, but exact solutions are often intractable; a semiclassical method can capture essential physics in regimes beyond the reaction coordinate approach.
method: The authors propose generalized spin-wave approximations tailored to quantum trajectories unraveled from the master equation, extending spin-wave theory to open systems.
result: The framework is shown to apply generically to driven-dissipative spin systems, providing a tractable semiclassical description.
conclusion: This work offers a new tool for studying non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics in spin systems, relevant to quantum thermal machines and open quantum systems.

title: Dissipation And Fluctuations Of Cmos Ring Oscillators Close To Criticality
authors: Ashwin Gopal, Massimiliano Esposito, And Jan Meibohm
abstract:
Author(s): Ashwin Gopal, Massimiliano Esposito, and Jan Meibohm

We analyze a thermodynamically consistent model of Complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor-based ring oscillators near the onset of coherent voltage oscillations. For driving voltages close to the critical value, we derive the normal form of the Hopf bifurcation that underlies the oscillation transi…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245308] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the thermodynamics of CMOS ring oscillators near a Hopf bifurcation, deriving fluctuation theorems and dissipation bounds for coherent oscillations.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost and fluctuations of classical computing elements near criticality is important for designing energy-efficient devices.
method: The authors develop a thermodynamically consistent model of CMOS ring oscillators and use stochastic thermodynamics to derive the normal form of the Hopf bifurcation and associated fluctuation relations.
result: They obtain analytical expressions for work, heat, and entropy production near the oscillation onset, and show that fluctuations obey a detailed fluctuation theorem.
conclusion: The work provides a thermodynamic framework for classical oscillators near criticality, linking dissipation to information processing in CMOS circuits.

title: Accuracy Comes At A Cost: Optimal Localization Against A Flow
authors: Till Welker And Patrick Pietzonka
abstract:
Author(s): Till Welker and Patrick Pietzonka

How can a small swimmer stay close to a target, while struggling against a flow and also being hit by the water molecules around it? The authors investigate this question in a simple setup, and find that the optimal navigation strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming with a trade-off between cost and accuracy.


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064142] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Optimal navigation strategy for a small swimmer in a flow trades off accuracy and cost, revealing thermodynamic constraints on information processing.
motivation: Understand how a microscopic swimmer can localize near a target despite flow and thermal noise, balancing energy expenditure and positional accuracy.
method: Theoretical analysis using stochastic thermodynamics and optimal control theory to derive the trade-off between cost (work) and accuracy (mean squared displacement).
result: The optimal strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming, with a fundamental bound linking accuracy and thermodynamic cost.
conclusion: Accuracy in localization comes at a thermodynamic cost, illustrating a general principle for information processing in noisy environments.

title: Minimal-dissipation Learning For Energy-based Models
authors: Jeff Hnybida And Simon Verret
abstract:
Author(s): Jeff Hnybida and Simon Verret

We show that the bias of the approximate maximum-likelihood estimation (MLE) objective of a persistent chain energy-based model (EBM) is precisely equal to the thermodynamic excess work of an overdamped Langevin dynamical system. We then answer the question of whether such a model can be trained wit…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065306] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: Shows that the bias in maximum-likelihood training of energy-based models equals thermodynamic excess work, and explores minimal-dissipation learning.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic cost of training energy-based models and whether they can be trained with minimal dissipation.
method: Connects the bias of persistent chain EBM training to excess work in overdamped Langevin dynamics, then analyzes minimal-dissipation protocols.
result: The bias is exactly the thermodynamic excess work; minimal-dissipation learning is possible under certain conditions.
conclusion: Energy-based model training has a thermodynamic interpretation, and dissipation can be minimized, linking machine learning to thermodynamics.

title: Dynamical Typicality In Classical Lattice Systems
authors: Nicolas Nessi And Peter Reimann
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Nessi and Peter Reimann

Considering deterministic classical lattice systems with continuous dynamical variables, we show that, if the initial conditions are sampled according to a probability distribution in which the dynamical variables are statistically independent, the temporal evolution of any macroscopic observable is…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064138] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that for deterministic classical lattice systems with independent initial conditions, the time evolution of macroscopic observables is typically well-described by the microcanonical ensemble, establishing a form of dynamical typicality.
motivation: Understanding how macroscopic irreversibility emerges from deterministic microscopic dynamics is a fundamental question in statistical mechanics. The paper aims to provide a rigorous justification for the typicality of equilibrium behavior in classical lattice systems.
method: The authors consider deterministic classical lattice systems with continuous variables and show that if initial conditions are sampled from a product distribution, the time evolution of any macroscopic observable is close to its microcanonical average for most times, using concentration of measure and dynamical systems arguments.
result: They prove that for large systems, the fraction of time a macroscopic observable deviates from its microcanonical average is exponentially small in system size, with explicit bounds that depend on the observable's sensitivity and system parameters.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous foundation for dynamical typicality in classical lattice systems, supporting the idea that equilibrium statistical mechanics emerges from deterministic dynamics under typical initial conditions.

title: Rotation Sensor Based On An Atom-cavity System
authors: Jim Skulte, Jayson G. Cosme, And Ludwig Mathey
abstract:
Author(s): Jim Skulte, Jayson G. Cosme, and Ludwig Mathey

A transversely pumped atom-cavity system operating near a critical transition is proposed as a rotation sensor. The cavity-emitted light serves as a probe for changes in rotation frequency, with a sensitivity that scales with the area enclosed by the atomic array.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022057] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an atom-cavity system as a rotation sensor with sensitivity scaling with the enclosed area.
motivation: To develop a quantum-enhanced rotation sensor using a transversely pumped atom-cavity system operating near a critical transition.
method: The system uses cavity-emitted light as a probe; sensitivity is analyzed via the critical behavior of the atom-cavity system.
result: The rotation sensitivity scales with the area enclosed by the atomic array, offering potential advantages over classical sensors.
conclusion: The atom-cavity system provides a promising platform for rotation sensing with quantum-enhanced performance.

title: Quantum Dynamical Signatures Of Topological Flow Transitions In Limit Cycle Phases
authors: Alejandro S. Gómez And Javier Del Pino
abstract:
Author(s): Alejandro S. Gómez and Javier del Pino

Quantum self-oscillatory phases are ubiquitous in driven-dissipative systems. Classically, each phase is defined by its flow pattern and how stationary sets organize phase space (e.g., fixed points and limit cycles), with transitions triggered by local bifurcations or global basin rearrangements. In…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023319] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum signatures of topological flow transitions in limit cycle phases of driven-dissipative systems, linking classical bifurcations to quantum observables.
motivation: Understanding how classical topological transitions in phase space manifest in quantum systems is crucial for characterizing driven-dissipative phases and their stability.
method: The authors analyze a quantum van der Pol oscillator model using phase-space methods and quantum trajectory simulations to identify signatures of limit cycle transitions.
result: They find that topological flow transitions are accompanied by changes in quantum fluctuations, entanglement, and spectral properties, providing observable quantum markers.
conclusion: Quantum dynamical signatures can detect classical flow transitions, offering a way to probe non-equilibrium phase structure in quantum systems.

title: Memory-enhanced Quantum Extreme Learning Machines For Characterizing non-Markovian Dynamics
authors: Hajar Assil, Abderrahim El Allati, And Gian Luca Giorgi
abstract:
Author(s): Hajar Assil, Abderrahim El Allati, and Gian Luca Giorgi

We use a quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) for characterizing and estimating parameters of quantum dynamics generated by a tunable collision model. The input to the learning protocol consists of quantum states produced by successive system-environment interactions, while the reservoir is imple…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023306] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses a quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) with memory to characterize non-Markovian dynamics in a collision model, demonstrating parameter estimation and detection of memory effects.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are important in quantum systems but challenging to characterize; machine learning offers a data-driven approach to extract parameters and detect memory effects without full tomography.
method: A QELM is implemented with a reservoir of qubits that interact sequentially with system states via a collision model; the reservoir's output is used to train a linear readout for parameter estimation and non-Markovianity detection.
result: The QELM successfully estimates system-environment coupling strengths and detects non-Markovianity, with memory-enhanced reservoirs improving performance over memoryless ones.
conclusion: Quantum extreme learning machines with memory are effective tools for characterizing non-Markovian quantum dynamics, offering a practical approach for quantum system identification.

title: Indefinite Causal Order In Cavity Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Lorenzo M. Procopio, And Tim J. Bartley
abstract:
Author(s): Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Lorenzo M. Procopio, and Tim J. Bartley

Indefinite causal order (ICO) has the potential to be a new resource for quantum information processing. In most of its experiments, ICO has been investigated in a photonic platform. Here, we investigate ICO in a cavity quantum electrodynamics system composed of two cavities. Our results show that I…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023295] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates indefinite causal order (ICO) in a cavity quantum electrodynamics system, showing that ICO can be realized in this platform and may serve as a resource for quantum information processing.
motivation: ICO is a potential resource for quantum information tasks, but most experiments have been photonic; exploring ICO in cavity QED could enable new applications.
method: The authors model two cavities coupled via a quantum switch, analyzing the dynamics and the emergence of ICO using master equations and numerical simulations.
result: They demonstrate that ICO can be achieved in cavity QED, with the degree of causal order controllable by system parameters.
conclusion: Cavity QED provides a viable platform for ICO, opening up possibilities for quantum information protocols exploiting indefinite causal order.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A review of the process tensor framework for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics using tensor networks.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are crucial in many quantum systems but computationally challenging; efficient methods are needed.
method: The paper reviews the process tensor formalism and demonstrates how tensor-network representations enable practical simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The framework is shown to be applicable across diverse physical fields, providing a unified approach to non-Markovian dynamics.
conclusion: Process tensor methods with tensor networks offer a powerful tool for simulating non-Markovian quantum systems, relevant to open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Lieb-Mattis entangled states enable robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing with intrinsic common-mode noise rejection.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for quantum sensor networks but suffers from common-mode noise; existing entangled states are fragile to such noise.
method: The authors propose using Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states of spin ensembles that are naturally insensitive to common-mode phase shifts, and analyze their performance for differential phase estimation.
result: Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for differential phase while being robust against common-mode noise, outperforming conventional entangled states in noisy environments.
conclusion: Lieb-Mattis states provide a practical and scalable approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, enabling robust quantum sensor networks.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, which are central to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and fluctuation theorems.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise identities and establishing connections to diffusion processes via continuum limits.
result: Achieves a unification of previously disjoint theories, enabling consistent treatment of observables across jump and diffusion regimes.
conclusion: The framework enhances the theoretical toolkit for studying stochastic thermodynamics and may facilitate new results in fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic bounds.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensates can process information through phase transitions, linking physical chemistry to cellular computation.
motivation: Cells must process high-dimensional environmental signals, but traditional molecular signaling may be insufficient; phase transitions offer a collective, nonlinear mechanism for information processing.
method: The authors present a conceptual framework drawing on phase separation, multivalent interactions, and condensate formation, discussing how these physical phenomena can implement computational operations like sensing, classification, and response.
result: They argue that phase transitions enable cells to perform complex computations, such as threshold detection and multi-input integration, with minimal molecular components.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation provides a powerful, physically-grounded paradigm for cellular information processing, with implications for synthetic biology and understanding of living systems.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits at finite depths, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Anticoncentration is a key property for quantum advantage and random circuit sampling, but its behavior under noise is not well understood. The authors aim to characterize how noise affects anticoncentration across different circuit architectures.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework using statistical mechanics mappings and replica methods to analyze the output distribution of noisy random circuits. They consider various noise models and circuit topologies.
result: They find that anticoncentration persists up to a depth-dependent noise threshold, with a universal scaling that is independent of circuit architecture. The transition between anticoncentrated and concentrated regimes is described by a universal function.
conclusion: The results provide a unified understanding of anticoncentration in noisy quantum circuits, which is important for assessing the feasibility of quantum advantage experiments and for designing error mitigation strategies.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing and simulation, but loading and imaging them with high fidelity and low atom loss remains challenging. EIT offers a way to perform nondestructive imaging and continuous loading.
method: The authors apply electromagnetically induced transparency to achieve nondestructive imaging of atom arrays, and use it to enable continuous loading of atoms into optical tweezers. They work in finite magnetic fields to control atomic states.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity imaging with low atom loss and efficient loading of atom arrays, showing that EIT can be a practical tool for neutral-atom quantum information processing.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading is a viable technique for improving the performance of neutral-atom arrays, with potential applications in quantum computing and simulation.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubits is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise cross-correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible frequency range.
result: They successfully demonstrate the method on a qubit platform, extracting noise cross-correlations and revealing new insights into noise sources.
conclusion: This technique provides a powerful tool for noise characterization in qubit systems, aiding in the development of more coherent quantum devices.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires fault-tolerant architectures that minimize space and time overhead, especially for neutral-atom platforms where native gates and error correction are still developing.
method: The authors design a transversal architecture that combines small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate quantum error-correcting codes, optimized for neutral-atom hardware constraints such as long-range interactions and parallel gate operations.
result: The architecture achieves significant savings in logical qubit count, physical qubit count, and runtime compared to conventional approaches, enabling megaquop-scale simulations with realistic hardware parameters.
conclusion: Neutral-atom quantum computers can feasibly reach megaquop-scale quantum simulation with the proposed transversal architecture, bridging the gap between current hardware and practical quantum advantage.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing bounds on loss function concentration to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus where gradients vanish, hindering trainability. Understanding how noise affects loss landscapes is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on the variance of loss functions under noise, relating expressivity (via the dimension of the dynamical Lie algebra) to concentration rates.
result: They show that noise can actually help by reducing the effective expressivity, leading to less concentrated loss functions and improved trainability, quantified by explicit concentration estimates.
conclusion: Noise in parametrized quantum circuits can be beneficial for training by counteracting barren plateaus, offering a principled guide for designing noise-resilient variational algorithms.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics beyond simple string breaking.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in confining gauge theories is important for quantum simulation and non-equilibrium dynamics, with potential implications for quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors use a combination of analytical models and numerical simulations, likely including tensor networks or exact diagonalization, to study the dynamics of string breaking in a quantum spin chain or lattice gauge theory.
result: They identify experimentally accessible regimes where string breaking exhibits rich quantum dynamics, including diabatic effects and non-adiabatic transitions.
conclusion: The work provides new probes for string breaking in quantum simulators, highlighting the interplay between confinement and quantum dynamics.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of methods for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, unified under a common framework.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems in quantum technologies, but the diversity of methods makes it hard to relate them.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and survey various numerical and analytical techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor networks.
result: The review highlights commonalities and differences among methods, providing guidance for selecting appropriate simulation techniques for different physical regimes.
conclusion: The unified framework clarifies the relationships between methods and aids in advancing simulations of non-Markovian open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in gate complexity and experimental feasibility.
motivation: Qudits offer potential resource savings in quantum computing by reducing the number of physical systems or gates needed for certain operations, such as the Toffoli gate.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decomposition techniques using qudits, and reviews experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Using a single qutrit can drastically simplify the Toffoli gate; qudits enable more efficient decomposition of multiqubit gates and can reduce circuit depth.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for quantum computing, particularly for near-term devices, though challenges remain in qudit control and error correction.

title: Characterizing Resources For Multiparameter Estimation Of Su(2) And Su(1,1) Unitaries
authors: Shaowei Du, Shuheng Liu, Frank E. S. Steinhoff, And Giuseppe Vitagliano
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2130 (2026).

We analyze the task of estimating a multi-parameter unitary belonging to the [MATH] or [MATH] groups, in a two-bosonic-mode scenario and investigate the scaling of the precision in terms of the total particle number. For the [MATH] case, the total particle number is conserved by the evolution and we discuss optimal states in fixed-[MATH] subspaces, identifying eigenstates of [MATH] as useful resources, even allowing simultaneous Heisenberg precision scaling for all three parameters. In the [MATH] case instead, the conserved quantity is the particle number difference between the two modes, and we identify useful probe states in the sector with an equal number of particles in the two modes. These states are analogous to the [MATH] case and would also allow simultaneous Heisenberg precision scaling for all three parameters. We then consider the more pragmatic scenario of an estimation via expectation values of time-evolved observables, which we restrict to be the first two moments of the generators. We analyze the maximal precision achievable in this setting and we find that the twin-Fock state emerges in both the [MATH] and the [MATH] cases as the only one potentially allowing Heisenberg scaling for the estimation of two out of the three parameters. As a complement, we also consider other probe states with fluctuating number of particles, with measurements restricted to quadratic expressions in the mode operators. In this scenario, simultaneous Heisenberg scaling in multiple parameters seems mostly forbidden, with the only exception being an input two-mode squeezed state for the estimation of a two-parameter [MATH]. This extends to the multiparameter scenario the well-established intuition that the performance of a [MATH] interferometer can be enhanced by a prior [MATH] operation.

.
tldr: Analyzes optimal probe states and measurement strategies for multiparameter estimation of SU(2) and SU(1,1) unitaries, achieving Heisenberg scaling in certain settings.
motivation: Multiparameter quantum estimation is crucial for quantum metrology; understanding resource requirements and achievable precision scaling for unitary groups is a fundamental problem.
method: The authors consider two-bosonic-mode scenarios, identify optimal probe states in fixed-particle-number subspaces, and analyze precision scaling using expectation values of time-evolved observables restricted to first two moments of generators.
result: Eigenstates of J_z for SU(2) and twin-Fock states for SU(1,1) allow simultaneous Heisenberg scaling for all three parameters; with restricted measurements, only twin-Fock states enable Heisenberg scaling for two parameters, and two-mode squeezed states for a two-parameter SU(1,1) case.
conclusion: The work extends single-parameter intuition to multiparameter settings, identifying specific states as resources for achieving Heisenberg-limited multiparameter estimation.

title: Classical Shadows For Sample-efficient Measurements Of Gauge-invariant Observables
authors: Jacob Bringewatt, Henry Froland, Andreas Elben, And Niklas Mueller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2127 (2026).

Classical shadows provide a versatile framework for estimating many properties of quantum states from repeated, randomly chosen measurements without requiring full quantum state tomography. When prior information is available, such as knowledge of symmetries of states and operators, this knowledge can be exploited to significantly improve sample efficiency. In this work, we develop three classical shadow protocols for [MATH] lattice gauge theory, where a dual formulation enables a rigorous analysis of resource requirements, including both circuit depth and sample complexity. Our approaches can offer exponential improvements in sample complexity over symmetry-agnostic methods, albeit at the cost of increased circuit complexity. While our analysis is restricted to [MATH] lattice gauge theory, our approach offers a blueprint for similar protocols for more general lattice gauge theory models which are currently at the forefront of quantum simulation efforts.

.
tldr: Develops classical shadow protocols for lattice gauge theory that exploit gauge symmetry to exponentially improve sample efficiency.
motivation: Estimating gauge-invariant observables in lattice gauge theory is crucial for quantum simulation but sample-inefficient without symmetry information.
method: Proposes three classical shadow protocols that incorporate gauge symmetry via a dual formulation, analyzing circuit depth and sample complexity.
result: Achieves exponential improvements in sample complexity over symmetry-agnostic methods, with trade-offs in circuit complexity.
conclusion: The approach provides a blueprint for efficient measurement of gauge-invariant observables in more general lattice gauge theories.

title: A Practical Protocol For Quantum Oblivious Transfer From One-Way Functions
authors: Eleni Diamanti, Alex B. Grilo, Adriano Innocenzi, Pascal Lefebvre, Verena Yacoub, And Álvaro Yángüez
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2124 (2026).

We present a new simulation-secure quantum oblivious transfer (QOT) protocol based on one-way functions in the plain model. With a focus on practical implementation, our protocol surpasses prior works in efficiency, promising feasible experimental realization. We address potential experimental errors and their correction, offering analytical expressions to facilitate the analysis of the required quantum resources. Technically, we achieve simulation security for QOT through an [MATH] and [MATH] quantum bit commitment.

.
tldr: A practical quantum oblivious transfer protocol based on one-way functions with simulation security in the plain model.
motivation: Oblivious transfer is a fundamental cryptographic primitive, and existing quantum protocols are often impractical or require additional assumptions.
method: The protocol uses quantum bit commitment and one-way functions to achieve simulation security, with analytical expressions for error correction.
result: The protocol is more efficient than prior works and includes analysis of experimental errors and resource requirements.
conclusion: The work advances practical quantum cryptography by providing a feasible QOT protocol.

title: On The Dynamical Lie Algebras Of Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithms
authors: Jonathan Allcock, Miklos Santha, Pei Yuan, And Shengyu Zhang
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2119 (2026).

Dynamical Lie algebras (DLAs) have emerged as a valuable tool in the study of parameterized quantum circuits, helping to characterize both their expressiveness and trainability. In particular, the absence or presence of barren plateaus (BPs) – flat regions in parameter space that prevent the efficient training of variational quantum algorithms – has recently been shown to be intimately related to quantities derived from the associated DLA. In this work, we investigate DLAs for the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA), one of the most studied variational quantum algorithms for solving graph MaxCut and other combinatorial optimization problems. While DLAs for QAOA circuits have been studied before, existing results have either been based on numerical evidence, or else correspond to DLA generators specifically chosen to be universal for quantum computation on a subspace of states. We initiate an analytical study of barren plateaus and other statistics of QAOA algorithms, and give bounds on the dimensions of the corresponding DLAs and their centers for general graphs. We then focus on the [MATH]-vertex cycle and complete graphs. For the cycle graph we give an explicit basis, identify its decomposition into the direct sum of a [MATH]-dimensional center and a semisimple component isomorphic to [MATH] copies of [MATH]. We give an explicit basis for this isomorphism, and a closed-form expression for the variance of the cost function, proving the absence of BPs. For the complete graph we prove that the dimension of the DLA is [MATH] and give an explicit basis for the DLA.

.
tldr: This paper analytically studies the dynamical Lie algebras of QAOA circuits, providing bounds on DLA dimensions and proving absence of barren plateaus for cycle graphs.
motivation: Understanding the trainability and expressiveness of variational quantum algorithms is crucial for their practical use; barren plateaus hinder training and are linked to DLA properties.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on DLA dimensions and centers for general graphs, then explicitly compute DLAs for cycle and complete graphs using representation theory.
result: For cycle graphs, the DLA decomposes into a center and semisimple part isomorphic to copies of sl(2), and the cost function variance is computed, proving no barren plateaus. For complete graphs, the DLA dimension is n^2-1.
conclusion: The work provides rigorous analytical results on QAOA DLAs, advancing the theoretical understanding of barren plateaus in variational quantum algorithms.

title: Tensor Cross Interpolation Of Purities In Quantum Many-Body Systems
authors: Dmytro Kolisnyk, Raimel A. Medina, Romain Vasseur, And Maksym Serbyn
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2114 (2026).

A defining feature of quantum many-body systems is the exponential scaling of the Hilbert space with the number of degrees of freedom. This exponential complexity naïvely renders a complete state characterization, for instance via the complete set of bipartite Renyi entropies for all disjoint regions, a challenging task. Recently, a compact way of storing subregions' purities by encoding them as amplitudes of a fictitious quantum wave function, known as entanglement feature, was proposed. Notably, the entanglement feature can be a simple object even for highly entangled quantum states. However the complexity and practical usage of the entanglement feature for general quantum states has not been explored. In this work, we demonstrate that the entanglement feature can be efficiently learned using only a polynomial amount of samples in the number of degrees of freedom through the so-called tensor cross interpolation (TCI) algorithm, assuming it is expressible as a finite bond dimension MPS. We benchmark this learning process on Haar and random MPS states, confirming analytic expectations. Applying the TCI algorithm to quantum eigenstates of various one dimensional quantum systems, we identify cases where eigenstates have entanglement feature learnable with TCI. We conclude with possible applications of the learned entanglement feature, such as quantifying the distance between different entanglement patterns and finding the optimal one-dimensional ordering of physical indices in a given state, highlighting the potential utility of the proposed purity interpolation method.

.
tldr: This paper uses tensor cross interpolation to efficiently learn the entanglement feature (set of bipartite Rényi entropies) of quantum many-body states, demonstrating polynomial sample complexity for states with finite bond dimension.
motivation: Characterizing entanglement in many-body systems is exponentially hard; the entanglement feature offers a compact representation, but its practical extraction for general states was unexplored.
method: The authors apply the tensor cross interpolation (TCI) algorithm to learn the entanglement feature as a matrix product state (MPS) from a polynomial number of samples, benchmarking on Haar random states and random MPS.
result: TCI can efficiently learn the entanglement feature for eigenstates of certain 1D quantum systems, and the learned feature enables tasks like quantifying distance between entanglement patterns and optimizing qubit ordering.
conclusion: The proposed purity interpolation method is a practical tool for extracting entanglement structure from many-body states, with potential applications in quantum information and condensed matter.

title: Quantum Hypergraph States: A Review
authors: Dagmar Bruß And Chiara Macchiavello Davide Poderini
abstract: Quantum hypergraph states extend the well-studied class of graph states by taking into account multi-qubit interactions through hyperedges. They provide a powerful framework to represent a family of quantum states with genuine multipartite entanglement. In this review, we provide a compact overview of the formal structure, entanglement characteristics, and operational relevance of hypergraph states in quantum information theory. We begin by introducing their mathematical foundations and generalizations of the stabilizer formalism. A central focus is placed on their entanglement properties, including the classification under local unitary and stochastic local operations with classical communication, the quantification of multipartite entanglement, and detection techniques via entanglement witnesses. We also explore other nonclassical features of hypergraph states, such as contextuality and genuine multipartite nonlocality, derived from stabilizer-based Bell-type inequalities. Additional attention is given to the role of hypergraph states in error correction, and as a computational resource in measurement-based quantum computation, and to their non-stabilizer character, quantified via resource-theoretic measures of quantum magic. Finally we review their generalization to higher dimensions, i.e. to qudits and continuous variables.
tldr: A review of quantum hypergraph states covering their formal structure, entanglement properties, contextuality, and applications in error correction and measurement-based quantum computation.
motivation: Hypergraph states generalize graph states to multi-qubit interactions, offering richer entanglement structures and potential advantages for quantum information tasks.
method: The paper provides a compact overview of mathematical foundations, stabilizer formalism, entanglement classification, and resource-theoretic measures of magic, along with generalizations to qudits and continuous variables.
result: It summarizes known results on entanglement quantification, nonlocality, contextuality, and the role of hypergraph states in error correction and as a computational resource.
conclusion: Hypergraph states are a versatile family with genuine multipartite entanglement and non-stabilizer character, relevant for quantum information theory and computation.

title: Detection Of Patterns In A Discrete-outcome Sensor Network
authors: Pranjal Agarwal, Nada Ali, Mark Hillery
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25100v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A discrete outcome quantum sensor network is one in which we are only interested in which detectors are activated. This can be studied in either the strong or weak interaction regime. If the detectors interact strongly with the environment, it is possible to definitely find which ones were activated. If the interaction is weaker, there is a possibility of making an error, and the object is to minimize the probability of this happening. Here we will be interested in this weaker interaction regime. We will also assume that only certain patterns of detectors will be activated, different patterns being translated versions of a fundamental one. Our object will be to find which pattern has been activated. We will look at both one and two-dimensional detector arrays and make use of techniques from minimum-error state discrimination.

result: Derives optimal discrimination strategies for pattern detection in the weak-interaction regime.
conclusion: Minimum-error state discrimination provides an effective framework for pattern detection in discrete-outcome quantum sensor networks.

title: Routing Codes: High-Rate Quantum Ldpc Codes With Short, Parallel Non-Local Connectivity
authors: Jiaxuan Zhang, Zhao-Yun Chen, Peng Duan, Jia-Ning Li, Tian-Hao Wei, Qing-Yang Hou, Wei-Cheng Kong, Yu-Chun Wu, Guo-Ping Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25330v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes are promising candidates for realizing large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computing. Although many codes with favorable theoretical parameters have been developed, their practical adoption must take hardware implementability into account. For mainstream quantum platforms such as superconductors and neutral atoms, the connectivity, the length of non-local couplings, and the complexity of wiring or atom rearrangement are key factors that dictate the difficulty of hardware realization. Here, we propose a new family of qLDPC codes, termed routing codes. Within this family, we find explicit instances whose encoding rates are comparable to those of bivariate bicycle (BB) codes, while systematically reducing qubit connectivity, shortening the length of non-local couplings, and, crucially, making all non-local couplings mutually parallel. This parallelism fundamentally eliminates wiring crossings in superconducting multi-layer architectures and drastically simplifies the scheduling of atom movement in neutral-atom arrays. Under circuit-level simulation, the weight-7 routing codes reduce the physical qubit overhead by approximately a factor of 8, compared to surface codes achieving a same logical error rate. These results establish routing codes as a hardware-centric qLDPC family that bridges the gap between theoretical optimality and near-term physical feasibility.

motivation: Practical adoption of qLDPC codes is hindered by hardware constraints like connectivity and non-local coupling length; routing codes aim to bridge theory and near-term feasibility.
method: Constructs routing codes by designing parity-check matrices that ensure all non-local couplings are mutually parallel, eliminating wiring crossings and simplifying atom movement scheduling.
result: Explicit routing code instances achieve encoding rates comparable to BB codes while reducing connectivity and non-local coupling length; circuit-level simulations show ~8x reduction in physical qubit overhead vs. surface codes at same logical error rate.
conclusion: Routing codes offer a hardware-centric qLDPC family that balances theoretical optimality with practical implementability on superconducting and neutral-atom platforms.

title: Quantum Tomography Of Free Electrons
authors: Y. Fang, J. Kuttruff, Z. Zhao, L. Moehrle, P. Hommelhoff, P. Baum
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25397v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Determining the quantum state of a given quantum-mechanical system is a fundamental task in physics. Quantum-state tomography has been pivotal for establishing quantum optics [1-4] and for revealing the properties of bound charges in materials [5-7]. An emerging other object for studying and utilizing quantum effects are free electrons, elementary particles that are central to high-resolution microscopy [8,9], electron-based quantum optics [10-17], ul-trafast electron microscopy [18-24] and particle accelerators [25-27]. However, free electrons are intrinsically incoherent, and we lack a broadly applicable method to measure and control their quantum state beyond special cases with discrete energy sidebands [28,29]. Here, we report a universal approach to measure arbitrary free-electron quantum states in continuous variables. Two monochromatic but spectrally shifted laser waves produce interfering quan-tum paths that directly reveal the density matrix and thus all essential properties of the pure wavepackets, the ensemble, and their interlinks. As a first application, we show how the quantum state of a single electron is modified by many-body Coulomb interactions of a sur-rounding electron gas. The reported concepts and results provide insight into otherwise hid-den correlations in electron beams and enable the controlled optimization of exceptional quantum states for free-electron quantum optics or quantum electron microscopy.

motivation: Free electrons are essential for high-resolution microscopy and electron-based quantum optics, but their quantum state is difficult to measure due to intrinsic incoherence.
method: Two monochromatic but spectrally shifted laser waves create interfering quantum paths that directly reveal the density matrix of the free-electron quantum state.
result: The method successfully measures the quantum state of a single electron and shows how it is modified by many-body Coulomb interactions with a surrounding electron gas.
conclusion: This approach enables controlled optimization of quantum states for free-electron quantum optics and quantum electron microscopy.

title: Quantum Metrology Of Electric And Magnetic Dipole Moments: Ultimate Limits And Optimal Regimes
authors: Simone Cavazzoni, Paolo Bordone, Matteo G. A. Paris
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25510v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The characterization of electric and magnetic dipole moments (EDM and MDM) in quantum systems is central to fundamental physics and quantum sensing. While EDM searches provide powerful probes of CP violation within and beyond the Standard Model, precise MDM estimation is crucial for high-precision magnetometry and the development of quantum sensors. In this work, we address the ultimate precision limits for separate and simultaneous estimation of both dipole moments in a generic two-level system coupled to electromagnetic fields. We analyze three classes of quantum probes/strategies: unitary and depolarizing dynamics, and thermal equilibrium states. For each, we derive the quantum Fisher information (matrix), identify optimal probes, and determine the ideal operating conditions, such as evolution times and temperatures, that maximize estimation precision. We further assess the compatibility and sloppiness of the statistical models, showing that orthogonal dipole moments configurations enable joint estimation of EDM and MDM, whereas parallel configurations are intrinsically sloppy, permitting only the estimation of a single parameter combination. Our results provide a unified metrological framework for estimation schemes ranging from neutron EDM searches to molecular magnetometry, and highlight the distinct roles of coherence, noise, and thermalization in multiparameter quantum sensing of dipole moments.
tldr: This paper derives ultimate precision limits for estimating electric and magnetic dipole moments in a two-level system using quantum metrology, analyzing unitary, depolarizing, and thermal strategies.
motivation: Characterizing dipole moments is crucial for fundamental physics (CP violation) and quantum sensing (magnetometry), but the ultimate precision limits and optimal regimes for joint estimation were not fully understood.
method: The authors compute the quantum Fisher information matrix for three probe strategies (unitary evolution, depolarizing dynamics, thermal states) and analyze compatibility and sloppiness of the statistical models.
result: Orthogonal dipole moment configurations enable joint estimation, while parallel configurations are sloppy; optimal evolution times and temperatures are identified for each strategy.
conclusion: The work provides a unified metrological framework for dipole moment estimation, highlighting the roles of coherence, noise, and thermalization in multiparameter quantum sensing.

title: Enhancing The Instantaneous Bandwidth Of Rydberg Microwave Sensors: A Proposed Scheme
authors: Yuhan Yan, Xuejie Li, Jinyin Wan, Xing Xia, Haojie Zhao, Binghong Yu, Jianliao Deng, L. Q. Chen, Huadong Cheng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rydberg atoms have emerged as a highly promising platform for microwave electric field sensing. Their practical deployment as next-generation sensors is fundamentally limited by the inherent trade-off between sensitivity and instantaneous bandwidth: enhancing instantaneous bandwidth while preserving high sensitivity remains a long-standing challenge in the field. Here we propose and experimentally demonstrate a novel scheme to overcome this limitation by introducing an auxiliary microwave field. This approach achieves a significant enhancement in instantaneous bandwidth while maintaining a high level sensitivity. Our experimental results demonstrate that an instantaneous bandwidth of 44.6[MATH]MHz ([MATH]22.3[MATH]MHz) is realized while achieving a sensitivity of 225.7[MATH]nV[MATH]cm[MATH]Hz[MATH]. This work provides a new pathway to simultaneously optimize the instantaneous bandwidth and sensitivity of Rydberg microwave sensors, facilitating their practical applications in radar and communications.
tldr: A scheme using an auxiliary microwave field enhances the instantaneous bandwidth of Rydberg microwave sensors while maintaining high sensitivity.
motivation: Rydberg microwave sensors face a trade-off between sensitivity and instantaneous bandwidth, limiting practical applications in radar and communications.

title: Inner And Outer Bounds On The Secrecy Capacity Of Degraded Broadcast Channels With Rmsi And Transmitter Csi
authors: Saeid Pakravan, Mohsen Ahmadzadeh, Ghosheh Abed Hodtani
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25351v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the secrecy capacity of a class of degraded broadcast channels in the presence of an external eavesdropper, where a transmitter aims to deliver two independent confidential messages to two legitimate receivers. The transmitter is assumed to have non-causal access to the channel state information (CSI), and each legitimate receiver possesses prior knowledge of the other receiver's message, referred to as receiver message side information (RMSI). We consider two distinct scenarios: complementary RMSI, where each receiver knows only the other's message, and non-complementary RMSI, where the side information does not perfectly align. For both scenarios, we derive novel inner bounds on the achievable secrecy rate region and present tight outer bounds, establishing the secrecy capacity region for the considered degraded channel settings. Unlike prior works, which primarily address general broadcast settings without secrecy constraints or omit key interactions between RMSI and CSI, our results provide a complete characterization of the secure communication limits under these conditions. Moreover, we extend our analysis to the Gaussian degraded broadcast channel, highlighting the pivotal role of CSI in enhancing secure transmission performance. Our findings demonstrate that the combination of RMSI and CSI can be strategically leveraged to expand the secrecy capacity region, thus offering new insights into secure multiuser communication system design.
tldr: This paper derives inner and outer bounds on the secrecy capacity of degraded broadcast channels with receiver message side information and transmitter channel state information.
motivation: To characterize the secure communication limits in multiuser broadcast channels where receivers have prior knowledge of each other's messages and the transmitter knows channel states.
method: The authors consider two RMSI scenarios (complementary and non-complementary) and derive achievable secrecy rate regions using coding schemes that leverage CSI and RMSI, along with tight outer bounds.
result: Novel inner bounds and tight outer bounds are established, fully characterizing the secrecy capacity region for the considered degraded channel settings, with extensions to Gaussian channels.
conclusion: The combination of RMSI and CSI can strategically expand the secrecy capacity region, offering insights for secure multiuser communication system design.

title: The Condition For Structured Coding To Improve Random Coding In The Binary Modulo-sum Problem
authors: Shun Watanabe Yohsuke Tsujino
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The modulo-sum problem, proposed by K\"orner and Marton (KM), is a representative problem in the field of distributed source coding. In the modulo-sum problem, two correlated sources are encoded separately, and the decoder decodes the modulo-sum of the sources. It is clear that the Slepian-Wolf (SW) coding rate region is achievable for the modulo-sum problem. K\"orner and Marton proved that the SW coding rate region can be improved by structured coding based on linear codes. Ahlswede and Han (AH) proposed AH coding, which combines structured coding and random coding, and expressed its rate using auxiliary random variables. However, it was conjectured that the minimum sum rate of AH coding cannot be smaller than the minimum of the sum rates achievable by KM coding or SW coding. Subsequently, Kakishima and Watanabe considered a multi-letter extension of AH coding, and designed the auxiliary random variables by taking the XOR of adjacent bits of the source sequences. Through numerical computation, they demonstrated the existence of source parameters for which multi-letter AH coding improves upon SW coding. However, this confirmation remained numerical, and the conditions under which multi-letter extended AH coding improves upon SW coding have not been analytically characterized. In this study, we analytically characterize the conditions under which multi-letter extended AH coding improves upon SW coding. Our condition is tight in the sense that it coincides with the complement of the known SW optimal sufficient condition. To obtain the conditions, we apply the method of types to reduce the evaluation of the multi-letter expression to a comparison of single-letter divergences, which might be of independent interest.
tldr: Analytically characterizes when multi-letter structured coding improves over random coding for the binary modulo-sum problem in distributed source coding.
motivation: The modulo-sum problem is a classic distributed source coding problem where structured coding (KM) can outperform random coding (SW), but the conditions for improvement via multi-letter AH coding were only numerically known.
method: Uses the method of types to reduce the multi-letter rate expression to a comparison of single-letter divergences, deriving tight analytical conditions.
result: Provides an analytical condition that coincides with the complement of the known SW optimal sufficient condition, showing exactly when multi-letter AH coding beats SW coding.
conclusion: The condition is tight and offers a complete characterization, advancing understanding of structured vs. random coding in distributed source coding.

Kakishima and Watanabe extended AH coding to a multi-letter setting, using XOR of adjacent bits as auxiliary variables, and numerically demonstrated improvements over SW coding for certain source parameters.
