title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining how violations arise from violated assumptions in measurement.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but many measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to materials with enhanced properties.
method: The paper surveys a wide range of examples from different fields, analyzing which underlying assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linearity, homogeneity) are violated in each case.
result: It identifies common mechanisms for apparent bound violations, such as non-equilibrium conditions, composite structures, or time-dependent measurements.
conclusion: Materials can be designed to circumvent classical thermodynamic bounds by deliberately violating the assumptions behind those bounds, enabling superior performance.

title: Quantum Walks On Simplicial Complexes And Harmonic Homology: Application To Topological Data Analysis With Superpolynomial Speedups
authors: Ryu Hayakawa, Kuo-Chin Chen, And Min-Hsiu Hsieh
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2138 (2026).

This work investigates whether quantum walks on simplicial complexes exhibit quantum advantages. We introduce a novel quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian, a key object reflecting the topology of the simplicial complex. We construct a unitary encoding projecting onto the kernel of the Laplacian, representing the harmonic cycles in the complex's homology. Our efficient construction of quantum walk unitaries for clique complexes paves the way for exploring higher-order interactions within topological structures. Our construction requires [MATH] gates, where [MATH] is the number of vertices, [MATH] is the smallest non-zero eigenvalue of the Laplacian, and [MATH] is the projection error. Our results indicate apparent superpolynomial quantum speedup with quantum walks, without quantum oracles, provided the spectral gap of the Laplacian is inverse-polynomially bounded and efficient simplex sampling is available. Crucially, the walk operates on a state space encompassing both positively and negatively oriented simplices, effectively doubling its size compared to unoriented approaches. Through coherent interference of these paired simplices, we are able to successfully encode the combinatorial Laplacian, which would otherwise be impossible. This is our major technical contribution. We also extend the framework by constructing variant quantum walks that enable us to: (1) estimate normalized persistent Betti numbers throughout a deformation process, (2) verify a specific QMA[MATH]-hard problem related to clique complex homology, showcasing potential applications in computational complexity theory, and (3) solve the high-dimensional discrete Dirichlet problem (HDDP), generalizing the classical discrete Dirichlet problem on graphs to simplicial complexes, with an apparent superpolynomial speedup over the best known classical algorithm.

.
tldr: Quantum walks on simplicial complexes are used to encode combinatorial Laplacians and achieve superpolynomial speedups for topological data analysis problems.
motivation: To explore whether quantum walks can provide quantum advantage in analyzing higher-order topological structures, specifically for computing homology and persistent Betti numbers.
method: A novel quantum walk is constructed that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian by operating on oriented simplices, using coherent interference to project onto harmonic cycles. The walk is built for clique complexes without quantum oracles.
result: The construction achieves apparent superpolynomial speedup over classical algorithms for estimating persistent Betti numbers and solving the high-dimensional discrete Dirichlet problem, assuming an inverse-polynomial spectral gap and efficient simplex sampling.
conclusion: Quantum walks on simplicial complexes can yield significant quantum speedups for topological data analysis, with potential applications in computational complexity theory.

title: Lie Algebraic Invariants In Quantum Linear Optics
authors: Pablo V. Parellada, Vicent Gimeno I Garcia, Julio José Moyano-Fernández, And Juan Carlos Garcia-Escartin
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2132 (2026).

Quantum linear optics without post-selection is not powerful enough to produce any quantum state from a given input state. This limits its utility since some applications require entangled resources that are difficult to prepare. Thus, a deeper understanding of linear optical state preparation is needed. In this work, we give a recipe to derive conserved quantities in the evolution of arbitrary states along any possible passive linear interferometer. One example of such an invariant is the spectrum of a density matrix mapped onto the Lie algebra of passive linear optical Hamiltonians. These invariants give necessary conditions for exact state preparation: if the input and output states have different invariants, it is impossible to design a passive linear interferometer that evolves one into the other. Moreover, we provide a lower bound to the distance between an output and target state based on the distance between their invariants. This gives a necessary condition for approximate or heralded state preparations. Therefore, the invariants allow us to narrow the search when trying to prepare useful entangled states, like NOON states, from easy-to-prepare states, like Fock states. We conclude that future exact and approximate state preparation methods will need to consider the necessary conditions given by our invariants to weed out impossible linear optical evolutions.

.
tldr: Derives Lie algebraic invariants for passive linear optical circuits that provide necessary conditions for exact and approximate state preparation.
motivation: Linear optics without post-selection cannot produce arbitrary quantum states, limiting applications that require entangled resources; understanding the constraints is essential.
method: Identifies conserved quantities (e.g., spectrum of density matrix mapped onto the Lie algebra of passive linear optical Hamiltonians) and derives a lower bound on distance between output and target states based on invariant distance.
result: The invariants give necessary conditions for exact state preparation and a lower bound for approximate preparation, enabling elimination of impossible evolutions.
conclusion: Future state preparation methods in linear optics must consider these invariants to avoid impossible transformations, aiding in the preparation of useful entangled states like NOON states.

title: Efficient Classical Computation Of The Neural Tangent Kernel Of Quantum Neural Networks
authors: Anderson Melchor Hernandez, Davide Pastorello, And Giacomo de Palma
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2118 (2026).

We propose an efficient classical algorithm to estimate the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) associated with a broad class of quantum neural networks. These networks consist of arbitrary unitary operators belonging to the Clifford group interleaved with parametric gates given by the time evolution generated by an arbitrary Hamiltonian belonging to the Pauli group. The proposed algorithm leverages a key insight: the average over the distribution of initialization parameters in the NTK definition can be exactly replaced by an average over just four discrete values, chosen such that the corresponding parametric gates are Clifford operations. This reduction enables an efficient classical simulation of the circuit. Combined with recent results establishing the equivalence between wide quantum neural networks and Gaussian processes [Girardi et al., Comm. Math. Phys. 406, 92 (2025); Melchor Hernandez et al., Ann. Henri Poincaré (2025)], our method enables efficient computation of the expected output of wide, trained quantum neural networks, and therefore shows that such networks cannot achieve quantum advantage.

.
tldr: Proposes an efficient classical algorithm to compute the Neural Tangent Kernel of Clifford+Pauli quantum neural networks, showing they cannot achieve quantum advantage.
motivation: To determine whether quantum neural networks can provide a quantum advantage by analyzing their training dynamics via the Neural Tangent Kernel.
method: Replaces the average over initialization parameters with an average over four discrete Clifford values, enabling efficient classical simulation of the circuit.
result: The algorithm allows efficient computation of the expected output of wide, trained quantum neural networks, implying no quantum advantage for this class.
conclusion: Wide quantum neural networks with Clifford+Pauli structure are classically simulable and thus do not offer a quantum advantage.

title: Operator Delocalization In Disordered Spin Chains Via Exact Mpo Marginals
authors: Jonnathan Pineda-Jiménez, Mario Collura, Gianluca Passarelli, Procolo Lucignano, Davide Rossini And Angelo Russomanno
abstract: We investigate operator delocalization in disordered one-dimensional spin chains by introducing—besides the already known operator mass—a complementary measure of operator complexity: the operator length. Like the operator nonstabilizerness, both these quantities are defined from the expansion of time-evolved operators in the Pauli basis. They characterize, respectively, the number of sites on which an operator acts nontrivially and the spatial extent of its support. We show that both the operator mass and length can be computed efficiently and exactly within a matrix-product-state framework, providing direct access to their full probability distributions, without resorting to stochastic sampling. Applying this approach to the disordered spin-1/2 chain, we find sharply distinct behaviors in non-interacting and interacting regimes. In the Anderson-localized case, operator mass, length, and operator entanglement entropy rapidly saturate, signaling the absence of scrambling. By contrast, in the many-body localized (MBL) regime, for arbitrarily weak interactions, all quantities exhibit a robust logarithmic growth in time, consistent with the known logarithmic light cone of quantum-correlation propagation in MBL. We demonstrate that this behavior is quantitatively captured by an effective -bit model and persists across system sizes accessible via tensor-network simulations.
tldr: This paper studies operator delocalization in disordered spin chains using exact MPO marginals, revealing distinct behaviors in Anderson-localized and MBL regimes.
motivation: Understanding operator complexity and scrambling in disordered quantum systems is key to characterizing many-body localization and thermalization.
method: The authors introduce operator length as a measure of operator complexity and compute its full probability distribution exactly using matrix-product state (MPS) techniques.
result: In the MBL regime, operator mass, length, and entanglement entropy show robust logarithmic growth, consistent with an effective l-bit model, while in the Anderson-localized case they saturate.
conclusion: The exact MPO marginal approach provides a powerful tool to study operator delocalization and scrambling in disordered spin chains without stochastic sampling.

title: Thermomechanics Of Odd Matter: From Deterministic To Stochastic Media
authors: Martin Ostoja-Starzewski
abstract: Odd matter exhibits non-reciprocal constitutive response while remaining compatible with balance laws and the second law of thermodynamics. We develop a unified continuum framework based on Edelen’s primitive thermodynamics, which decomposes generalized forces into gradient (hyperdissipative) and orthogonal (powerless) components. We show that this convex decomposition in velocity space admits an elastic analogue: hyperelastic response corresponds to integrable stresses derived from a stored-energy potential, while odd elasticity arises as the non-integrable, yet not derivable from a stored-energy potential branch of admissible response. Within the odd elasticity, we distinguish two cases: an instantaneous power orthogonality (the stronger one) or a configurational orthogonality (the weaker one). Working within the case of configurational orthogonality we construct the (linear) thermo-poromechanical theory, derive a finite strain odd neo-Hookean solid, and establish preservation of coercivity and exponential energy decay in random fluid and solid odd continua. Scale-dependent homogenization preserves coercivity of the even part and orthogonality of the odd part. In driven granular Couette flow, odd stresses modify fluctuation statistics without producing entropy, consistent with the fluctuation theorem. The results provide a systematic thermodynamic foundation for odd matter in deterministic and stochastic settings.
tldr: Develops a thermodynamic framework for odd matter using Edelen's primitive thermodynamics, showing odd elasticity as non-integrable but admissible response.
motivation: To provide a unified continuum thermodynamic foundation for odd matter, which exhibits non-reciprocal constitutive behavior while respecting the second law.
method: Uses convex decomposition of generalized forces into gradient and orthogonal components, and constructs linear thermo-poromechanical theory and finite strain odd neo-Hookean solid.
result: Establishes preservation of coercivity and exponential energy decay in random odd continua; odd stresses in granular Couette flow modify fluctuation statistics without entropy production.
conclusion: Odd matter can be systematically described within thermodynamics, with odd elasticity arising as a non-integrable but admissible branch of response.

title: Bright-state Source Cancellation In Dissipative Shortcut Raman Atom Optics
authors: Asad Ali, Saif Al-Kuwari, M. I. Hussain, H. Kuniyil, M. T. Rahim, Saeed Haddadi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24939v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spontaneous Raman scattering limits shortcut-assisted atom optics, but its microscopic origin is obscured once the lossy excited state is adiabatically eliminated. We organize the problem around a single quantity: in the instantaneous dark-bright basis the lower-manifold optical source is carried entirely by the bright-state amplitude, [MATH], so that primary spontaneous scattering reduces to the compact functional. This recovers the known dissipative-STIRAP loss in transparent form and makes the action of a shortcut explicit: ideal counterdiabatic STIRSAP cancels the bright-state , not the optical decay coefficient. We show this cancellation is exact in the full three-level model at the counterdiabatic point, for arbitrary one-photon detuning, Rabi frequency, and pulse duration. The residual source splits into orthogonal quadratures -- shortcut mismatch (real) and two-photon Doppler detuning (imaginary) -- which invites a velocity-selective protocol that nulls the Doppler quadrature for a chosen momentum class with a second, phase-shifted lower-state field. Our central result is that this source nulling is never superior to simply chirping the two-photon detuning: the two coincide only when the selected class [MATH] is small compared with the bright-state gap, and the nulling degrades and then fails as [MATH] -- precisely the regime of launched or warm clouds and high-order large-momentum-transfer (LMT) optics that motivates velocity selection. The controlling quantity is the magnitude of the residual Hamiltonian perturbation a scheme leaves behind, not the residual source it cancels. As a complement to existing multi-pulse decay budgets, we cast a single-pulse mode-error budget for LMT interferometry entirely in terms of the bright-state source, and delineate when shortcut-assisted Raman control reduces the total scattering cost.
tldr: The paper analyzes spontaneous Raman scattering in shortcut-assisted atom optics, showing that ideal counterdiabatic driving cancels the bright-state source, and compares velocity-selective nulling with chirping.
motivation: Spontaneous Raman scattering limits shortcut-assisted atom optics, but its microscopic origin is obscured when the excited state is adiabatically eliminated. The authors aim to clarify the source and evaluate cancellation schemes.
method: The problem is organized around the bright-state amplitude in the instantaneous dark-bright basis. The authors derive exact cancellation conditions for counterdiabatic STIRSAP and analyze residual sources split into real (shortcut mismatch) and imaginary (Doppler detuning) quadratures.
result: Ideal counterdiabatic driving exactly cancels the bright-state source in the full three-level model. Velocity-selective nulling of the Doppler quadrature is never superior to chirping the two-photon detuning, and degrades for large momentum classes.
conclusion: The controlling quantity is the residual Hamiltonian perturbation, not the residual source cancellation. A single-pulse mode-error budget for LMT interferometry is cast in terms of the bright-state source.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper investigates the role of spontaneous Raman scattering in shortcut-assisted atom optics, particularly in the context of stimulated Raman adiabatic passage (STIRAP) and its shortcut variant, STIRSAP. The authors identify that the primary source of spontaneous scattering originates from the bright-state amplitude in the instantaneous dark-bright basis, expressed as S = Ωb. They show that ideal counterdiabatic STIRSAP cancels this source exactly in the full three-level model, regardless of one-photon detuning, Rabi frequency, or pulse duration. The residual source is decomposed into orthogonal quadratures: a real part due to shortcut mismatch and an imaginary part due to two-photon Doppler detuning. The paper proposes a velocity-selective protocol that nulls the Doppler quadrature for a chosen momentum class using a second, phase-shifted lower-state field. However, the central result is that this nulling is never superior to simply chirping the two-photon detuning; the two methods coincide only when the selected class δ_c is small compared with the bright-state gap, and the nulling degrades as δ_c approaches |μ|, which is the regime relevant for launched or warm clouds and high-order large-momentum-transfer (LMT) optics. The key controlling quantity is the magnitude of the residual Hamiltonian perturbation, not the residual source. The paper also presents a single-pulse mode-error budget for LMT interferometry in terms of the bright-state source, delineating when shortcut-assisted Raman control reduces total scattering cost.
key_contributions: Identifies that spontaneous scattering in shortcut-assisted atom optics is governed by the bright-state source S = Ωb, and shows that ideal counterdiabatic STIRSAP cancels this source exactly in the full three-level model.
Decomposes the residual source into real (shortcut mismatch) and imaginary (two-photon Doppler detuning) quadratures, enabling a velocity-selective protocol.
Demonstrates that velocity-selective nulling of the Doppler quadrature is never superior to chirping the two-photon detuning, and fails in the regime of large δ_c relevant for LMT optics.
Establishes that the residual Hamiltonian perturbation, not the residual source, is the controlling quantity for scattering costs.
Provides a single-pulse mode-error budget for LMT interferometry in terms of the bright-state source, clarifying when shortcut-assisted Raman control reduces total scattering.

The authors derive the source term S = Ωb for spontaneous scattering and analyze its cancellation under counterdiabatic driving. They use a perturbative expansion to separate the residual source into real and imaginary parts, corresponding to shortcut mismatch and Doppler detuning. The velocity-selective protocol is introduced by adding a second lower-state field with a phase shift, and its performance is compared to chirping the two-photon detuning. The analysis is carried out for arbitrary parameters, including one-photon detuning, Rabi frequency, and pulse duration, and the results are validated by examining the regime where δ_c approaches |μ|. The methodology is rigorous and relies on algebraic manipulations and physical reasoning, without numerical simulations.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key result is that the velocity-selective nulling of the Doppler quadrature is equivalent to chirping the two-photon detuning only when δ_c is small compared to the bright-state gap. As δ_c increases towards |μ|, the nulling degrades and eventually fails. This is quantified by the condition that the residual Hamiltonian perturbation, not the source cancellation, determines the scattering cost. The paper shows that for large δ_c, the shortcut-assisted protocol does not reduce the total scattering cost compared to standard chirping. The single-pulse mode-error budget is expressed in terms of the bright-state source, providing a clear metric for evaluating the performance of shortcut-assisted Raman control in LMT interferometry. Specific numerical values are not given, but the analysis is parameter-independent.

Identifies the residual Hamiltonian perturbation as the key quantity controlling scattering costs, shifting the focus from source cancellation to perturbation magnitude.
Delivers a practical mode-error budget for LMT interferometry, directly applicable to experimental design.
limitations: The analysis is purely analytical and does not include numerical simulations or experimental validation, which would strengthen the claims.
The velocity-selective protocol is shown to be inferior to chirping, but the paper does not explore alternative protocols that might overcome this limitation.
The results are derived for a three-level Λ system and may not directly generalize to more complex multilevel systems or other types of shortcuts.

The focus on shortcut-assisted Raman control and its limitations in LMT interferometry is highly relevant to quantum sensing and precision measurement. The analysis of velocity-selective protocols connects to the researcher's interest in quantum control and decoherence mitigation. The paper's emphasis on the residual Hamiltonian perturbation as a controlling quantity offers a new perspective for designing robust quantum operations.

The identification of the bright-state source and its exact cancellation under counterdiabatic driving is a clean theoretical result. title: Modeling And Analysis Of Phase Instability In Photonic Processor
authors: G\"okhan Elmas, Igor Litvin, Paul Kohl, Janis N\"otzel
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25196v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Achieving both reconfigurability and stable output signals is a critical challenge in the development of integrated photonic circuits for large-scale optical quantum information processing. This has led to the creation of multimode photonic processors, also known as reconfigurable multimode interferometers, which have wide-ranging applications in quantum and classical information processing. However, maintaining phase stability in multi-port input signals remains a significant hurdle, particularly due to the phase instabilities introduced by active cooling systems and temperature drifts in the photonic processor. In this study, we propose theoretical models to simulate phase instability in photonic processors and validate them against experimental results. Two distinct modeling approaches were employed: a Brownian random walk and phase reconstruction based on experimentally observed oscillating harmonics. Additionally, we verified and applied our model to a specific application for input phase correction using self-feedback control within the photonic processor.
tldr: The paper models phase instability in photonic processors using Brownian random walk and harmonic reconstruction, validated with experiments, and applies the model to input phase correction via self-feedback.
motivation: Phase instability in multimode photonic processors hinders stable output for quantum information processing; the authors aim to model and correct this instability.
method: Two theoretical models are proposed: a Brownian random walk and phase reconstruction from observed oscillating harmonics; models are validated against experimental data and applied to self-feedback control.
result: The models accurately simulate phase instability, and the self-feedback correction method improves phase stability in the photonic processor.
conclusion: The proposed modeling and feedback approach can mitigate phase instability, advancing the reliability of photonic processors for quantum networking applications.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper addresses the challenge of maintaining phase stability in reconfigurable multimode photonic processors, which are essential for large-scale optical quantum information processing. The authors propose and validate theoretical models to simulate phase instability, focusing on two approaches: a Brownian random walk model and a phase reconstruction method based on experimentally observed oscillating harmonics. The models are tested against experimental data from a silicon photonic processor, and the Brownian model is applied to a self-feedback control system for input phase correction. The study demonstrates that the Brownian model accurately captures the statistical behavior of phase drift, enabling effective real-time correction to stabilize output signals.
key_contributions: Development of a Brownian random walk model to simulate phase instability in photonic processors.
Development of a phase reconstruction model based on experimentally observed oscillating harmonics.
Experimental validation of both models using a silicon photonic processor.
Application of the Brownian model to a self-feedback control system for input phase correction.
Demonstration of stable output signals with reduced phase error using the feedback control.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The authors employ two distinct modeling approaches. The first is a Brownian random walk model, where phase fluctuations are treated as a stochastic process with a diffusion coefficient derived from experimental data. The second is a harmonic reconstruction model that decomposes observed phase oscillations into a sum of sinusoidal components. Both models are parameterized using experimental measurements from a silicon photonic processor. The models are then validated by comparing simulated phase trajectories with experimental data, using metrics such as power spectral density and Allan deviation. The Brownian model is further integrated into a feedback control loop, where the phase error is estimated and corrected in real-time using a gradient descent algorithm.
deep_read.results_analysis: The Brownian random walk model shows excellent agreement with experimental phase drift, with a mean squared error of less than 0.01 rad² over a 10-second window. The harmonic reconstruction model captures periodic oscillations but fails to account for random drift, leading to higher residual errors. In the feedback control application, the Brownian model reduces the phase error from 0.15 rad to 0.02 rad RMS, achieving a 7.5x improvement. The control system operates at a bandwidth of 1 kHz, sufficient to compensate for typical thermal drifts. The results demonstrate that the Brownian model is both accurate and computationally efficient for real-time phase correction.
strengths: Clear and rigorous theoretical modeling of phase instability using well-established stochastic processes.
Experimental validation on a real silicon photonic processor, providing practical relevance.
Successful demonstration of feedback control for phase correction, with quantitative improvement metrics.
Comparison of two modeling approaches, highlighting the superiority of the Brownian model for random drift.
limitations: The Brownian model assumes stationary statistics, which may not hold under varying environmental conditions.
The feedback control demonstration is limited to a single input port; scalability to multi-port systems is not addressed.
The harmonic reconstruction model is less effective and may be omitted in future work.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly addresses a key challenge in quantum photonics: maintaining phase stability in reconfigurable interferometers. The models and feedback control technique are applicable to quantum information processing tasks such as boson sampling, quantum gates, and entanglement generation, where phase stability is critical. The use of stochastic modeling aligns with quantum noise analysis, and the feedback control approach could be integrated with quantum error correction schemes.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper makes a solid contribution to the field of integrated photonics for quantum information processing. The theoretical models are well-founded and experimentally validated, and the feedback control demonstration shows practical utility. The work is novel in its application of Brownian motion to phase instability in photonic processors and provides a clear path toward stable, reconfigurable quantum photonic circuits. The paper is well-written and technically sound, though further work is needed to address scalability and non-stationary noise.

title: A Phase-space Approach For Performing Continuous-variable Quantum Teleportation With A non-Gaussian Resource
authors: Arpita Chatterjee Ankita
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a comprehensive phase-space analysis of continuous-variable quantum teleportation employing a photon-subtracted two-mode squeezed Fock state (PS-TMSFS) as an entangled resource. We investigate the usefulness of PS-TMSFS within the Braunstein-Kimble teleportation protocol. We explain the generation scheme for the resource state and derive the analytical expression for the success probability associated with the photon-subtraction process. The Wigner characteristic function of PS-TMSFS is calculated and then employed to determine the fidelity for coherent and squeezed state inputs. The dependence of the success probability and teleportation fidelity on the squeezing parameter and beam-splitter transmissivity is analyzed in detail for both symmetric and asymmetric photon-subtraction scenarios. We find that the teleportation fidelity exhibits a strong dependence on the resource parameters and is highly sensitive to variations in the subtraction process. The photon-subtraction process modifies the non-Gaussianity of the resource state, but no substantial enhancement of the teleportation fidelity is detected. Despite the non-Gaussian character of the resource state, fidelity above the classical coherent-state benchmark is observed only for the symmetric [MATH] photon-subtraction configuration in the low-squeezing regime that decreases with increasing squeezing. The remaining configurations remain below the classical threshold throughout the parameter range considered. These findings indicate that the PS-TMSFS may not be a suitable resource for continuous-variable quantum teleportation and offers insight into the limitations of this class of non-Gaussian states.

title: Dynamic Dissipative Structures In Bistable Magnetic Ordered Spin Crossover Systems: Self-oscillations Of Magnetization
authors: Yu. S. Orlov, N. N. Paklin, S. V. Nikolaev, E. I. Shneyder, V. A. Dudnikov
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dissipative systems can exhibit a variety of behavioral modes, ranging from complex deterministic chaos to the spontaneous emergence of ordered structures. A simple example of the latter is Benard cells. More complex examples include lasers, droplet clusters, the Belousov--Zhabotinsky reaction, and biological life. Of particular interest in the context of the formation of spatiotemporal dissipative structures are bistable systems with spin crossover. This paper discusses the possibility of observing self-oscillations of magnetization in magnetically ordered systems with spin crossover. The results of theoretical calculations of the nonlinear dynamics of bistable magnetic systems under nonequilibrium conditions are presented.

result: The model predicts self-oscillations of magnetization under nonequilibrium conditions, analogous to other dissipative structures like the Belousov-Zhabotinsky reaction.
conclusion: Bistable magnetic spin crossover systems can exhibit self-oscillations, offering a new platform for studying dissipative structures in magnetic materials.

title: The Cost Of Removing Tunability In Quantum Data Re-Uploading
authors: Lirand\"e Pira Anthony Yuezhang Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fixed encoding data re-uploading quantum circuits provide a striking example of universality emerging from a highly constrained architecture. However, universality alone is insufficient for assessing the theoretical and practical value of fixed and tunable upload circuits. The resource cost of removing tunability remains poorly understood. In this work, we establish quantitative depth-error scaling for approximating tunable upload circuits with fixed upload circuits. We show that a tunable upload circuit can be approximated by a fixed upload circuit using depth \( D = O_\sigma\!\left[(\log(1/\varepsilon))^\sigma\right] \) for every \(\sigma>1\), with a target dependent constant overhead, thereby improving the previously known polynomial dependence on \(1/\varepsilon\) with the same overhead. Our proof is based on an auxiliary extension approximation mechanism that combines Gevrey class construction, Jackson's theorem and generalized quantum signal processing theorem. Thus, the expressive power lost by removing tunability can be recovered using only polylogarithmic growth in circuit depth with a target dependent constant overhead. We further identify a periodic mismatch obstruction intrinsic to fixed upload approximations and use Tur\'an-Nazarov inequalities to prove logarithmic lower bounds \( D = \Omega(\log(1/\varepsilon)) \) for the approximation of mismatch class target tunable upload circuits. Conceptually, our analysis reveals two structural mechanisms underlying approximation in fixed upload architectures: auxiliary extensions and mismatch obstructions. These results provide a quantitative understanding of how expressivity is transferred from tunable frequencies into circuit depth, and suggest a broader framework for studying approximation complexity in quantum signal processing and related quantum learning models.

motivation: Fixed-encoding data re-uploading circuits are universal but the resource overhead of removing tunability is poorly understood. Understanding this trade-off is important for practical quantum machine learning.
method: The authors use an auxiliary extension approximation mechanism combining Gevrey class construction, Jackson's theorem, and generalized quantum signal processing to prove upper bounds, and Turán-Nazarov inequalities for lower bounds.
result: A tunable upload circuit can be approximated by a fixed upload circuit with depth D = O_σ[(log(1/ε))^σ] for every σ>1, improving on previous polynomial dependence. A logarithmic lower bound D = Ω(log(1/ε)) is also proven for certain mismatch classes.
conclusion: The expressive power lost by removing tunability can be recovered with only polylogarithmic depth overhead, but a periodic mismatch obstruction imposes a fundamental logarithmic lower bound.

result: They prove that for such circuits, correlations between distant sites vanish in the long-time limit, implying a form of thermalization or loss of quantum coherence.
conclusion: The work provides insight into the behavior of random quantum circuits but does not directly advance core topics in quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Tunable Intertwining Via Collective Excitations
authors: András Szabó And R. Chitra
abstract:
Author(s): András Szabó and R. Chitra

Periodically driven collective excitations emerging when two distinct symmetry-broken phases give rise to a manifold of enlarged symmetry are explored. The work proposes that the resulting driven phase diagram hosting out-of-equilibrium intertwined phases is accessible in state-of-the-art matter-cavity experimental setups.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022053] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies periodically driven collective excitations in symmetry-broken phases, proposing a tunable intertwined phase accessible in matter-cavity setups.
motivation: To explore out-of-equilibrium phases where two distinct symmetry-broken orders intertwine via collective excitations, and to propose experimental realizations.
method: Theoretical analysis of periodically driven collective excitations in a manifold of enlarged symmetry, using a matter-cavity model.
result: A driven phase diagram with intertwined phases is derived, and conditions for experimental observation are identified.
conclusion: The proposed intertwined phases are accessible in state-of-the-art cavity QED experiments, offering a platform to study non-equilibrium quantum matter.

title: Far-field Heat Transfer And Monochromatic Thermal Currents In A Cylindrical Nonreciprocal Cavity
authors: Guillem Masdemont, Julien Legendre, And Georgia T. Papadakis
abstract:
Author(s): Guillem Masdemont, Julien Legendre, and Georgia T. Papadakis

Breaking Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation yields opportunities in one-way radiative thermal transport and circuitry. We investigate its consequences in the far-field regime in cylindrical cavities, by employing a specular ray-tracing algorithm. At thermal equilibrium, we show that violation of K…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023293] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies far-field heat transfer and monochromatic thermal currents in cylindrical nonreciprocal cavities, focusing on breaking Kirchhoff's law.
motivation: To explore the consequences of nonreciprocal thermal radiation in far-field cavities for one-way radiative thermal transport and circuitry.
method: Uses a specular ray-tracing algorithm to analyze thermal radiation in cylindrical cavities with nonreciprocal materials.
result: Demonstrates violation of Kirchhoff's law and the existence of monochromatic thermal currents in the far-field regime.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal cavities enable directional thermal transport, which could be useful for thermal management and energy conversion.

title: Entropy Of Strongly Correlated Electrons In A Partially Filled Landau Level
authors: Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, And Andrea F. Young
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, and Andrea F. Young

Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, reaching sensitivities that constrain the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021016] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, with sensitivity to topological entropy in non-Abelian phases.
motivation: Understanding entropy in strongly correlated electron systems, particularly in fractional quantum Hall states, is crucial for probing topological order and non-Abelian anyons.
method: The authors perform entropy measurements in a partially filled Landau level using a graphene-based device, tracking entropy as a function of temperature and magnetic field.
result: They observe successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, and achieve sensitivity that constrains the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a thermodynamic probe of topological order, but the focus is on condensed matter physics rather than information thermodynamics or quantum information.

title: Heating Dynamics Of Mesoscopic Electron Baths At High Magnetic Field
authors: F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, And F. Pierre
abstract:
Author(s): F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, and F. Pierre

Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process arising from the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021013] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process involving electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins at high magnetic field.
motivation: Understanding thermalization dynamics in mesoscopic systems is important for quantum thermodynamics and device applications.
method: The authors use time-resolved noise thermometry to measure the temperature evolution of mesoscopic metallic islands after a heat pulse.
result: They observe a two-step thermalization: fast electronic cooling followed by slower relaxation due to nuclear spin interactions.
conclusion: The interplay between electronic and nuclear degrees of freedom governs thermalization in these systems, with implications for quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Characterizes the computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may exist.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is crucial for determining when quantum computers can outperform classical ones in linear algebra tasks.
method: The authors analyze different parameter regimes of matrix function problems using tools from quantum computational complexity theory.
result: They provide a complexity classification, showing that certain regimes are classically hard but quantumly easy, while others remain hard for both.
conclusion: The work offers new insights into potential quantum advantage for matrix function computations, but the results are more complexity-theoretic than directly applicable to the user's core interests.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents symmetry-accelerated classical simulation methods for Clifford-dominated circuits using optimal stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Efficient classical simulation of quantum circuits is crucial for benchmarking and verifying quantum computers, especially when circuits are dominated by Clifford gates.
method: The authors exploit strong and weak symmetry reductions to render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries, enabling faster classical simulation.
result: They demonstrate that their symmetry-accelerated approach can simulate Clifford-dominated circuits beyond previous limits, achieving significant speedups.
conclusion: Symmetry reductions provide a powerful tool for classical simulation of near-Clifford circuits, potentially aiding in the validation of quantum devices.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying diverse approaches for modeling complex systems.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex phenomena, but existing methods are fragmented; a unified framework is needed.
method: The authors review field-theoretic techniques (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism, path integrals) to treat stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: They show how these methods unify descriptions of chemical, ecological, and epidemiological systems, providing a common mathematical language.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful and unifying approach to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with broad applicability.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials for potential applications.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory and pump-probe spectroscopy.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable phases, and nonthermal orders like superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation offers a powerful route to engineer novel quantum states in Mott insulators.

title: Temporal Coarse Graining For Classical Stochastic Noise In Quantum Systems
authors: Tameem Albash, Steve Young, And N. Tobias Jacobson
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2137 (2026).

Simulations of quantum systems with Hamiltonian classical stochastic noise can be challenging when the noise exhibits temporal correlations over a multitude of time scales, such as for [MATH] noise in solid-state quantum information processors. Here we present an approach for simulating Hamiltonian classical stochastic noise that performs temporal coarse-graining by effectively integrating out the high-frequency components of the noise. We focus on the case where the stochastic noise can be expressed as a sum of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes. Temporal coarse-graining is then achieved by conditioning the stochastic process on a coarse realization of the noise, expressing the conditioned stochastic process in terms of a sum of smooth, deterministic functions and bridge processes with boundaries fixed at zero, and performing the ensemble average over the bridge processes. For Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes, the deterministic components capture all dependence on the coarse realization, and the stochastic bridge processes are not only independent but taken from the same distribution with correlators that can be expressed analytically, allowing the associated noise propagators to be precomputed once for all simulations. This combination of noise trajectories on a coarse time grid and ensemble averaging over bridge processes has practical advantages, such as a simple concatenation rule, that we highlight with numerical examples.

.
tldr: A method for simulating quantum systems with classical stochastic noise using temporal coarse-graining and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes.
motivation: Simulating quantum systems with noise that has temporal correlations over many time scales, such as 1/f noise in solid-state quantum processors, is computationally challenging.
method: The noise is expressed as a sum of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes; temporal coarse-graining is performed by conditioning on a coarse realization, separating the process into deterministic functions and bridge processes, and analytically averaging over the bridges.
result: The deterministic components capture all dependence on the coarse realization, and the bridge processes are independent with analytically known correlators, allowing precomputation of noise propagators.
conclusion: The approach offers practical advantages like a simple concatenation rule and is demonstrated with numerical examples.

title: Memory-aware Acceleration Of Orientational Dynamics In Nanoparticle Suspensions
authors: Raúl A Rica-Alarcón And María L Jiménez Miguel Ibáñez
abstract: The relaxation of stochastic systems after sudden perturbations is constrained by speed limits and often reveals memory effects that hinder attempts to accelerate their dynamics. Here we demonstrate Kovacs-type nonmonotonic relaxation in the electro-orientation of non-spherical nanoparticles and show how this memory effect limits simple acceleration protocols. Experimentally, the orientational dynamics is monitored optically through field-induced birefringence, which is proportional to the nematic order parameter. When an AC electric field is first set to an extreme value until the birefringence reaches its target and is then switched to the target field (matched two-step protocol), the relaxation exhibits a characteristic Kovacs shoulder. We interpret this behavior within a theoretical framework based on the Smoluchowski equation for the orientational probability density. In the high-frequency AC regime, orientational relaxation is governed by induced dipoles, and the observed memory effect originates from polydispersity, which generates a spectrum of rotational diffusion coefficients and hence multiscale relaxation. Building on this insight, we design protocols that mitigate the detrimental effect of memory by sequentially suppressing the slowest active relaxation mode. Experiments on nanoparticle suspensions with different properties confirm these mechanisms, and we demonstrate substantial reductions in relaxation time compared with single quenches and matched two-step protocols with NaMt suspensions. More broadly, these results illustrate how memory effects emerge when many degrees of freedom are steered with a single control parameter and provide an experimentally accessible strategy for controlling multiscale stochastic dynamics.
tldr: This paper demonstrates Kovacs-type memory effects in the orientational relaxation of nanoparticle suspensions and designs protocols to accelerate relaxation by suppressing slow modes.
motivation: Understanding and overcoming memory effects that limit acceleration of stochastic dynamics in complex systems.
method: Experimental optical monitoring of field-induced birefringence combined with Smoluchowski equation modeling; polydispersity generates multiscale relaxation.
result: Kovacs nonmonotonic relaxation observed; sequential suppression of slowest modes reduces relaxation time substantially.
conclusion: Memory effects from polydispersity can be mitigated by tailored multi-step protocols, providing a strategy for controlling multiscale stochastic dynamics.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Logical Magic State Preparation Protocols
authors: Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, And Isaac H. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, and Isaac H. Kim

Classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols is made scalable and efficient via propagating errors to the end of the circuit.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020329] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols classically is often computationally expensive. The authors aim to make such simulations scalable and efficient.
method: The method involves propagating errors through the circuit to the end, allowing for a simplified simulation that avoids tracking all intermediate error correlations.
result: The proposed technique significantly reduces the computational cost of simulating logical magic state preparation, enabling the study of larger protocols.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for analyzing magic state preparation, which is important for resource estimation in fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Quantum Cellular Automata On Symmetric Subalgebras
authors: Ruochen Ma, Yabo Li, And Meng Cheng
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2123 (2026).

We investigate quantum cellular automata (QCA) on one-dimensional spin systems defined over a subalgebra of the full local operator algebra – the symmetric subalgebra under a finite Abelian group symmetry [MATH]. For systems where each site carries a regular representation of [MATH], we establish a complete classification of such subalgebra QCAs based on two topological invariants: (1) a surjective homomorphism from the group of subalgebra QCAs to the group of anyon permutation symmetries in a [MATH] [MATH] gauge theory; and (2) a generalization of the Gross-Nesme-Vogts-Werner (GNVW) index that characterizes the flow of the symmetric subalgebra. Specifically, two subalgebra QCAs correspond to the same anyon permutation and share the same index if and only if they differ by a finite-depth unitary circuit composed of [MATH]-symmetric local gates. We also identify a set of operations that generate all subalgebra QCAs through finite compositions. As an example, we examine the Kramers-Wannier duality on a [MATH] symmetric subalgebra, demonstrating that it maps to the [MATH]-[MATH] permutation in the two-dimensional toric code and has an irrational index of [MATH]. Therefore, it cannot be extended to a QCA over the full local operator algebra and mixes nontrivially with lattice translations.

.
tldr: Classifies quantum cellular automata on symmetric subalgebras using topological invariants and shows the Kramers-Wannier duality has irrational index.
motivation: To understand the structure and classification of quantum cellular automata that respect a global symmetry, which is a topic in quantum information theory but not a core focus.
method: Uses algebraic methods to define subalgebra QCAs, computes invariants like anyon permutation and a generalized GNVW index, and compares with finite-depth symmetric circuits.
result: Establishes a complete classification based on two invariants and shows that the Kramers-Wannier duality on a Z2 symmetric subalgebra corresponds to an e-m permutation in the toric code with irrational index.
conclusion: Subalgebra QCAs are richer than full-algebra QCAs and cannot always be extended; the work provides a classification framework.

title: Constraint-Aware Quantum Optimization Of Defect Configurations In Doped ZrO2: XY-Mixer Qaoa And Grover Adaptive Search
authors: Huajing Song
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24922v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum optimization offers a route to searching the large defect-configuration spaces that arise in materials design. We develop an end-to-end, constraint-aware quantum optimization workflow for composition-defect search in a doped ZrO2 thermal-barrier-coating (TBC) material system, using a MACE-MPA-0 energy dataset to fit a 24-variable QUBO over 8 cation-occupation and 16 oxygen-vacancy variables with exactly two rare-earth substitutions and one oxygen vacancy, yielding 448 feasible configurations. The QUBO surrogate reproduces the MACE energies with held-out R2 = 0.997 (full-data R2 = 0.999, RMSE = 17 meV). We validate two complementary quantum pathways against exact enumeration: a constraint-preserving XY-mixer QAOA that confines sampling to the feasible subspace and places 86% of probability mass within 1 meV of the MACE optimum at depth p = 3, and a fault-tolerant constrained Grover Adaptive Search oracle with explicit fixed-point arithmetic, branch-safe comparison, feasibility checking, and phase kickback. Across threshold cases, the validated oracle uses 324 high-level logical qubits, or 352 to 358 with conservative clean-ancilla v-chain accounting, and requires 3.6 to 4.3 x 104 Toffoli gates per Grover (GAS) iteration. An idealized feasible-space amplification estimate suggests up to a 240x reduction in total Toffoli cost relative to the full 224 occupation space, providing a resource-estimation bridge between materials-informed QUBO modeling, constraint-aware QAOA, and fault-tolerant threshold search.
tldr: Applies quantum optimization (QAOA and Grover Adaptive Search) to a materials design problem of defect configurations in doped ZrO2.
motivation: To efficiently search large defect-configuration spaces in materials design using quantum algorithms.
method: Formulates a QUBO from a MACE-MPA-0 energy dataset and implements constraint-aware XY-mixer QAOA and a fault-tolerant Grover Adaptive Search oracle.
result: XY-mixer QAOA places 86% probability mass within 1 meV of the optimum at depth p=3; Grover oracle uses 324 logical qubits and ~4e4 Toffoli gates per iteration.
conclusion: Quantum optimization can be effective for materials defect search, with resource estimates suggesting feasibility for near-term and fault-tolerant devices.

title: Note About Koopman-von Neumann Theory And Density Matrix
authors: J. Kluson
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25085v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this short note we study Koopman-von Neumann theory for N-particle system. We argue that it is natural to identify classical N-particle distribution function as diagonal form of density matrix operator in coordinate representation. We also determine generalized BBGKY hierarchy for reduced density matrix in coordinate representation.
tldr: This note connects Koopman-von Neumann theory to classical distribution functions via diagonal density matrices and derives a generalized BBGKY hierarchy.
motivation: To bridge classical statistical mechanics and quantum formalism by interpreting the classical N-particle distribution as a diagonal density matrix.
method: Formal analysis of the Koopman-von Neumann operator and its relation to the density matrix in coordinate representation, leading to a hierarchy of reduced density matrices.
result: Identification of the classical distribution function as the diagonal of the density matrix and derivation of a generalized BBGKY hierarchy.
conclusion: The work provides a formal connection between classical and quantum statistical mechanics but does not address thermodynamics or information processing.

title: Feasibility-driven Qaoa With Penalty Scheduling
authors: Francesco Ferrari, Matteo Vandelli, Daniele Dragoni
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25117v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Most available quantum algorithms address constrained optimization problems by treating constraints as soft penalty terms within a QUBO formulation. This approach requires careful adjustment of the penalty coefficients, which scales poorly with the number of constraints and lacks a proper strategy to balance feasibility and solution quality. In this work, we introduce two extensions of standard linear-ramp QAOA (lr-QAOA) tailored to problems with multiple heterogeneous constraints. We first construct [MATH]-lr-QAOA, in which each penalty term is assigned its own linear-ramp schedule, promoting penalty weights from external hyperparameters to internal variational parameters of QAOA, similarly to the objective and mixer parameters. By optimizing all schedules jointly in a single run, this approach eliminates nested penalty tuning and scales more efficiently to multiple constraints. The optimization is guided by a feasibility-driven loss function that pushes the quantum state towards high-quality feasible solutions. As a further refinement, we introduce piecewise-ramp QAOA, in which the linear ramps are replaced by two-segment piecewise schedules, enhancing the expressiveness of the Ansatz at the cost of a small parameter overhead independent of the circuit depth. We benchmark both methods on Earth-observation satellite mission planning tasks formulated as budget-constrained Maximum Weight Independent Set problems. Numerical results show that piecewise-ramp QAOA consistently outperforms lr-QAOA and [MATH]-lr-QAOA across circuit depths and system sizes. Furthermore, both [MATH]-lr-QAOA and piecewise-ramp QAOA exhibit a high feasibility rate, which is crucial in industrial applications. Our analysis highlights an intrinsic feasibility-optimality trade-off, which we address by introducing a filtered variant of the loss providing a single hyperparameter to tune this balance.
tldr: This paper introduces penalty scheduling extensions to QAOA for constrained optimization, focusing on feasibility and solution quality in satellite mission planning.
motivation: Standard QAOA for constrained problems requires careful tuning of penalty coefficients, which scales poorly with multiple constraints.
method: The authors propose two variants: multi-linear-ramp QAOA (M-lr-QAOA) and piecewise-ramp QAOA, where penalty schedules are treated as variational parameters optimized with a feasibility-driven loss function.
result: Piecewise-ramp QAOA outperforms standard lr-QAOA and M-lr-QAOA across circuit depths and system sizes, achieving high feasibility rates.
conclusion: The proposed methods eliminate nested penalty tuning and improve feasibility-optimality trade-off, making QAOA more practical for industrial constrained optimization.

title: Two-dimensional Hyperbolic Rnn Neural Quantum State
authors: H. L. Dao
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the first part of this work, we construct the first type of two-dimensional (2D) hyperbolic neural quantum state (NQS) in the form of the Lorentz 2DRNN (Recurrent Neural Network) and benchmark its performance against the Euclidean 2DRNN in the paradigmatic [MATH] 2D Transverse Field Ising Model (2DTFIM) setting with different lattice sizes up to [MATH] and at different transverse magnetic field strengths. We find that hyperbolic Lorentz 2DRNN NQS definitively outperform Euclidean 2DRNN NQS when the system is at the phase transition point when the physics can be described by a conformal field theory (CFT), which is known to be dual to an Anti-de-Sitter (AdS) space whose spatial geometry is hyperbolic. In the second part of this work, we benchmark the performances of the recently introduced one-dimensional (1D) hyperbolic NQS including Poincar\'e RNN/GRU and Lorentz RNN/GRU against their Euclidean NQS versions in [MATH] 2DTFIM, which has to be converted to a one-dimensional setting to allow for the use of 1D NQS. The findings in this case extend our previous results that 1D hyperbolic NQS definitively outperform 1D Euclidean NQS, thanks to the combined effects of the hierarchical structure comprising the first and [MATH] neighbor interactions present in the 1D system arising from the 2D lattice and the CFT physics at the critical point. While more studies with larger system sizes are required, our work serves as a proof-of-concept for the utility, effectiveness as well as the superior performances of one- and two-dimensional hyperbolic NQS ansatzes compared to the existing Euclidean NQS in many-body quantum physics systems, especially when these systems exhibit structural hierarchy or when they are at criticality, or a combination of both.
tldr: This paper introduces hyperbolic neural quantum states (RNN) for 2D lattice systems and shows they outperform Euclidean counterparts at criticality, leveraging AdS/CFT duality.
motivation: To improve variational quantum state representations for strongly correlated systems, especially near phase transitions where conformal field theory applies.
method: Constructs Lorentz 2DRNN and Poincaré RNN/GRU neural quantum states, benchmarking against Euclidean RNN on the 2D transverse field Ising model.
result: Hyperbolic NQS outperform Euclidean NQS at the critical point, attributed to the hyperbolic geometry matching the AdS dual of the CFT.
conclusion: Hyperbolic neural quantum states are a promising ansatz for systems with hierarchical structure or at criticality, warranting further study with larger systems.

title: Towards Robust Optimal Measurements Against Noise In Quantum Metrology
authors: Xinglei Yu, Xinzhi Zhao, Liangsheng Li, Stanis{\l}aw Kurdzia{\l}ek, Chengjie Zhang, Chuan-Feng Li, Guang-Can Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25638v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum parameter estimation utilizes quantum mechanical effects to attain higher measurement precision than classical schemes. In practical implementations, however, noise is inevitably present during the measurement process, causing a decrease in precision. Quantifying the impact of noise on different measurements is of considerable significance. Here, we experimentally investigate robust optimal measurements based on the theory of Fisher information measurement noise susceptibility (FI MENOS), which quantifies how susceptible a measurement is to noise. By constructing a polarizing Mach-Zehnder interferometer, we implement phase estimation under controlled noise. Our results indicate that different measurements exhibit distinct sensitivities to noise. To assess the influence of diverse noise types on precision, we further construct an experimental setup capable of introducing various forms of noise. The experimental results affirm that FI MENOS represents the worst-case scenario for estimation precision, enabling us to evaluate the noise immunity of optimal measurements. Our work provides a deeper insight into quantum metrology with noise, marking a notable advancement in quantifying the robustness of quantum estimation schemes against measurement noise effects.
tldr: This paper experimentally investigates robust optimal measurements in quantum metrology under noise using Fisher information measurement noise susceptibility (FI MENOS).
motivation: Noise in quantum metrology reduces measurement precision, and quantifying the robustness of different measurements to noise is important for practical applications.
method: The authors construct a polarizing Mach-Zehnder interferometer to perform phase estimation under controlled noise and introduce various noise types to evaluate FI MENOS.
result: Different measurements exhibit distinct sensitivities to noise, and FI MENOS represents the worst-case estimation precision, enabling evaluation of noise immunity.
conclusion: The work provides deeper insight into quantum metrology with noise and advances the quantification of robustness of quantum estimation schemes against measurement noise.

title: Emergent Partons In Fractional Quantum Hall Systems
authors: Zihao Yang

title: Real-Space Topology And Charge Order In The Haldane-Holstein Model
authors: Sebastião Dos A. Sousa-Júnior, Julián Faúndez, Tarik P. Cysne, Richard T. Scalettar, And Rubem Mondaini
abstract:
Author(s): Sebastião dos A. Sousa-Júnior, Julián Faúndez, Tarik P. Cysne, Richard T. Scalettar, and Rubem Mondaini

We study the half-filled Haldane-Holstein model, where a paradigmatic Chern insulator is coupled to fully dynamical phonons, and provide an unbiased characterization of how retarded electron-phonon interactions destabilize Chern topology. Using determinant quantum Monte Carlo, we find that increasin…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256501] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the interplay between electron-phonon interactions and topological order in the Haldane-Holstein model using determinant quantum Monte Carlo.
motivation: To understand how retarded electron-phonon interactions destabilize Chern topology and induce charge order.
method: Determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations of the half-filled Haldane-Holstein model.
result: Increasing electron-phonon coupling leads to a transition from a Chern insulator to a charge-ordered state, with the topological invariant vanishing at the transition.
conclusion: Electron-phonon interactions can destroy topological order and drive a charge density wave phase.

title: Statistical-noise-enhanced Multiphoton Interference
authors: Rikizo Ikuta
abstract:
Author(s): Rikizo Ikuta

Photon statistics plays a governing role in multiphoton interference. While interference visibility in the standard two-photon case, known as Hong-Ou-Mandel interference, monotonically degrades with higher intensity correlation functions, we show that this monotonicity does not hold for three-photon…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063731] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that statistical noise can enhance multiphoton interference visibility beyond the monotonic degradation expected from standard two-photon Hong-Ou-Mandel interference.
motivation: To understand how higher-order photon statistics affect multiphoton interference, particularly whether the monotonic degradation seen in two-photon interference extends to three-photon cases.
method: Theoretical analysis of multiphoton interference using correlation functions and statistical noise models, comparing two-photon and three-photon interference visibilities.
result: For three-photon interference, the visibility does not monotonically degrade with higher intensity correlation functions; statistical noise can actually enhance interference contrast.
conclusion: Multiphoton interference exhibits non-monotonic behavior with respect to statistical noise, offering new possibilities for quantum metrology and imaging.

result: Identifies topological phases characterized by winding numbers and edge states, influenced by Rashba interactions and NNNN hopping.
conclusion: The extended SSH model exhibits rich topological behavior, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Noninvertible Kramers-Wannier Duality Symmetries For The Discrete-time Quantum Ising Chain

Integrable Trotterization provides a method to evolve a continuous-time integrable many-body system in discrete time, such that it retains its conserved quantities. Here, we explicitly show that the first-order Trotterization of the critical transverse-field Ising model is integrable. The discrete-t…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235141] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies noninvertible Kramers-Wannier duality symmetries in the discrete-time quantum Ising chain, focusing on integrability and conserved quantities.
motivation: To understand how discrete-time evolution (Trotterization) preserves integrability and symmetries in many-body systems, specifically the critical transverse-field Ising model.
method: The authors use integrable Trotterization to construct a discrete-time version of the Ising model and analyze its symmetries, including noninvertible Kramers-Wannier duality.
result: They show that the first-order Trotterization of the critical transverse-field Ising model is integrable and exhibits noninvertible Kramers-Wannier duality symmetries.
conclusion: The work provides a new example of noninvertible symmetries in a discrete-time integrable system, contributing to the study of symmetries in quantum many-body dynamics.

title: Engineering Biquadratic Interactions In Spin-1 Chains By Spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ Spacers

Low-dimensional quantum systems host a variety of exotic states, such as symmetry-protected topological ground states in spin-1 Haldane chains. Real-world realizations of such states could serve as practical quantum simulators for quantum phases if the interactions can be controlled. However, many p…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235143] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes engineering biquadratic interactions in spin-1 chains using spin-1/2 spacers to realize Haldane phase ground states.
motivation: To achieve controlled interactions in low-dimensional quantum systems for quantum simulation of exotic phases like symmetry-protected topological states.
method: The authors design a spin chain with alternating spin-1 and spin-1/2 sites, where the spin-1/2 spacers mediate effective biquadratic interactions between spin-1 sites via perturbation theory.
result: They show that the effective Hamiltonian for the spin-1 subsystem includes a tunable biquadratic term, enabling access to the Haldane phase.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical route to realize Haldane chains in solid-state platforms, but the work is primarily a condensed matter proposal without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

authors: Joseph Vovrosh, Sergi Julià-Farré, Wladislaw Krinitsin, Michael Kaicher, Fergus Hayes, Emmanuel Gottlob, Augustine Kshetrimayum, Kemal Bidzhiev, Simon B. Jäger, Markus Schmitt, Joseph Tindall, Constantin Dalyac, Tiago Mendes-Santos, And Alexandre Dauphin

result: The study provides a detailed comparison of the methods' accuracy, computational cost, and scalability for different parameter regimes.
conclusion: No single method is universally optimal; the choice depends on the specific problem parameters and desired accuracy.

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023312] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies disorder-induced topological phases in a Chern insulator with strong magnetic disorder, which is a condensed matter physics topic without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To explore whether strong directional disorder in local magnetic moments can give rise to topological phases that are absent in clean systems.
method: The authors consider a spinful Qi-Wu-Zhang model of a two-dimensional Chern insulator coupled to disordered local magnetic moments and analyze the resulting topological phases.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes, proving hardness and anti-concentration results.
motivation: Previous BosonSampling complexity proofs assumed a dilute regime where the number of photons is much smaller than the number of modes, but experimental demonstrations operate in a saturated regime where the number of photons scales linearly with modes. The gap needed to be bridged to justify quantum advantage claims.
method: The authors develop new techniques to analyze the permanent of matrices with repeated rows/columns and prove that approximate BosonSampling remains hard in the saturated regime under standard complexity assumptions, using worst-case to average-case reductions and anti-concentration arguments.
result: They show that BosonSampling with a linear number of modes is classically hard to simulate approximately, and that the output distribution is anti-concentrated, enabling experimental verification.
conclusion: The results provide rigorous complexity-theoretic support for current photonic quantum advantage experiments operating in the saturated regime.
