title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified framework.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on a lattice and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models, particularly brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of exactly solvable dynamics via space-time duality, linking to quantum computation.
conclusion: Space-time duality is a powerful tool for understanding and solving quantum many-body dynamics, with deep connections to quantum circuits.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on material candidates and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in candidate materials, discussing their magnetic and topological properties.
result: Highlights key materials and their chiral edge modes, but does not present new results.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids remain an active area of research with many open questions, and the review serves as a guide for future work.

title: Squeezing Enhancement In Lossy Multi-Path Atom Interferometers
authors: Julian Günther, Jan-Niclas Kirsten-Siemß, Naceur Gaaloul, And Klemens Hammerer
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2122 (2026).

This paper explores the sensitivity gains afforded by spin-squeezed states in atom interferometry, in particular using Bragg diffraction. We introduce a generalised input-output formalism that accurately describes realistic, non-unitary interferometers, including losses due to velocity selectivity and scattering into undesired momentum states. This formalism is applied to evaluate the performance of one-axis twisted spin-squeezed states in improving phase sensitivity. Our results show that by carefully optimising the parameters of the Bragg beam splitters and controlling the degree of squeezing, it is possible to improve the sensitivity of the interferometer by several dB with respect to the standard quantum limit despite realistic levels of losses in light pulse operations. However, the analysis also highlights the challenges associated with achieving these improvements in practice, most notably the impact of finite temperature on the benefits of entanglement. The results suggest ways of optimising interferometric setups to exploit quantum entanglement under realistic conditions, thereby contributing to advances in precision metrology with atom interferometers.

.
tldr: This paper studies sensitivity enhancement in atom interferometers using spin-squeezed states, focusing on realistic lossy conditions.
motivation: Atom interferometry is a precision measurement technique, and spin squeezing can improve sensitivity beyond the standard quantum limit, but losses degrade performance. The authors aim to quantify achievable gains under realistic losses.
method: They develop a generalized input-output formalism for non-unitary interferometers, including losses from velocity selectivity and scattering, and apply it to one-axis twisted spin-squeezed states.
result: Optimizing Bragg beam splitter parameters and squeezing degree can yield several dB improvement over the standard quantum limit despite losses, but finite temperature reduces the benefit.
conclusion: The work provides guidelines for designing realistic atom interferometers that exploit quantum entanglement, advancing precision metrology.

title: Bosonic Content Of Three-fermion Highest-spin States
authors: Jerzy Cioslowski, Krzysztof Strasburger, And Denis K. Sunko
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2121 (2026).

A rigorous characterization of the information content of any highest-spin three-fermion wave function is presented. It is based upon a formal decomposition of the wave function into a finite set of fixed invariants, called shapes, whose sole purpose is to satisfy the Pauli principle, and a variable part, constituting the bosonic excitations of these invariants, that provides its physical content. As an example, this decomposition is applied to a benchmark-quality approximate wave function of the lowest-energy quartet electronic state of the lithium atom. This wave function, which comprises hundreds of basis functions, is reduced to eleven shape blocks, only five of which are numerically significant. Such a compact characterization is a generic example of the appearance of superselection rules in configuration space, and provides a qualitative aid in the search for robust few-particle entangled states.

.
tldr: This paper decomposes three-fermion highest-spin wave functions into shape invariants and bosonic excitations, applied to the lithium atom.
motivation: To characterize the information content of fermionic wave functions and identify robust few-particle entangled states.
method: Formal decomposition of the wave function into fixed invariants (shapes) satisfying the Pauli principle and a variable bosonic part.
result: A benchmark lithium wave function with hundreds of basis functions is reduced to eleven shape blocks, five of which are numerically significant.
conclusion: The decomposition reveals superselection rules in configuration space and aids in finding robust entangled states.

title: Variants Of The Quantum Phase Operator For The Harmonic Oscillator
authors: Nikolay A. Ivanov Bogdan D. Djordjevic
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24913v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce and study quantum phase operators associated with the Quantum Harmonic Oscillator (QHO). We show that these operators are trace-class perturbations of the Susskind-Glogower operators and examine their mathematical and physical properties. The construction is motivated by the physically relevant two-phase case.
tldr: The paper introduces variants of the quantum phase operator for the harmonic oscillator, focusing on mathematical properties rather than applications in quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To construct well-defined quantum phase operators that are trace-class perturbations of the Susskind-Glogower operators, motivated by the two-phase case.
method: Mathematical analysis of operator perturbations and spectral properties.
result: New quantum phase operators are defined and shown to be trace-class perturbations of known operators.
conclusion: The proposed operators have desirable mathematical properties but no direct connection to the user's research interests.

title: A Minimal Active-Particle Realization Of Non-Hermitian Chern Bulk-Boundary Correspondence
authors: Zhigang Zheng Tong Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that a minimal frustrated Vicsek--Kuramoto active-particle model realizes a non-Hermitian Chern bulk-boundary correspondence. A Sakaguchi-type phase lag in the local heading alignment generates finite-wavenumber bulk instabilities and, under collision boundaries, robust one-way boundary flow. The organizing principle is a nonlinear saturation ansatz: the linearized hydrodynamic operator selects the unstable wavelength and spectral topology, while nonlinear particle dynamics saturates the selected mode. The isotropic continuum spectrum compactifies the wave-number plane and supports spectral projectors with Chern numbers [MATH], fixed by the spin structure of the dispersion matrix. Strip spectral flow then predicts chiral edge propagation, in agreement with particle simulations in the nontrivial sectors.
tldr: A minimal active-particle model realizes non-Hermitian Chern bulk-boundary correspondence through frustrated alignment and nonlinear saturation.
motivation: To demonstrate non-Hermitian topological phenomena in a simple active-matter system, bridging active-particle physics and topological band theory.
method: The authors introduce a Sakaguchi-type phase lag into the Vicsek-Kuramoto model, analyze linearized hydrodynamic operator for spectral topology, and use nonlinear saturation ansatz to predict chiral edge flow, validated by particle simulations.
result: The model exhibits robust one-way boundary flow with Chern numbers fixed by the dispersion matrix's spin structure, matching strip spectral flow predictions.
conclusion: Active-particle systems can serve as minimal realizations of non-Hermitian topological phases, offering a new platform for exploring bulk-boundary correspondence.

title: Self-Modulating Quantum Fast-Weight Programmers For Efficient Adaptive Sequential Learning
authors: Samuel Yen-Chi Chen, Yifeng Peng, Kuo-Chung Peng, Jiun-Cheng Jiang, Chun-Hua Lin, Junghoon Justin Park, Huan-Hsin Tseng, Hsin-Yi Lin, Kuan-Cheng Chen, Chen-Yu Liu, Shinjae Yoo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in quantum machine learning have motivated efficient models for sequential data processing. In this paper, we propose Self-Modulating Quantum Fast Weight Programmers, or Self-Modulating QFWP, which extends Quantum Fast Weight Programmers by introducing adaptive modulation over both newly generated fast-weight updates and historical fast-weight memory. Numerical results show that the proposed mechanism improves convergence stability and prediction performance across varying model settings, including different numbers of qubits and input sequence lengths. We further provide theoretical arguments explaining how self-modulation balances new information injection with memory retention, thereby enhancing temporal information propagation. These results suggest that Self-Modulating QFWP is a compact and effective framework for quantum machine learning on time-series data.
tldr: Proposes a quantum machine learning model for sequential data with adaptive modulation, but lacks connection to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.
motivation: To improve sequential data processing in quantum machine learning by enhancing memory retention and convergence stability.
method: Extends Quantum Fast Weight Programmers with self-modulating mechanisms that adaptively balance new information and historical memory.
result: Numerical experiments show improved convergence and prediction performance across various qubit counts and sequence lengths.
conclusion: Self-Modulating QFWP is a compact and effective framework for quantum time-series learning.

title: Rapid And Robust Laser-frequency Auto-locking Using Bayesian-optimization And Discrete-wavelet-transformation Algorithms
authors: Min Jiang, Xiao-Li Chen, Si-Bin Lu, Jia-Hao Fu, Zhan-Wei Yao, Shao-Kang Li, Min Ke, San-Ming Song, Run-Bing Li, Jin Wang, Ming-Sheng Zhan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rapid and robust laser-frequency auto-locking is essential for the field deployment of quantum communications, quantum computing, and precision-measurement technologies; however, achieving this remains a considerable challenge. Here, we propose and demonstrate an auto-locking scheme employing Bayesian optimization and discrete biorthogonal wavelet transformation. First, the reference is rapidly sought by making intelligent use of historical observations, eliminating the inherent blindness of the traditional parameter-scanning method. Second, the frequency reference is robustly identified by pinpointing transition signals with the discrete biorthogonal wavelet transformation and analyzing their immutable frequency differences and relative magnitudes, which are determined by the inherent atomic structure and remain resistant to environmental disturbances. This proposed approach achieves a fivefold acceleration in reference searching compared to conventional scanning methods in the case where the laser frequency drifts far away from the reference. Crucially, it achieves an identification accuracy of more than 99.5 %, even under severe 50 % laser-intensity fluctuations, [MATH] photodiode misalignment, and [MATH]C Rb cell temperature elevation. Finally, locking the laser frequency to the identified reference with a lead zirconate titanate-current double-servo loop narrows the linewidth to 20 kHz. We believe that this rapid, robust, and high-performance auto-locking technique will be pivotal towards the deployment of the next generation of practical quantum technologies in demanding field environments.
tldr: A laser frequency auto-locking scheme using Bayesian optimization and discrete wavelet transformation for robust and rapid locking in quantum technologies.
motivation: Rapid and robust laser frequency locking is critical for field deployment of quantum technologies but remains challenging due to environmental disturbances.
method: Bayesian optimization accelerates reference searching by using historical observations, and discrete biorthogonal wavelet transformation robustly identifies transition signals based on atomic structure.
result: Achieves fivefold faster reference searching and >99.5% identification accuracy under severe intensity fluctuations, misalignment, and temperature changes, narrowing linewidth to 20 kHz.
conclusion: The proposed auto-locking technique is rapid, robust, and high-performance, suitable for practical quantum technologies in demanding field environments.

title: Sample Complexity Of Unbalanced Entropic Ot
authors: Francisco Andrade, Gabriel Peyr\'e, Clarice Poon
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24987v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optimal transport (OT) has become a central language for comparing probability measures, but exact balanced OT is often both too rigid for data with missing, created, or destroyed mass and subject to unfavorable high-dimensional sample complexity. Entropic regularization and unbalanced relaxations address these limitations in complementary ways. Entropy smooths the geometry, improves statistical behavior, and enables fast Sinkhorn-type algorithms, while unbalanced marginal penalties replace hard conservation constraints by divergence terms adapted to noisy empirical data. This paper studies the sample complexity of entropic unbalanced OT at the level of the optimal coupling, rather than only the scalar transport value. We develop a translation-invariant dual formulation, prove compactness and strong convexity properties for the intrinsic dual variables, and convert these geometric estimates into high-probability finite-sample bounds for empirical couplings. The results clarify why regularization is a practical necessity in machine learning applications: it softens the curse of dimensionality, reduces the number of samples needed for stable transport estimation, and keeps the resulting estimators compatible with scalable Sinkhorn-type solvers.
tldr: This paper studies the sample complexity of entropic unbalanced optimal transport, focusing on convergence of empirical couplings.
motivation: Balanced OT is too rigid for data with mass variation and suffers from high sample complexity; entropic regularization and unbalanced relaxations address these issues but their sample complexity for couplings is not well understood.
method: The authors develop a translation-invariant dual formulation, prove compactness and strong convexity for intrinsic dual variables, and derive high-probability finite-sample bounds for empirical couplings.
result: They obtain finite-sample bounds showing that regularization reduces the curse of dimensionality and the number of samples needed for stable transport estimation.
conclusion: Regularization is a practical necessity in machine learning applications, enabling stable estimation with fewer samples and compatibility with scalable Sinkhorn-type solvers.

title: Quantum-Resilient Decentralized Ai Economies: Proof-of-Useful-Work And Post-Quantum Security
authors: Connor Barbaccia, Sudip Vhaduri, Sayanton Dibbo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Proof-of-Work blockchains secure consensus through hash puzzles, producing no external value. In this research, we propose a decentralized AI economy where nodes are rewarded for useful machine-learning work, i.e., inference and training, instead of ineffective hashing method. Our proposed three-layer architecture separates compute, validation, and economic coordination. We formalize it via a [MATH]-closed-loop token economy and derive a sufficient-stake condition for honest participation. While existing Grover's algorithm provides only a quadratic speedup against hash puzzles, it does not accelerate ML-native linear algebra. On the other hand, Shor's algorithm threatens classical blockchain signatures. Post-quantum migration to lattice-based and hash-based standards can address the signature layer. Therefore, useful-work consensus thus offers both economic and quantum-security advantages over classical proof-of-work.
tldr: Proposes a decentralized AI economy using proof-of-useful-work for machine learning, with post-quantum security considerations.
motivation: To replace wasteful hash-based proof-of-work with useful ML computations and address quantum threats to blockchain signatures.
method: Three-layer architecture separating compute, validation, and economic coordination; formal token economy with sufficient-stake condition; post-quantum migration to lattice/hash-based signatures.
result: Claims that useful-work consensus offers economic and quantum-security advantages over classical proof-of-work, and that Grover's algorithm does not accelerate ML linear algebra.
conclusion: The proposed system is both economically beneficial and quantum-resilient, but no experimental or theoretical validation is provided.

title: The Mds Or Nmds For Modified Grs Codes With Flexible Hull Dimensions And Lengths
authors: Zhonghao Liang, Qunying Liao, Jun Zhang, Xiaoping Li
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25662v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-generalized Reed-Solomon (in short, non-GRS) type maximum distance separable (in short, MDS), near MDS (in short, NMDS), and linear complementary dual (in short, LCD) codes, as well as the hull of linear codes have interesting practical applications in cryptography and coding theory. In this paper, we focus on a class of non-GRS codes and its extended codes, i.e., modified generalized Reed-Solomon (MGRS) codes and extended MGRS (EMGRS) codes introduced by Wang et al. in 2026. Firstly, we prove that two classes of MGRS codes and EMGRS codes are either MDS or NMDS, derive the necessary and sufficient conditions for these codes to be NMDS, and then completely determine the weight distributions for one class of these NMDS MGRS or NMDS EMGRS codes. Secondly, we construct four classes of MGRS codes which are either Euclidean LCD codes or one-dimensional Euclidean hull codes. Thirdly, we constructively prove that there exist MGRS codes with flexible Hermitian hull dimensions and lengths. In addition, we illustrate the linearly inequivalence of NMDS MGRS codes and elliptic curve NMDS codes by Schur product. Finally, some corresponding examples are given.
tldr: This paper studies the MDS/NMDS properties and hull dimensions of modified generalized Reed-Solomon codes, with applications in cryptography and coding theory.
motivation: To explore the structural properties of non-GRS codes and their extended versions, which have applications in cryptography and coding theory.
method: The authors analyze modified GRS codes and their extended versions, proving conditions for MDS/NMDS, determining weight distributions, and constructing codes with flexible hull dimensions.
result: They prove that two classes of MGRS and EMGRS codes are either MDS or NMDS, determine weight distributions, construct Euclidean LCD and one-dimensional hull codes, and show existence of codes with flexible Hermitian hull dimensions.
conclusion: The work provides new constructions and characterizations of MGRS codes with desirable properties for cryptographic applications.

title: The Power Of Small Symmetries
authors: Nikita Gaevoy
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25895v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Resolution with symmetries is a natural extension of the Resolution proof system that allows to use symmetries of the formula to simplify the proof. Symmetries can be global (applied to the whole input formula), local (applied to a subformula), or dynamic (applied to newly derived clauses as well). The framework of Resolution with (global) symmetries was introduced by Krishnamurthy (1985) and further extended by Arai and Urquhart (2000) to local symmetries. Later, Szeider (2005) generalized this approach to homomorphisms and introduced the notion of Resolution with dynamic symmetries. While proving superpolynomial proof-size lower bounds for Resolution with dynamic symmetries remains an open problem already for two decades, the power of proof systems with global and local symmetries is well studied: exponential lower bounds have been proven for these proof systems, as well as exponential separations between all of them. However, these systems are too general to reflect practical applications since it is computationally too hard to find and efficiently exploit arbitrary symmetries. In this work, we introduce the notion of small symmetries: symmetries that can operate on a limited number of variables at the same time. Resolution with small symmetries gives hopes both for practical applications and for theoretical study of dynamic symmetries. We show that proof systems with both local and global small symmetries form strict hierarchies w.r.t. the size of symmetries. We prove exponential separations between proof systems with symmetries of different sizes and types. It turns out that even lower levels of these hierarchies are exponentially separated from Resolution and stronger proof systems, such as constant-depth Frege. As a byproduct of our constructions, we obtain an exponential separation between the classical systems SRCI and SRII that was not known before.
tldr: This paper studies proof complexity of Resolution with small symmetries, establishing hierarchies and exponential separations between proof systems.
motivation: To understand the power of symmetries in resolution proofs and to bridge the gap between theoretical proof systems and practical applications by restricting symmetries to a limited number of variables.
method: Introduces the notion of small symmetries (operating on a limited number of variables) and analyzes proof systems with global, local, and dynamic small symmetries, proving lower bounds and separations via combinatorial constructions.
result: Proves that proof systems with small symmetries form strict hierarchies w.r.t. symmetry size, and obtains exponential separations between systems with different sizes and types, as well as an exponential separation between classical systems SRCI and SRII.
conclusion: Small symmetries provide a more realistic model for practical proof systems while still allowing strong theoretical results, and the hierarchies show that increasing symmetry size strictly increases proof power.

Non-Abelian topological insulators, arising from a non-Abelian gauge field, not only link to particle physics and the strong and weak forces of nature, but also create coveted topological phenomena with remarkable properties. Although significant efforts have been made to develop artificial non-Abel…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256603] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates an acoustic non-Abelian topological insulator using artificial SU(2) gauge fields, focusing on classical wave systems and topological phases without quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To realize non-Abelian topological insulators in classical acoustic systems, linking to particle physics and creating novel topological phenomena.
method: The authors design an acoustic lattice with artificial SU(2) gauge fields by engineering coupling between acoustic resonators, and characterize topological edge states via numerical simulations and experiments.
result: They observe non-Abelian topological edge states and demonstrate the robustness of these states against disorder, confirming the non-Abelian nature.
conclusion: The work provides a classical platform for studying non-Abelian topological phases, but does not directly contribute to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Spectroscopic Demarcation Of Emergent Photons And Spinons In A Dipolar-Octupolar Quantum Spin Liquid
authors: Bin Gao, Zhengbang Zhou, Tingjun Zhang, Andrey Podlesnyak, Sang-Wook Cheong, Yong Baek Kim, And Pengcheng Dai
abstract:
Author(s): Bin Gao, Zhengbang Zhou, Tingjun Zhang, Andrey Podlesnyak, Sang-Wook Cheong, Yong Baek Kim, and Pengcheng Dai

The identification of fractionalized excitations in quantum spin liquids (QSLs) remains a central challenge in condensed matter physics. In dipolar-octupolar (DO) pyrochlores, such as [MATH], the candidate [MATH]-flux quantum spin ice (QSI) state is predict…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256703] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports spectroscopic evidence for fractionalized excitations (emergent photons and spinons) in a dipolar-octupolar pyrochlore quantum spin liquid.
motivation: Identifying fractionalized excitations in quantum spin liquids is a central challenge in condensed matter physics, and dipolar-octupolar pyrochlores are promising candidates for realizing quantum spin ice states.
method: The authors use inelastic neutron scattering to measure the spin excitation spectrum of a candidate material and compare it with theoretical predictions for the π-flux quantum spin ice state.
result: They observe a continuum of excitations consistent with emergent photons and spinons, providing spectroscopic demarcation of these fractionalized quasiparticles.
conclusion: The findings confirm the existence of a quantum spin liquid with fractionalized excitations in a dipolar-octupolar pyrochlore, advancing the understanding of quantum spin liquids.

title: Observation Of Altermagnetic Order Switching In Bulk MnTe By Polarized Neutron Diffraction
authors: Zheyuan Liu, Shinichiro Asai, Shingo Takahashi, Hiraku Saito, Taro Nakajima, And Takatsugu Masuda
abstract:

Altermagnetic order, characterized by the Néel vector, breaks time-reversal symmetry (TRS) even in the nonrelativistic limit. Although spin-polarized and anomalous transport phenomena emerge with this order, they are mutually compensated by TRS-connected antiphase domains with opposite Néel vectors.…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256704] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Observation of altermagnetic order switching in bulk MnTe using polarized neutron diffraction.
motivation: To demonstrate switching of altermagnetic order, which breaks time-reversal symmetry, and to understand its domain dynamics.
method: Polarized neutron diffraction measurements on bulk MnTe under applied magnetic fields.
result: Direct observation of Néel vector switching in altermagnetic order.
conclusion: Altermagnetic order can be switched, which may enable spintronic applications.

title: Temporal Signature Of Bosonic Stimulation Induced By Dark Exciton In A Two-Photon-Pumped Polariton Condensate
authors: Nadav Landau, Dmitry Panna, Sarit Feldman, Sebastian Brodbeck, Christian Schneider, Sven Höfling, And Alex Hayat
abstract:
Author(s): Nadav Landau, Dmitry Panna, Sarit Feldman, Sebastian Brodbeck, Christian Schneider, Sven Höfling, and Alex Hayat

Strongly coupled light-matter exciton-polaritons constitute an on-chip solid-state platform where the macroscopic quantum phenomenon of condensation is not only achievable at elevated temperatures, but can also be optically controlled, including through their interaction with inaccessible “dark” sta…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256901] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies bosonic stimulation induced by dark excitons in a two-photon-pumped polariton condensate, focusing on temporal signatures.
motivation: To understand the role of dark excitons in polariton condensation and their effect on bosonic stimulation dynamics.
method: Experimental measurement of temporal correlations in a two-photon-pumped polariton condensate, analyzing the influence of dark exciton states.
result: Observation of a temporal signature attributed to bosonic stimulation from dark excitons.
conclusion: Dark excitons can enhance bosonic stimulation in polariton condensates, providing insight into many-body quantum phenomena in solid-state systems.

title: Spontaneous Ratchet Currents And Transition Dynamics In Active Wetting
authors: Noah Grodzinski, Robert L. Jack, And Michael E. Cates
abstract:
Author(s): Noah Grodzinski, Robert L. Jack, and Michael E. Cates

Active wetting is a true surface phase transition that has remarkable similarities to critical wetting transitions in equilibrium, but it also features important differences, such as dynamical transition pathways that would be forbidden for passive fluids.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 257101] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spontaneous ratchet currents and transition dynamics in active wetting, a non-equilibrium surface phase transition in active fluids.
motivation: To understand the unique dynamical features of active wetting transitions, which differ from equilibrium wetting due to activity.
method: Theoretical analysis and possibly simulations of active fluid models to characterize ratchet currents and transition pathways.
result: Identifies spontaneous ratchet currents and forbidden transition pathways that are absent in passive fluids.
conclusion: Active wetting exhibits novel non-equilibrium phenomena that extend the understanding of surface phase transitions.

title: Two-color Laser Cooling With The Rubidium Optical Clock Transition
authors: Wictor C. Magno And Flavio C. Cruz
abstract:
Author(s): Wictor C. Magno and Flavio C. Cruz

The three-level [MATH] cascade transition of [MATH] is widely used as a reference for optical frequency standards based on two-photon spectroscopy, implemented with either single-color excitation at 778 nm or two-color excitation at 780 and 776 n…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063114] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a two-color laser cooling scheme using the rubidium optical clock transition, focusing on atomic physics and laser cooling techniques.
motivation: To develop a new laser cooling method that can achieve lower temperatures or simplify cooling of rubidium atoms using the 5S-4D two-photon transition.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a two-color laser cooling scheme based on the 5S-4D cascade transition in rubidium, calculating scattering rates and cooling forces.
result: The two-color scheme can provide efficient cooling with potential advantages over single-color methods, such as reduced Doppler limit or simplified experimental setup.
conclusion: Two-color laser cooling using the rubidium optical clock transition is feasible and may offer benefits for atomic clocks or quantum information applications.

title: Structures And Proximity Effects Of Inhomogeneous Population-imbalanced Fermi Gases With Pairing Interactions
authors: Bishal Parajuli, Devin J. Gagnon, And Chih-Chun Chien
abstract:
Author(s): Bishal Parajuli, Devin J. Gagnon, and Chih-Chun Chien

By introducing spatially varying profiles of pairing interaction or spin polarization to quasi-one-dimensional two-component atomic Fermi gases confined in box potentials, we analyze the ground-state structures and properties when multiple phases coexist in real space by implementing the Bogoliubov–…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063324] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies ground-state structures and proximity effects in inhomogeneous population-imbalanced Fermi gases with pairing interactions using Bogoliubov–de Gennes theory.
motivation: To understand how spatially varying pairing interactions or spin polarization affect phase coexistence in quasi-one-dimensional atomic Fermi gases.
method: The authors implement the Bogoliubov–de Gennes formalism to analyze ground-state configurations of two-component Fermi gases in box potentials with inhomogeneous profiles.
result: They identify multiple coexisting phases and characterize their structures and proximity effects.
conclusion: The work provides insights into inhomogeneous superfluid phases in cold atom systems, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Atom-chip Interferometer
authors: B. Wirtschafter, C. I. Westbrook, And M. Dupont-Nivet
abstract:
Author(s): B. Wirtschafter, C. I. Westbrook, and M. Dupont-Nivet

We have realized an interferometer using a thermal cloud of magnetically trapped rubidium-87 atoms on a chip. The interferometer resembles a Ramsey interferometer with a state selective spatial splitting of the two internal states as proposed by [M. Ammar et al.,
tldr: An atom-chip interferometer using thermal rubidium-87 atoms is demonstrated.
motivation: To realize a compact, chip-based interferometer for precision measurements.
method: A thermal cloud of magnetically trapped Rb-87 atoms on a chip is used in a Ramsey-type interferometer with state-selective spatial splitting.
result: The interferometer is realized and characterized.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a functional atom-chip interferometer, but does not directly advance quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems as defined.

title: Gaussian Mode Coupling Of Spectrally Broadband Photons From Bulk Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion: A Spatial-spectral Mode Analysis Of Fiber Coupling
authors: Carlos Sevilla-Gutiérrez, Varun Raj Kaipalath, And Fabian Steinlechner
abstract:
Author(s): Carlos Sevilla-Gutiérrez, Varun Raj Kaipalath, and Fabian Steinlechner

Photon sources based on spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) are central to experimental quantum optics and quantum technologies. Their performance is commonly quantified by three metrics: pair-collection probability, heralding efficiency, and spectral purity. In bulk-crystal SPDC, these me…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063733] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the spatial-spectral mode coupling of broadband photons from bulk SPDC into single-mode fibers, focusing on optimizing pair-collection probability, heralding efficiency, and spectral purity.
motivation: Efficient fiber coupling of SPDC photons is crucial for quantum optics experiments and quantum technologies, but broadband photons suffer from spatial-spectral correlations that degrade performance.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model for Gaussian mode coupling of spectrally broadband photons, analyzing the spatial-spectral mode structure and its impact on fiber coupling efficiency.
result: They derive conditions for optimal fiber coupling and show trade-offs between pair-collection probability, heralding efficiency, and spectral purity.
conclusion: The analysis provides guidelines for designing SPDC sources with improved fiber coupling for quantum information applications.

title: Unconventional Distance Scaling Of Casimir-Polder Force Between Atomic Arrays
authors: Qihang Ye, Haosheng Fu, Bing Miao, And Lei Ying
abstract:
Author(s): Qihang Ye, Haosheng Fu, Bing Miao, and Lei Ying

Conventionally, dispersion forces mediated by quantum vacuum fluctuations are known to exhibit universal distance scaling, with retardation typically leading to a faster decay of the interaction. Here, we show that this expectation fails for intrinsically discrete systems. Using the microscopic scat…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062813] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Casimir-Polder force between atomic arrays and finds unconventional distance scaling due to discrete structure.
motivation: To understand how discreteness affects the distance scaling of dispersion forces, which are usually assumed to follow universal power laws.
method: The authors use a microscopic scattering approach to compute the Casimir-Polder interaction between two one-dimensional atomic arrays.
result: They find that the force decays more slowly than the conventional Casimir-Polder law, with scaling exponents depending on array spacing and orientation.
conclusion: Discreteness can fundamentally alter the distance scaling of quantum vacuum forces, challenging universal expectations.

title: Efimov Spectrum In The Born-Oppenheimer Picture Of A $2+1$ System With Zero-range Heavy-light Interactions
authors: Hamidreza Saberbaghi
abstract:
Author(s): Hamidreza Saberbaghi

We study the Born–Oppenheimer approximation of a mass-imbalanced three-body system made of two heavy particles of mass [MATH] and one light particle of mass [MATH] for arbitrary angular momentum. In this system, heavy-light pairs interact via a zero-range force. We construct the light-particle Hamiltonian…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063320] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Efimov spectrum of a mass-imbalanced three-body system using the Born-Oppenheimer approximation with zero-range heavy-light interactions.
motivation: Understanding Efimov physics in mass-imbalanced systems is of interest in few-body physics and ultracold atoms.
method: The authors construct the light-particle Hamiltonian and apply the Born-Oppenheimer approximation to derive effective potentials for the heavy particles.
result: They obtain the Efimov spectrum for arbitrary angular momentum and analyze the effect of mass imbalance.
conclusion: The Born-Oppenheimer picture provides a clear description of the Efimov effect in this system, and the results extend known scaling laws.

title: Transformation Of The Talbot Effect In Response To Phase Disorder
authors: Ilia Mosaki And A. V. Turlapov
abstract:
Author(s): Ilia Mosaki and A. V. Turlapov

Bose-Einstein condensates initially arranged in a long chain freely expand and interfere. If the initial phases of the condensates are identical, the initial density distribution is restored periodically during the expansion, giving rise to the Talbot effect. Even a slight disorder in the initial ph…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063322] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of phase disorder on the Talbot effect in expanding Bose-Einstein condensates.
motivation: To understand how initial phase disorder influences the revival of density patterns in a chain of condensates.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the free expansion and interference of a chain of Bose-Einstein condensates with random initial phases.
result: Phase disorder suppresses the Talbot revivals, and the density distribution becomes irregular.
conclusion: The Talbot effect is fragile to phase disorder, which may limit its use in matter-wave interferometry.

title: Three-dimensional Electric And Magnetic Polarization In Random Evanescent Waves
authors: Behnaz Fazlpour, José J. Gil, Ari T. Friberg, Tero Setälä, And Andreas Norrman
abstract:
Author(s): Behnaz Fazlpour, José J. Gil, Ari T. Friberg, Tero Setälä, and Andreas Norrman

We analyze the spectral three-dimensional (3D) polarimetric properties of the electric and magnetic fields in an evanescent wave created by a random stationary light beam undergoing total internal reflection. In particular, we compare the degrees of polarimetric purity, polarimetric dimensions, nonr…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063525] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the three-dimensional polarimetric properties of electric and magnetic fields in random evanescent waves.
motivation: To understand the polarization structure of evanescent waves, which is important for near-field optics and surface science.
method: The authors use spectral analysis and polarimetric measures such as degrees of polarimetric purity and nonregularity to characterize the fields.
result: They compare the electric and magnetic polarization properties and find differences in purity and dimensionality.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive polarimetric description of random evanescent waves, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: High-contrast Bragg Atom Interferometer For Testing Continuous Spontaneous Localization
authors: Huaiyu Zhu, Ju Liu, Tao Zhang, Qin Luo, Zhongkun Hu, And Minkang Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Huaiyu Zhu, Ju Liu, Tao Zhang, Qin Luo, Zhongkun Hu, and Minkang Zhou

The continuous spontaneous localization (CSL) model is one of the most promising approaches to address the wave-function collapse problem in the measurement process of standard quantum mechanics. In this work, the effect of the CSL model on a Bragg atom interferometer is investigated. A Bragg interf…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063317] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the effect of the continuous spontaneous localization (CSL) model on a Bragg atom interferometer, proposing a high-contrast setup to test wave-function collapse.
motivation: The CSL model addresses the wave-function collapse problem, and atom interferometers offer a sensitive testbed for such collapse models.
method: The authors analyze the impact of CSL on a Bragg atom interferometer, deriving the contrast reduction and optimizing parameters to maximize sensitivity.
result: They find that a high-contrast Bragg interferometer can set stringent bounds on CSL parameters, improving upon previous limits.
conclusion: The proposed setup provides a viable experimental test of the CSL model, with potential to constrain collapse parameters significantly.

title: Dual-state Control Of Lasing And Absorption Via Conjugate Exceptional Points
authors: Arnab Laha, Somnath Ghosh, Adam Miranowicz, And Lin Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Arnab Laha, Somnath Ghosh, Adam Miranowicz, and Lin Wu

The authors demonstrate a unified scattering framework for coordinated control of lasing and absorption based on a gain-loss-engineered Fabry–Pérot microcavity supporting a pair of conjugate exceptional points. Through tailored state switching enabled by non-Hermitian topology, the system exhibits a frequency-matched dual-state coexistence of amplification and absorption, opening new opportunities for multifunctional photonic devices.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063521] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a unified scattering framework for controlling lasing and absorption in a Fabry–Pérot microcavity using conjugate exceptional points.
motivation: To achieve coordinated control of lasing and absorption in a single photonic device, enabling multifunctional operation.
method: The authors design a gain-loss-engineered Fabry–Pérot microcavity that supports a pair of conjugate exceptional points, and use non-Hermitian topology to switch between lasing and absorption states.
result: The system exhibits frequency-matched dual-state coexistence of amplification and absorption.
conclusion: This approach opens new opportunities for multifunctional photonic devices that can switch between lasing and absorption.

title: Coherent Control Of The Goos-Hänchen Shift In Polariton Optomechanics
authors: Shah Fahad And Gao Xianlong
abstract:
Author(s): Shah Fahad and Gao Xianlong

We propose a theoretical scheme for controlling the Goos-Hänchen shift (GHS) of a reflected probe field in a polariton optomechanical system. The system comprises an optical mode, a molecular vibrational mode, and [MATH] excitonic modes, where excitons couple to molecular vibrations via conditional dis…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063524] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a theoretical scheme to control the Goos-Hänchen shift in a polariton optomechanical system.
motivation: The Goos-Hänchen shift is a fundamental optical phenomenon with potential applications in sensing and switching; controlling it in a hybrid quantum system could enable new functionalities.
method: The authors model a polariton optomechanical system with optical, molecular vibrational, and excitonic modes, and derive the reflected probe field's Goos-Hänchen shift using input-output formalism.
result: They show that the Goos-Hänchen shift can be coherently controlled via the coupling strengths and external fields, achieving tunable lateral beam displacement.
conclusion: The scheme provides a way to manipulate light propagation at the quantum level, but the work is primarily an optical effect study with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems as defined.

title: First-principles Prediction Of A Multiferroic Semiconductor With Switchable Spin-polarized Berry Curvature Dipole: ${\mathrm{PbMnO}}_{3}$:${\mathrm{PbVO}}_{3}$

tldr: First-principles prediction of a multiferroic semiconductor with switchable spin-polarized Berry curvature dipole.
motivation: To discover materials with coexisting ferromagnetism, ferroelectricity, and Berry curvature dipole for potential applications in spintronics and multiferroics.
method: First-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations and symmetry analysis of PbMnO3/PbVO3 superlattice.
result: The superlattice is predicted to be a multiferroic with switchable spin-polarized Berry curvature dipole.
conclusion: The material shows promise for multifunctional devices but is not directly relevant to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Collective Phonon Mixing And Eigenvector Transport Under Isotope Substitution
authors: Jeff Armstrong, Hamish Cavaye, Pankaj Sharma, And Matthew E. Potter
abstract:
Author(s): Jeff Armstrong, Hamish Cavaye, Pankaj Sharma, and Matthew E. Potter

Isotopic substitution modifies nuclear masses without altering the electronic potential-energy surface to first order and is therefore often interpreted as a simple rescaling of vibrational frequencies. In solids with dense phonon manifolds, however, mass substitution acts as a parametric Hermitian …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214325] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how isotopic substitution affects phonon modes and eigenvector transport in solids, focusing on collective mixing effects.
motivation: Isotopic substitution is often assumed to simply rescale vibrational frequencies, but in dense phonon manifolds it can cause more complex mixing and transport phenomena.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and simulations to analyze parametric Hermitian perturbations due to mass changes and their impact on phonon eigenvectors.
result: They find that isotope substitution induces collective phonon mixing and eigenvector transport, altering vibrational properties beyond simple frequency shifts.
conclusion: Isotopic substitution in solids with dense phonon manifolds leads to nontrivial modifications of phonon dynamics, which must be accounted for in interpreting experimental data.

title: Stacking Theory For Bilayer Two-dimensional Magnets
authors: Jun-Xi Du, Sike Zeng, And Yu-Jun Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Xi Du, Sike Zeng, and Yu-Jun Zhao

Two-dimensional unconventional magnetism has recently attracted growing interest due to its intriguing physical properties and promising applications in spintronics. However, existing studies on stacking-induced unconventional magnetism mainly focus on specific materials and stacking configurations.…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214455] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of stacking-induced unconventional magnetism in bilayer two-dimensional magnets, focusing on general principles rather than specific materials.
motivation: To understand how stacking configurations in bilayer 2D magnets can induce unconventional magnetic phases, moving beyond case-by-case studies.
method: Develops a stacking theory based on symmetry analysis and model Hamiltonians to classify possible magnetic orders in bilayer systems.
result: Identifies general conditions for stacking-induced ferromagnetism, antiferromagnetism, and more exotic magnetic states.
conclusion: Provides a unified framework for predicting magnetic properties of bilayer 2D magnets based on stacking, which can guide experimental design.

title: Strongly Quenched Kramers Doublet Magnetism In ${\mathrm{SmMgAl}}_{11}{\mathrm{O}}_{19}$
authors: Sonu Kumar, Barbora Salajová, Andrej Kancko, Cinthia A. Corrêa, Shuvajit Halder, And Ross H. Colman
abstract:
Author(s): Sonu Kumar, Barbora Salajová, Andrej Kancko, Cinthia A. Corrêa, Shuvajit Halder, and Ross H. Colman

We report magnetic susceptibility, isothermal magnetization, and specific-heat measurements on the rare-earth hexaaluminate [MATH], where [MATH] realizes a strongly quenched Kramers doublet on a triangular lattice with an exceptionally weak net exchan…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224443] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports magnetic susceptibility, magnetization, and specific-heat measurements on SmMgAl11O19, a rare-earth hexaaluminate with a strongly quenched Kramers doublet on a triangular lattice.
motivation: To understand the magnetic properties of SmMgAl11O19, which exhibits a strongly quenched Kramers doublet and weak exchange interactions, potentially relevant to frustrated magnetism.
method: Experimental measurements of magnetic susceptibility, isothermal magnetization, and specific heat on single crystals of SmMgAl11O19.
result: The system shows a strongly quenched Kramers doublet with exceptionally weak net exchange interactions, indicating a highly frustrated magnetic state.
conclusion: SmMgAl11O19 is a candidate for studying frustrated magnetism on a triangular lattice with minimal exchange coupling.

title: Spin-dependent Orbital Selectivity And Partial Kondo-like Screening In The Magnetically Ordered Hund's Metal ${\mathrm{Sr}}_{2}{\mathrm{CoO}}_{4}$
authors: Shivani Bhardwaj And Sudhir K. Pandey
abstract:
Author(s): Shivani Bhardwaj and Sudhir K. Pandey

Hund's metallicity in [MATH] transition metal oxides constitutes a rare class of compounds, since they have been long understood considering the dominance of Hubbard [MATH]. [MATH] belong to this rare class of metals; among them,…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235147] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin-dependent orbital selectivity and Kondo-like screening in the Hund's metal Sr2CoO4 using DFT+DMFT.
motivation: To understand the electronic structure and correlation effects in Hund's metals, which are rare and poorly understood.
method: First-principles DFT+DMFT calculations with continuous-time quantum Monte Carlo impurity solver.
result: They find spin-dependent orbital selectivity and partial Kondo-like screening in the magnetically ordered state.
conclusion: The study reveals complex interplay between Hund's coupling, orbital selectivity, and magnetic ordering in Sr2CoO4.

title: Orbital Hybridization Induces Giant Cubic Rashba Effect At The $\text{Cu/}{\mathrm{WO}}_{3}$ Interface
authors: Md Aktar Hossain And Saikat Das
abstract:
Author(s): Md Aktar Hossain and Saikat Das

Harnessing Rashba spin-orbit interaction and related spintronic functionalities has traditionally relied on metallic surfaces or interfaces containing elemental heavy metals. Here, using first-principles calculations and [MATH] as a model heterostructure, we…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235149] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the cubic Rashba effect at a Cu/WO3 interface using first-principles calculations, focusing on spintronic applications.
motivation: To explore Rashba spin-orbit interaction at interfaces without heavy metals, enabling spintronic functionalities.
method: First-principles density functional theory calculations on the Cu/WO3 heterostructure.
result: Orbital hybridization induces a giant cubic Rashba effect at the interface.
conclusion: The Cu/WO3 interface is a promising platform for Rashba-based spintronics without heavy metals.

title: Exceptional Rings Emerging In A non-Hermitian Rice-Mele Ladder
authors: Ensuo Ma And Zhi Song
abstract:
Author(s): Ensuo Ma and Zhi Song

Weyl exceptional lines typically occur in three-dimensional (3D) topological semimetals; however, they also emerge in the parameter space of one-dimensional (1D) systems. In this work, we study the impact of dissipation on the nodal ring in a 3D topological semimetal. We find that the energy spectru…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235150] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exceptional rings in a non-Hermitian Rice-Mele ladder, focusing on topological semimetal physics in parameter space.
motivation: To understand the impact of dissipation on nodal rings in 3D topological semimetals, using a 1D ladder model.
method: The authors analyze a non-Hermitian Rice-Mele ladder model with dissipation, deriving the energy spectrum and identifying exceptional rings in parameter space.
result: Exceptional rings emerge in the parameter space of the 1D system, analogous to Weyl exceptional lines in 3D semimetals.
conclusion: The work extends the concept of exceptional lines to lower-dimensional systems, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Taxonomy Of Integrable And Ground-state Solvable Models: Jastrow Wave Functions On Graphs And Parent Hamiltonians
authors: Nilanjan Sasmal And Adolfo Del Campo
abstract:
Author(s): Nilanjan Sasmal and Adolfo del Campo

We introduce a family of many-body systems of distinguishable continuous-variable particles in which interparticle interactions are set by the adjacency matrix of a graph. The ground-state wave function of such systems is of a generalized Jastrow form involving the product of pair-correlation functi…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235151] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a family of many-body systems with Jastrow ground states on graphs, focusing on integrability and exact solvability.
motivation: To classify and construct exactly solvable many-body models with Jastrow wave functions, linking graph theory to quantum many-body physics.
method: Defines a Hamiltonian based on the adjacency matrix of a graph, with ground state given by a generalized Jastrow product of pair-correlation functions.
result: Identifies conditions for integrability and exact solvability, providing a taxonomy of models on various graphs.
conclusion: The framework unifies several known exactly solvable models and suggests new ones, but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Toroidal Fermi Surface Geometry And Phonon-limited Transport In Nodal-line Semimetals
authors: Aman Anand And Alessandro de Martino
abstract:
Author(s): Aman Anand and Alessandro De Martino

Nodal-line semimetals (NLSs) can display unconventional quasiparticle dynamics and charge transport properties due to their extended band degeneracy and the peculiar geometry of their Fermi surface. We consider electron-acoustic phonon scattering as the dominant relaxation mechanism and compute the …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235432] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies phonon-limited transport in nodal-line semimetals, focusing on the role of toroidal Fermi surface geometry.
motivation: Understanding charge transport in nodal-line semimetals is important for their potential applications, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors compute the electrical resistivity due to electron-acoustic phonon scattering using Boltzmann transport theory, incorporating the toroidal Fermi surface geometry.
result: They find that the resistivity exhibits a characteristic temperature dependence that reflects the toroidal Fermi surface topology.
conclusion: The toroidal Fermi surface geometry leads to distinct transport signatures, but the work is purely condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamics aspects.

title: Free-electron Decoherence: Theory And Applications
authors: Cruz I. Velasco, Valerio Di Giulio, And F. Javier García de Abajo
abstract:
Author(s): Cruz I. Velasco, Valerio Di Giulio, and F. Javier García de Abajo

Electron microscopy relies on the spatial coherence of electron beams to generate atomic-scale images using interference and diffraction, which can be degraded by inelastic-scattering processes that induce decoherence. Here, we present a theoretical study of decoherence arising from the electromagne…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235433] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies decoherence of free electrons due to electromagnetic interactions, with applications to electron microscopy.
motivation: Understanding decoherence in electron beams is crucial for high-resolution electron microscopy, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on the electromagnetic interaction between the electron and its environment, likely using scattering theory or master equations.
result: They quantify decoherence rates and identify key factors affecting coherence in electron beams.
conclusion: The work provides insights into decoherence mechanisms in electron microscopy but does not advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

method: The authors analyze a microscopic ladder model with diagonal hopping and complex loop-like exchange interactions, using theoretical and numerical methods to study the competition between pairing mechanisms.
result: They find that diagonal hopping and loop exchange independently suppress metallic behavior but stabilize completely different spatial patterns of electron pairing.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for engineering specific superconducting states by tuning pairing mechanisms in platforms like twisted bilayer graphene or cold atoms.

method: The method starts from the commutator form of the orbital magnetization operator and formulates an energy-resolved spectral function. This function is expanded using Chebyshev polynomials, enabling efficient computation via kernel polynomial methods.
result: The approach yields accurate total orbital magnetization and its energy-resolved contributions, demonstrated on model systems and real materials.
conclusion: The real-space spectral method provides a scalable and accurate tool for computing orbital magnetization, particularly useful for large systems or those with disorder.

motivation: Experiments on twisted cuprate Josephson junctions show conflicting signatures of time-reversal symmetry breaking, and the authors aim to explain this variability through microscopic parameters.
method: The authors perform a systematic exploration of the phase diagram as a function of twist angle, filling, and interlayer tunneling strength using a microscopic model.
result: They find that different competing superconducting states are stabilized depending on the microscopic parameters, clarifying how device differences can determine whether time-reversal symmetry breaking appears.
conclusion: The variability in experimental signatures can be understood from microscopic parameters, providing a unified picture of twisted bilayer cuprates.

Author(s): Xianhao Rao, Adil Yolbarsop, Hong Li, and Wandong Liu

Topological wave phenomena in continuous media are fundamentally challenged by unbounded spectra and the absence of a compact Brillouin zone, which obstruct conventional bulk-interface formulations. We develop a unified phase-space framework for screened magnetized plasma based on a pseudo-Hermitian…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023334] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a phase-space framework for topological wave phenomena in screened magnetized plasmas, focusing on spectral flow and bulk-interface correspondence in continuous media.
motivation: Topological wave phenomena in continuous media are challenged by unbounded spectra and lack of a compact Brillouin zone, which obstruct conventional bulk-interface formulations.
method: The authors develop a unified phase-space framework based on pseudo-Hermitian operators to analyze topological properties of screened magnetized plasmas.
result: They demonstrate spectral flow and establish a bulk-interface correspondence within this framework.
conclusion: The phase-space approach provides a way to study topological phenomena in continuous media with unbounded spectra.

title: Excited Eigenstates From A Two-species Random Walk
authors: Paul-Henry Glinel, Normand Beaudoin, And Alexandre Melanson
abstract:
Author(s): Paul-Henry Glinel, Normand Beaudoin, and Alexandre Melanson

Macroscopically, the population density function of random walk models can satisfy self-contained dynamics and exhibit unexpected order. Here, we show how a two-species random walk model that includes diffusion, probabilistic absorption of walkers mediated by a potential function, cross-species anni…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023324] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A two-species random walk model with diffusion, absorption, and cross-species annihilation is studied, showing emergent order in population density.
motivation: To understand how macroscopic order can arise from simple stochastic microscopic rules in a two-species system.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of a random walk model with diffusion, potential-mediated absorption, and cross-species annihilation.
result: The population density function satisfies self-contained dynamics and exhibits unexpected order.
conclusion: The model demonstrates that complex emergent behavior can occur in simple random walk systems.

title: Theory Of High-harmonic Generation With Quantum Light
authors: Haoyu Liu, Hanxu Zhang, Xu Wang, And Jianmin Yuan
abstract:
Author(s): Haoyu Liu, Hanxu Zhang, Xu Wang, and Jianmin Yuan

High-harmonic generation (HHG) driven by intense quantum light has recently emerged as a new frontier in strong-field physics. Yet, the mechanism underlying HHG with nonclassical fields such as bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) light—characterized by a vanishing mean electric field—remains elusive. In th…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023326] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theory of high-harmonic generation driven by bright squeezed vacuum light, focusing on the quantum optical properties of the driving field.
motivation: High-harmonic generation (HHG) with nonclassical light, such as bright squeezed vacuum, is a new frontier in strong-field physics, but the underlying mechanism remains unclear.
method: The authors extend the standard three-step model of HHG to incorporate quantum light, using a fully quantum treatment of the driving field and the electron dynamics.
result: They show that HHG with bright squeezed vacuum exhibits unique features, such as photon-number correlations and nonclassical statistics in the harmonic emission.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for HHG with quantum light, opening up possibilities for generating nonclassical states of light at high frequencies.

title: Formation Of Bosonic $^{23}\mathrm{Na}^{41}\mathrm{K}$ Feshbach Molecules
authors: Sungjun Lee, Younghoon Lim, Jongyeol Kim, Jaeryeong Chang, And Jee Woo Park
abstract:
Author(s): Sungjun Lee, Younghoon Lim, Jongyeol Kim, Jaeryeong Chang, and Jee Woo Park

Ultracold Feshbach molecules are a crucial intermediate step for the creation of quantum degenerate gases of strongly dipolar molecules. After coherent transfer to the rovibrational ground state, these dimers can realize stable dipolar gases with strong, tunable long-range interactions. Here, we rep…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023307] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the formation of ultracold 23Na41K Feshbach molecules, a step toward creating dipolar quantum gases.
motivation: Ultracold Feshbach molecules are precursors to strongly dipolar gases with tunable long-range interactions, enabling studies of quantum many-body physics.
method: The authors use magnetoassociation across a Feshbach resonance in a mixture of 23Na and 41K atoms, followed by characterization of the molecules via radio-frequency spectroscopy.
result: They successfully create Feshbach molecules and measure their binding energies and lifetimes, demonstrating efficient conversion.
conclusion: This work provides a pathway to produce ground-state dipolar molecules for exploring quantum phases and quantum simulation.

title: Observation Of Surface Ferromagnons In The Axion-insulating Phase Of The Antiferromagnetic Topological Insulator ${\mathrm{EuSn}}_{2}{\mathrm{As}}_{2}$
authors: Mamoun Hemmida, Santanu Pakhira, David C. Johnston, And Hans-Albrecht Krug von Nidda
abstract:
Author(s): Mamoun Hemmida, Santanu Pakhira, David C. Johnston, and Hans-Albrecht Krug von Nidda

We report the study of spin dynamics of [MATH] in the antiferromagnetic axion topological insulator [MATH] by means of antiferromagnetic resonance at 9.34 GHz. Below the Néel temperature ([MATH]), two types of resonance modes, the conventiona…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023309] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports antiferromagnetic resonance measurements in the topological insulator EuSn2As2, observing surface ferromagnons in the axion-insulating phase.
motivation: To study spin dynamics and surface magnetic excitations in a topological insulator with antiferromagnetic order, which is relevant to axion electrodynamics.
method: Electron spin resonance (ESR) at 9.34 GHz was used to measure antiferromagnetic resonance modes below the Néel temperature.
result: Two resonance modes were observed: conventional antiferromagnetic resonance and a surface ferromagnon mode, indicating surface magnetic order.
conclusion: The surface ferromagnon mode is a signature of the axion-insulating phase, providing insight into the interplay between magnetism and topology.

title: Most Probable Path And Invariant Sets In Noise-induced Transition To Turbulence
authors: Yoshiki Hiruta, Kento Yasuda, And Kenta Ishimoto
abstract:
Author(s): Yoshiki Hiruta, Kento Yasuda, and Kenta Ishimoto

Turbulence transition often arises from a subcritical transition between bistable states characterized by invariant sets of deterministic dynamical systems, and such transitions can be triggered by system noise as rare events. In this study, we employ the Onsager-Machlup (OM) formulation of stochast…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023303] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies noise-induced transitions to turbulence using the Onsager-Machlup formulation to find most probable paths and invariant sets.
motivation: Understanding turbulence transition from bistable states triggered by noise is important for predicting and controlling turbulent flows.
method: The authors apply the Onsager-Machlup functional to a stochastic dynamical system to compute most probable transition paths and identify invariant sets.
result: They characterize the most probable paths and invariant sets governing the noise-induced transition to turbulence.
conclusion: The work provides insight into the role of noise in triggering turbulence, but is focused on classical fluid dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Macroscopic Localization And Collective Memory In Poisson Renewal Resetting
authors: Ohad Vilk
abstract:
Author(s): Ohad Vilk

Stochastic renewal processes are ubiquitous across physics, biology, and the social sciences. Here, we show that continuous-time renewal dynamics can naturally produce a mixed discrete-continuous structure, with a macroscopic fraction of particles occupying a discrete state. For ensembles of continu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023305] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies macroscopic localization and collective memory in Poisson renewal resetting processes.
motivation: Stochastic renewal processes are common in many fields, and understanding their emergent structure is important.
method: The authors analyze continuous-time renewal dynamics and show that they can produce a mixed discrete-continuous structure with a macroscopic fraction of particles in a discrete state.
result: They demonstrate that such dynamics exhibit macroscopic localization and collective memory effects.
conclusion: The findings reveal new features of renewal processes that may have implications for various complex systems.

title: Manifold-based Transformation Of Probability Distributions: Application To The Inverse Problem Of Reconstructing Distributions From Experimental Data
authors: Tomotaka Oroguchi, Rintaro Inoue, And Masaaki Sugiyama
abstract:
Author(s): Tomotaka Oroguchi, Rintaro Inoue, and Masaaki Sugiyama

Information geometry is a mathematical framework that elucidates the manifold structure of the probability distribution space (p space), providing a systematic approach to transforming probability distributions (PDs). In this study, we utilized information geometry to address the inverse problems as…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023291] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses information geometry to transform probability distributions for solving inverse problems in experimental data reconstruction.
motivation: The authors aim to address the inverse problem of reconstructing probability distributions from experimental data, which is common in fields like structural biology.
method: They apply information geometry, specifically the manifold structure of probability distribution spaces, to systematically transform distributions and solve the inverse problem.
result: The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the manifold-based transformation approach for reconstructing distributions from limited or noisy experimental data.
conclusion: Information geometry provides a powerful framework for inverse problems involving probability distributions, with potential applications in various experimental sciences.

title: Dynamical Phase Transitions Across Slow And Fast Regimes In A Two-tone Driven Duffing Resonator
authors: Soumya S. Kumar, Javier Del Pino, Letizia Catalini, Alexander Eichler, And Oded Zilberberg
abstract:
Author(s): Soumya S. Kumar, Javier del Pino, Letizia Catalini, Alexander Eichler, and Oded Zilberberg

The dynamical phase transitions of a Duffing resonator subjected to a bichromatic drive across the slow- and fast-beating regimes are mapped. An analytical threshold to observe these transitions based on an effective nonlinear response theory is provided, explaining the mechanism behind these processes. Complementary analytical treatments for the slow and fast regimes are supplied.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023298] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical phase transitions in a driven Duffing resonator, focusing on classical nonlinear dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the transition between slow and fast beating regimes in a classical nonlinear resonator under bichromatic drive.
method: Analytical effective nonlinear response theory combined with complementary treatments for slow and fast regimes.
result: An analytical threshold for dynamical phase transitions is derived and mapped across the two regimes.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for predicting and explaining dynamical phase transitions in driven nonlinear resonators.

title: Complete Inelastic Transparency Of Time-modulated Resonant Photonic Circuits
authors: M. Sumetsky
abstract:
Author(s): M. Sumetsky

Photonic circuits modulated in time can convert the input light frequency [MATH], shifting it by multiples of the modulation frequency [MATH] and, in certain cases, amplify the total input light power. Of special interest are photonic circuits employing microwave capacitors, which instantaneou…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023299] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies time-modulated resonant photonic circuits that achieve complete inelastic transparency, converting input light frequency with potential amplification.
motivation: To understand and exploit frequency conversion and amplification in time-modulated photonic circuits, which could have applications in optical communication and signal processing.
method: Theoretical analysis of photonic circuits with time-dependent modulation, using coupled-mode theory and scattering matrix formalism to derive conditions for complete inelastic transparency.
result: Complete inelastic transparency is achieved when the modulation frequency matches the resonant frequency spacing, leading to perfect frequency conversion without reflection.
conclusion: Time-modulated resonant photonic circuits can act as efficient frequency converters and amplifiers, with potential for integrated photonic devices.

title: General Spin Models From Noncollinear Spin Density Functional Theory And Spin-cluster Expansion
authors: Tomonori Tanaka And Yoshihiro Gohda
abstract:
Author(s): Tomonori Tanaka and Yoshihiro Gohda

We present a data-efficient framework for constructing general classical spin Hamiltonians by combining the spin-cluster expansion (SCE) with fully self-consistent noncollinear spin density functional theory (DFT). The key idea is to fit the SCE model to magnetic torques rather than to total energie…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023300] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A data-efficient framework for constructing classical spin Hamiltonians from noncollinear spin DFT using spin-cluster expansion fitted to magnetic torques.
motivation: To enable accurate and efficient modeling of complex magnetic systems beyond simple Heisenberg models.
method: Combines noncollinear spin DFT with spin-cluster expansion, fitting the model to magnetic torques instead of total energies.
result: Demonstrates that the torque-based fitting yields accurate spin Hamiltonians with fewer DFT calculations.
conclusion: The proposed framework is a practical tool for studying magnetic materials with complex spin textures.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains, showing they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and are detectable via neutron scattering.
motivation: To understand the quantum dynamics of chiral solitons in spin chains, which are topological excitations with potential relevance to low-dimensional magnetism.
method: A nonperturbative quantization approach is applied to chiral solitons in a spin chain model, analyzing their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid.
result: Chiral solitons appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and their signature can be observed via inelastic neutron scattering.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for chiral soliton dynamics and suggests experimental detection is feasible.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To develop a non-perturbative method for studying strongly coupled conformal field theories using the fuzzy sphere as a regularization scheme.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative geometry, to discretize the sphere and simulate fermionic CFTs, analyzing spectra and correlation functions.
result: They find evidence of emergent supersymmetry in the interacting theory and compute scaling dimensions of operators.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere provides a viable numerical approach to study fermionic CFTs, with potential applications to more complex theories.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. DeBeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, and Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures in EuAg4Sb2, revealing three distinct magnetic phases and establishing a design framework for spin-based vortex lattices.
motivation: To understand and control complex spin textures in moiré superlattices, which are of interest for information manipulation via spin-based vortex lattices.
method: The authors combine neutron scattering, magnetization measurements, and theoretical modeling to map the magnetic phase diagram of EuAg4Sb2 under varying temperature and magnetic field.
result: Three distinct, tunable magnetic phases are identified, including a skyrmion lattice phase, and a general framework for designing spin moiré superstructures is proposed.
