method: The authors develop amalgam-type characterizations and apply them to convergence, absolute continuity of norm, and almost-compact embeddings, also treating rearrangement-invariant spaces.
result: They obtain conditions for compactness formulated in terms of non-increasing rearrangement and representation space.
conclusion: The amalgam approach yields a unified framework for compactness in quasi-Banach function spaces.

title: OAMP-Aided Joint Channel Estimation And Data Detection For Oddm Systems
authors: Kehan Huang, Min Qiu, Akram Shafie, Jinhong Yuan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, to address the challenge of joint channel estimation and data detection (JED) for orthogonal delay-Doppler (DD) division multiplexing (ODDM) in doubly selective channels, we propose an orthogonal approximate message passing (OAMP)-aided JED (OAMP-JED) receiver. We first formulate a bilinear cross-domain JED model, which can be linearized into separate channel estimation and data detection subproblems. The proposed OAMP-JED receiver alternately executes two OAMP modules for these subproblems, effectively coupled through a variational noise term to account for model uncertainty. Leveraging OAMP's error orthogonality, we derive closed-form scalar-variance updates to enable efficient and principled soft information exchange between the modules, thereby mitigating error propagation during JED. Simulation results show that, for both uncoded and coded ODDM, OAMP-JED achieves a lower bit error rate (BER) than benchmark schemes. Moreover, its BER performance closely approaches that of OAMP with perfect CSI.
tags: joint channel estimation and data detection
tldr: This paper proposes an OAMP-based receiver for joint channel estimation and data detection in ODDM systems, focusing on communication engineering rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Joint channel estimation and data detection in doubly selective channels is challenging for ODDM systems, and existing methods suffer from error propagation.
method: A bilinear cross-domain JED model is linearized into separate subproblems, and two OAMP modules are alternately executed with closed-form scalar-variance updates for soft information exchange.
result: The proposed OAMP-JED receiver achieves lower BER than benchmark schemes and approaches the performance of OAMP with perfect CSI.
conclusion: OAMP-JED effectively mitigates error propagation and provides efficient joint estimation and detection for ODDM systems.
keywords: joint channel estimation and data detection

title: Boundedness Of $p$-adic Hardy--Hilbert And Erd\'elyi--Kober Fractional Integral Operators On $p$-adic Ces\`aro Function Spaces
authors: Rishabh Saini, Qaiser Jahan, Salman Ashraf
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce Ces\`aro function spaces over [MATH]-adic fields and investigate their fundamental properties, such as the dilation operator and the Minkowski-type integral inequality. We establish boundedness result for [MATH]-adic Hardy--Hilbert-type integral operators acting on [MATH]-adic Ces\`aro function spaces, and as an application we derive [MATH]-adic analogue of the Hardy inequality, the Hilbert inequality, and the Hardy-Littlewood-P\'{o}lya inequality. Furthermore, we define the [MATH]-adic analogue of the Erd\'elyi--Kober fractional integral operators and prove their boundedness on [MATH]-adic Ces\`aro function spaces with the help of the obtained boundedness result.
tldr: This paper studies boundedness of p-adic Hardy-Hilbert and Erdélyi-Kober fractional integral operators on p-adic Cesàro function spaces, which is a topic in p-adic harmonic analysis and functional analysis.
motivation: To extend classical inequalities and operator theory to the p-adic setting, which has applications in number theory and p-adic analysis.
method: Introduces Cesàro function spaces over p-adic fields, studies their properties, and proves boundedness of integral operators using Minkowski-type inequalities.
result: Establishes boundedness results for p-adic Hardy-Hilbert-type operators and p-adic Erdélyi-Kober fractional integral operators on these spaces, deriving p-adic analogues of classical inequalities.
conclusion: The work contributes to p-adic analysis but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Abstract Orlicz-Morrey Spaces And Applications
authors: J. Zhou F. Shan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25455v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work introduces a class of abstract Orlicz-Morrey spaces endowed with a ball-basis on general measure spaces and defines the associated concept of \(\Psi\)-bounded oscillation operators. Within this framework, we establish pointwise estimates and norm inequalities for these operators via sparse domination techniques. As applications, we verify that this class of \(\Psi\)-bounded oscillation operators includes maximal operators and Carleson-type operators on general measure spaces, as well as \(\omega\)-Calder\'on-Zygmund operators and intrinsic square operators on \(^n\), thus providing a generalization of certain classical Orlicz-Morrey spaces and their associated operator theory.
tldr: This paper introduces abstract Orlicz-Morrey spaces and establishes norm inequalities for Ψ-bounded oscillation operators via sparse domination.
motivation: To generalize classical Orlicz-Morrey spaces and operator theory to general measure spaces.
method: Defines abstract Orlicz-Morrey spaces with a ball-basis and Ψ-bounded oscillation operators, then uses sparse domination techniques to derive pointwise estimates and norm inequalities.
result: The class of Ψ-bounded oscillation operators includes maximal operators, Carleson-type operators, ω-Calderón-Zygmund operators, and intrinsic square operators.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for operator theory on general measure spaces, extending classical results.

title: Kontsevich Graphs Associated With Specific Multiple Zeta Values
authors: Kota Baba
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The primary aim of this paper is to provide an explicit construction of Kontsevich graphs whose integrals give certain multiple zeta values. Furthermore, by using this construction, we explicitly determine the weights of [MATH]-linear combinations of graphs whose integrals yield normalized multiple zeta values of a given weight. The methods employed in this paper are based on those introduced by Ritland, and our results provide a refinement of his results.
tldr: This paper constructs Kontsevich graphs whose integrals yield multiple zeta values, a topic in pure mathematics.
motivation: To provide explicit constructions of Kontsevich graphs for multiple zeta values and refine previous results.
method: Uses methods introduced by Ritland to construct graphs and determine weights of linear combinations.
result: Explicitly constructs Kontsevich graphs for normalized multiple zeta values of given weight.
conclusion: The work refines Ritland's results and provides a systematic construction for these graphs.

title: Equilibrium Singular Dividend Control Under Ambiguity Aggregation Of Heterogeneous Discount Rates
authors: Yue Cao, Guohui Guan, Zongxia Liang, Xiaodong Luo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25461v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies a singular dividend control problem for a firm with heterogeneous shareholders whose discount rates follow a given distribution. The central planner aggregates expected discounted payoffs using an ambiguity aggregation function [MATH], which captures shareholder heterogeneity and ambiguity attitudes but also leads to time inconsistency. To address this issue, we seek a time-homogeneous equilibrium dividend law characterized by a partition of the state space into waiting and dividend-paying regions. We provide a rigorous mathematical characterization by proving a verification theorem and deriving necessary conditions for the equilibrium law. We then analyze barrier-type equilibria, showing non-existence for a class of aggregation functions that includes power-type and logarithmic aggregation functions, and establishing existence and uniqueness under linear and exponential aggregation. In the linear case, the bounded-rate equilibrium is shown to converge to the singular barrier-type equilibrium as the dividend rate bound tends to infinity. Numerical examples illustrate the effects of discount-rate heterogeneity and ambiguity aversion on the equilibrium barrier.
tldr: This paper studies a singular dividend control problem with heterogeneous discount rates and ambiguity aggregation, unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: The authors aim to model dividend distribution for a firm with heterogeneous shareholders whose discount rates vary, incorporating ambiguity attitudes via an aggregation function.
method: They formulate a time-inconsistent stochastic control problem and seek a time-homogeneous equilibrium dividend law using a verification theorem and necessary conditions.
result: They characterize barrier-type equilibria, show non-existence for power/logarithmic aggregation, and prove existence/uniqueness for linear/exponential aggregation.
conclusion: The equilibrium barrier depends on discount-rate heterogeneity and ambiguity aversion, with linear aggregation converging to singular barrier-type equilibrium as the dividend rate bound tends to infinity.

title: A Krieger Embedding Theorem For Near Markov Sofic Shifts
authors: Brian Marcus, Tom Meyerovitch, Chengyu Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Krieger's classical embedding theorem gives necessary and sufficient conditions for embedding a subshift into a mixing shift of finite type (SFT) as a proper subshift. The same result does not hold if one replaces mixing SFT by a mixing sofic shift. In this paper, we generalize Krieger's conditions to give necessary and sufficient conditions for embedding a subshift into a mixing (in fact irreducible) near Markov sofic shift (a special conjugacy-invariant class of sofic shifts). We also show that if the subshift to be embedded is irreducible sofic, then the conditions are finitely decidable.
tldr: This paper generalizes Krieger's embedding theorem to near Markov sofic shifts, providing necessary and sufficient conditions for embedding a subshift into a mixing near Markov sofic shift.
motivation: Krieger's classical embedding theorem for mixing SFTs does not extend to mixing sofic shifts; the authors aim to find analogous conditions for a broader class of sofic shifts.
method: The authors introduce near Markov sofic shifts, a conjugacy-invariant class, and derive embedding conditions using symbolic dynamics and topological entropy.
result: Necessary and sufficient conditions for embedding a subshift into a mixing (irreducible) near Markov sofic shift are established; for irreducible sofic subshifts, the conditions are finitely decidable.
conclusion: The work extends Krieger's theorem to a wider class of shifts, contributing to symbolic dynamics and topological entropy theory.

title: Towards Analysis-aware Geometry Defeaturing For Inception Voltage Predictions
authors: Ondine Chanon
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25482v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Defeaturing is routinely employed in numerical simulations of medium- and high-voltage equipment, not only to reduce computational costs but also to make meshing possible. But the errors that this practice introduces in the predicted breakdown/inception voltages are currently neglected. This work presents a goal-oriented error estimation framework that aims at assessing such defeaturing errors in inception voltage computations. The methodology combines a first-order approximation of the inception voltage error with dual-weighted residual estimators, providing an error bound that quantifies the impact of defeaturing on the simulation results. The approach builds upon the streamer integral model for inception voltage prediction and uses the recently proposed certified goal-oriented analysis-aware defeaturing estimator of~[1] for elliptic PDEs. The first-order approximation of the inception voltage is a linear functional J of the background electric field whose definition involves a line integral along the critical field line, and is therefore only of low regularity. To meet the abstract regularity assumption of the goal-oriented theory, we introduce a Gaussian mollification of J. The methodology is illustrated on a pin-plate benchmark with a small protrusion of varying size and shape, using a single shared adaptive mesh and an adaptive coupling of the mollification width to the local mesh size in order to ensure that the defeaturing error dominates over the discretization and the regularization errors.
tldr: This paper presents a goal-oriented error estimation framework for assessing defeaturing errors in inception voltage predictions for high-voltage equipment.
motivation: Defeaturing is commonly used in numerical simulations of high-voltage equipment to reduce computational cost, but the errors introduced in predicted breakdown voltages are currently neglected.
method: The methodology combines a first-order approximation of the inception voltage error with dual-weighted residual estimators, using a Gaussian mollification to meet regularity assumptions.
result: The approach provides an error bound quantifying the impact of defeaturing on inception voltage simulations, demonstrated on a pin-plate benchmark with a small protrusion.
conclusion: The framework enables analysis-aware defeaturing for inception voltage predictions, ensuring that defeaturing errors dominate over discretization and regularization errors.

title: Generalized Convexity Of Spectral Functions On Euclidean Jordan Algebras
authors: Juyoung Jeong
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates transfer principles for generalized convexity of spectral functions on Euclidean Jordan algebras. A spectral function is induced by the eigenvalue map and an underlying symmetric function on a symmetric subset of [MATH]. We establish transfer principles for several generalized convexity notions, such as (strict/semistrict) quasiconvexity and (strict) pseudoconvexity, together with their strong variants, by showing that these properties are preserved in both directions between a spectral function and its associated symmetric function. These results extend the transfer principles for (strict) convexity and provide a unified framework for generalized convexity in the setting of Euclidean Jordan algebras.
tldr: The paper studies generalized convexity of spectral functions on Euclidean Jordan algebras, a topic in pure mathematics.
motivation: To extend transfer principles for generalized convexity from symmetric functions to spectral functions on Euclidean Jordan algebras.
method: The authors prove that properties like quasiconvexity and pseudoconvexity are preserved between a spectral function and its associated symmetric function.
result: Transfer principles for strict/semistrict quasiconvexity and strict pseudoconvexity are established, generalizing known results for convexity.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for generalized convexity in the setting of Euclidean Jordan algebras.

title: Efficient Krylov Solvers For Inverse Source Problem In 2d Space-time Fractional Diffusion Equation
authors: Stefano Serra-Capizzano Asim Ilyas
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we consider a two-dimensional time-space fractional diffusion equation with a variable coefficient and investigate the inverse source problem of reconstructing the source term f(x,y) , after regularizing the problem using the quasi-boundary value method to mitigate ill-posedness. A finite difference discretization results in a large-scale linear system with a multilevel Toeplitz-like block structure. We perform a spectral analysis of the associated matrix sequences, employing tools from Generalized Locally Toeplitz (GLT) theory, and construct efficient preconditioners based on the GLT analysis. The proposed preconditioners preserve the multilevel structure of the discretization matrices and leads to a general eigenvalue clustering around one for the preconditioned sequence. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical findings and demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly accelerates the convergence of the GMRES method in reconstructing the source term in the two-dimensional space-time fractional diffusion equation.
tldr: This paper develops efficient Krylov solvers for an inverse source problem in a 2D space-time fractional diffusion equation, using GLT theory for preconditioning.
motivation: Inverse source problems in fractional diffusion equations are ill-posed and computationally demanding; efficient solvers are needed for practical reconstruction.
method: The problem is regularized via quasi-boundary value method, discretized with finite differences yielding multilevel Toeplitz-like systems, and preconditioners are designed using Generalized Locally Toeplitz (GLT) spectral analysis.
result: The preconditioners cluster eigenvalues around one, significantly accelerating GMRES convergence in numerical experiments.
conclusion: The proposed GLT-based preconditioners are effective for solving the inverse source problem in space-time fractional diffusion equations.

title: Two-sample Test With Wasserstein Distance On Gaussian Samples Based On A Log-normal Approximation
authors: Johann Cl\'ement-Cottuz (UNIROUEN, LITIS, LITIS - App), Maxime B\'erar (UNIROUEN, LITIS, LITIS - App), Gilles Gasso
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25521v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we propose a two-sample test based on the Wasserstein 2-distance between two 1D samples, where the first sample is assumed to be Gaussian based on an approximation of the underlying distribution by a log-normal distribution. A two-sample test is performed to decide whether two samples are drawn from the same distribution or not. We evaluate the proposed method on synthetic data and extend it to the multivariate case. We also show that this test is closely related to the Shapiro-Wilk normality test.
tldr: This paper proposes a two-sample test using Wasserstein distance with a log-normal approximation for Gaussian samples.
motivation: To develop a statistical test for comparing two samples, assuming one is Gaussian and approximating the other by a log-normal distribution.
method: The test uses the Wasserstein-2 distance between 1D samples and extends to multivariate cases; it is related to the Shapiro-Wilk normality test.
result: The method is evaluated on synthetic data and shown to be effective for two-sample testing.
conclusion: The proposed test provides a novel approach to two-sample testing with connections to normality tests.

title: A Path-Survival Analytical Framework For Scl Decoding Of Polar Code
authors: Xianbin Wang, Zhichao Liu, Yuan Li, Huazi Zhang, Jiajie Tong, Jun Wang, And Wen Tong
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A theoretical analysis of CRC-aided successive cancellation list (CA-SCL) decoding for polar codes remains an open problem, despite its widespread practical adoption. While low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes benefit from mature analytical tools, such as density evolution (DE), for predicting the performance of belief-propagation (BP) decoding, similar techniques are not directly applicable to CA-SCL decoding. This limitation stems from the complex path-pruning mechanism inherent in CA-SCL decoding. In this paper, we propose an analytical framework based on a novel path-survival model that captures the evolution of the correct path's rank during decoding. The proposed framework enables efficient prediction of CA-SCL decoding performance without requiring exhaustive list-specific Monte Carlo simulations. Extensive numerical evaluations demonstrate its effectiveness across a wide range of code lengths, code rates, list sizes, and channel models.
tldr: This paper proposes an analytical framework for predicting the performance of CRC-aided successive cancellation list decoding of polar codes.
motivation: Theoretical analysis of CA-SCL decoding for polar codes is an open problem, unlike LDPC codes which have mature analytical tools.
method: A path-survival model is introduced to capture the evolution of the correct path's rank during decoding, enabling performance prediction without exhaustive Monte Carlo simulations.
result: The framework effectively predicts CA-SCL decoding performance across various code lengths, rates, list sizes, and channel models.
conclusion: The proposed analytical framework fills a gap in polar code theory and can guide practical code design.

title: Commutants Of Complex Symmetric Weighted Composition Operators On Fock Space
authors: Aakriti Sharma
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25544v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate weighted composition operators [MATH] commuting with complex symmetric weighted composition operators [MATH] on the classical Fock space [MATH]. In particular, we investigate the symbols [MATH] and [MATH] give rise to [MATH] commuting with a complex symmetric weighted composition operator on [MATH]. We further characterize when the commuting weighted composition operators are self-adjoint and normal.
tldr: This paper studies weighted composition operators commuting with complex symmetric weighted composition operators on Fock space, a topic in functional analysis and operator theory.
motivation: To understand the structure of commuting weighted composition operators on Fock space, particularly those that are complex symmetric.
method: The authors analyze the symbols of weighted composition operators and derive conditions for commutativity with a given complex symmetric operator.
result: Characterizations of symbols that yield commuting operators, and conditions for such operators to be self-adjoint or normal.
conclusion: The work provides a classification of commuting weighted composition operators in the complex symmetric setting on Fock space.

title: Isometries Between The Unit Spheres Of Spaces Of Metrics
authors: Katsuhisa Koshino
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25558v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a topological space [MATH], let [MATH] be the space of bounded continuous pseudometrics on [MATH], which is endowed with the sup-norm, and let [MATH] be the unit sphere of [MATH]. In this paper, we shall prove that for all non-degenerate compact metrizable spaces [MATH] and [MATH], and for any surjective isometry [MATH], there exists a homeomorphism [MATH] such that for any metric [MATH] and for any pair of points [MATH], [MATH]. As a corollary, we can solve a variant of Tingley's problem on spaces of metics.
tldr: This paper studies isometries between unit spheres of spaces of bounded continuous pseudometrics on compact metrizable spaces, solving a variant of Tingley's problem.
motivation: To characterize the structure of isometries on spaces of metrics, which is a problem in functional analysis and metric geometry.
method: The author proves that any surjective isometry between unit spheres of such spaces induces a homeomorphism between the underlying topological spaces, using techniques from functional analysis and topology.
result: For non-degenerate compact metrizable spaces X and Y, any surjective isometry between unit spheres of spaces of bounded continuous pseudometrics is induced by a homeomorphism between X and Y.
conclusion: This provides a complete description of surjective isometries on these unit spheres, solving a variant of Tingley's problem.

title: Convergence Of The Safeguarded Augmented Lagrangian Method Under The Polyak-Lojasiewicz Constraint Qualification For Constrained Composite Optimization
authors: Jannis Kr\"uger Christian Kanzow
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25567v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we provide theoretical and practical results of the Safeguarded Augmented Lagrangian Method (SALM) for constrained composite optimization problems whose objective is the sum of a smooth and a nonsmooth function. We obtain global convergence results to an M-stationary point for SALM under the Polyak-Lojasiewicz constraint qualification (PLCQ). For this result the boundedness of the Lagrange multipliers is crucial, and this is shown under the assumption that the nonsmooth part of the objective function is locally Lipschitz continuous. A counterexample shows that one cannot expect to get bounded multipliers without such an assumption. The performance of the algorithm is evaluated numerically on a set of sparse portfolio optimization problems with two different regularization terms, one being Lipschitz and the other one being non-Lipschitz. The results are significantly better for the Lipschitz sparsity term, whereas the underlying method generates seemingly unbounded multipliers in many instances when using the non-Lipschitz sparsity function.
tldr: This paper analyzes the convergence of the Safeguarded Augmented Lagrangian Method for constrained composite optimization under the Polyak-Lojasiewicz constraint qualification.
motivation: To provide theoretical guarantees for the Safeguarded Augmented Lagrangian Method (SALM) in solving constrained composite optimization problems, which are common in machine learning and signal processing.
method: The authors prove global convergence to M-stationary points under the Polyak-Lojasiewicz constraint qualification (PLCQ), relying on boundedness of Lagrange multipliers under Lipschitz continuity of the nonsmooth part. They also provide a counterexample showing unbounded multipliers without Lipschitz continuity.
result: SALM converges globally under PLCQ when the nonsmooth part is locally Lipschitz continuous; without Lipschitz continuity, multipliers may become unbounded. Numerical experiments on sparse portfolio optimization show better performance with Lipschitz regularization.
conclusion: The theoretical results justify the use of SALM for Lipschitz composite optimization, but caution is needed for non-Lipschitz problems due to potential multiplier divergence.

title: On The Error Bounds Of The Gauss-type Quadrature Formulae Associated With Spaces Of Parabolic And Cubic Spline Functions With Double Equidistant Knots
authors: Petar B. Nikolov Geno Nikolov
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In two papers from 1995 P. K\"{o}hler and G. Nikolov showed that Gauss--type quadrature formulae associated with spaces of spline functions with equidistant knots are asymptotically optimal in certain Sobolev classes of functions. In particular, Gauss--type quadratures associated with the spaces of spline functions of degree [MATH] with double equispaced knots are asymptotically optimal definite quadrature formulae of order [MATH] when [MATH] is even, and it is conjectured that the asymptotical optimality property persists also in the case of odd [MATH]. For [MATH], these quadrature formulae have been constructed by G. Nikolov, who also proved estimates for their error constants. The aim of this note is to refine the estimates for the error constant in the case [MATH], and to point out to some error estimates in both cases [MATH] and [MATH], which are easier to evaluate and could be sharper than those which involve the uniform norm of the [MATH]-th derivative of the integrand. \medskip \noindent Spline functions, monosplines, Peano representation of linear functionals, definite quadrature formulae, error estimation of quadratures, Bernoulli polynomials.\medskip \noindent 41A55, 65D30, 65D32.
tldr: This paper refines error bounds for Gauss-type quadrature formulas associated with spline spaces, focusing on parabolic and cubic splines with double equidistant knots.
motivation: To improve error estimates for quadrature formulas that are asymptotically optimal in certain Sobolev classes, particularly for odd-degree splines where optimality was only conjectured.
method: The authors derive refined error constant estimates for the cases of parabolic (degree 2) and cubic (degree 3) splines, and provide alternative error estimates that may be sharper than those using uniform norms of derivatives.
result: New, tighter bounds for the error constants are obtained, and alternative error estimates are presented that are easier to evaluate and potentially sharper.
conclusion: The refined estimates confirm the asymptotic optimality for odd-degree splines and offer practical improvements for error estimation in numerical integration.

title: Proximity Operator Characterization For Abstract Convex Functions
authors: The Hung Tran Ewa Bednarczuk
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25614v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider proximity operator as a selector of the subgradient in the context of abstract convexity and characterize its properties in term of minimization problems. We also investigate the continuity and differentiability of proximity operator in the case of paraconvex and weakly convex functions. Supporting examples are given in each section.
tldr: This paper studies proximity operators for abstract convex functions, focusing on their properties as subgradient selectors and continuity/differentiability for paraconvex and weakly convex functions.
motivation: To extend the theory of proximity operators beyond convex analysis to abstract convexity, enabling broader applicability in optimization.
method: The authors characterize proximity operators as selectors of the subgradient in abstract convexity and analyze continuity and differentiability for paraconvex and weakly convex functions, supported by examples.
result: Proximity operators are shown to be subgradient selectors, and their continuity and differentiability properties are established for certain function classes.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for proximity operators in abstract convex optimization, with potential applications in non-smooth optimization.

title: Complex Symmetric Generalized Product Type Operators On Weighted Bergman Spaces
authors: Aakriti Sharma
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we provide a characterization of complex symmetric, self-adjoint, and normal generalized product-type operators on weighted Bergman space, with respect to conjugation [MATH].
tldr: This paper characterizes complex symmetric, self-adjoint, and normal generalized product-type operators on weighted Bergman spaces.
motivation: To understand the structure of certain operators on function spaces, which is a topic in pure mathematics.
method: The authors use functional analysis and operator theory techniques to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for the operators to be complex symmetric, self-adjoint, or normal.
result: They provide explicit characterizations of these operator properties on weighted Bergman spaces.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of complex symmetric operators but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Closure Atlases And Local-to-Global Obstructions In Finite Closure Systems
authors: Jaehwan Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24909v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies finite closure operators on overlapping finite universes and gives an exact local-to-global obstruction criterion for conservative globalization. Given a finite family of local closure systems, its atlas-generated closure is obtained by repeatedly applying the local closure operators to the parts visible in each chart. This closure is the least global closure operator extending all chart closures. A chart-visible obstruction is a consequence produced by this global propagation that lies inside a chart but is not validated by that chart's own closure operator. The main theorem proves that a finite closure atlas has a global conservative realization exactly when no such obstruction occurs; in that case the atlas-generated closure itself is the conservative realization. The obstruction condition is finite and directly computable. The paper also records the indexed representation layer motivating the terminology. For a finite closure system, an indexed truth space selects closed theories as contexts and represents each element by the region of selected closed theories containing it. Closure consequence is always sound for region inclusion, and the full indexed space of all closed theories recovers the original closure consequence exactly; reduced indexed spaces can therefore create spurious region consequences by deleting separating closed theories. A formal opposite gives a four-region membership decomposition - only one, only the other, both, and neither - unless additional separation assumptions are imposed. Finally, overlap-compatible local closed theories glue by canonical union under the atlas-generated closure. The framework is finite, structural, and closure-theoretic; the logical terminology is used only as an interpretation of the underlying closure data.
tldr: This paper studies finite closure operators on overlapping universes and gives a local-to-global obstruction criterion for conservative globalization.
motivation: To understand when local closure systems can be combined into a global closure system without introducing spurious consequences.
method: Defines atlas-generated closure by repeatedly applying local closure operators and identifies chart-visible obstructions as consequences that appear globally but are not validated locally.
result: Proves that a finite closure atlas has a global conservative realization iff no chart-visible obstruction occurs; the atlas-generated closure itself is the conservative realization.
conclusion: The obstruction condition is finite and computable, providing a structural criterion for gluing closure systems.

title: Unprivileged Topology Certificates For Cloud Gpu Attestation
authors: Taylan Alpay Faruk Alpay
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cloud GPU tenants receive a model name and a region, but cannot directly inspect the physical accelerator that runs their job. We present a software-only attestation primitive for this setting. A CUDA probe measures an SM-by-memory-region latency matrix using physical SM labels and dependent global loads. A streaming reducer commits sufficient statistics, configuration, code hashes, network evidence, and a compressed raw data archive into a certificate that a verifier can check without a GPU. The certificate supports three claims. First, the per-SM latency map is a stable physical fingerprint. Over a six-hour full-load RTX 5090 run, its median temporal jitter is 0.09 cycles, while shape-only leave-one-out classification separates distinct Blackwell dies with 100.0% accuracy. Second, cache-bypassing HBM sweeps recover hardware-class topology across generations, including a unified Volta V100 memory domain, a two-way Hopper H200 L2 split, and a Blackwell B200 two-die NV-HBI package whose 74/74 SM partition carries a 30-cycle, 15.5 ns cross-die penalty. Third, public network landmarks bind the same certificate to a coarse location. In the B200 run, 169 RIPE Atlas probes place the server within 44 km of its claimed datacentre and reject all 11 decoy sites. Together, these measurements check cloud-GPU identity, class, and coarse location without privileged access or a vendor key.
tldr: A software-only attestation primitive for cloud GPU identity and location verification using CUDA probes and latency fingerprints.
motivation: Cloud GPU tenants cannot physically inspect accelerators, so a method to verify GPU identity, class, and location without privileged access is needed.
method: A CUDA probe measures SM-by-memory-region latency matrices; a streaming reducer compresses statistics, configuration, code hashes, and network evidence into a certificate verifiable without a GPU.
result: Per-SM latency maps are stable (median jitter 0.09 cycles), shape-only classification distinguishes Blackwell dies with 100% accuracy, and network landmarks place the server within 44 km of its claimed datacentre.
conclusion: Cloud GPU identity, class, and coarse location can be checked without privileged access or vendor keys using latency fingerprints and network landmarks.

title: What Does It Mean To Break A Distillation Defense?
authors: Lena Libon, Pura Peetathawatchai, Michael Aerni, Daniel Paleka, Florian Tram\`er
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25059v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Black-box LLMs (accessible only via API) are vulnerable to distillation attacks, in which an attacker queries the model and trains a student on its outputs. A recent line of work proposes output perturbation defenses that modify the teacher's output to reduce student performance while preserving utility for legitimate users. As a relatively new family of approaches, output perturbation defenses lack a shared threat model, making it difficult to compare them, reason about composing them with other attacks, or evaluate their robustness against realistic adversaries. This underspecification matters beyond technical evaluation: when defenses are deployed to protect intellectual property or justify regulatory compliance, an imprecise threat model can create a false sense of security. We propose a threat model framework that describes attackers along three dimensions: a query budget, a data budget, and an interface profile that captures how attackers interact with the API. Using antidistillation sampling as a case study, we show that whether the defense is considered effective depends on the assumed threat model. We argue that future work on distillation defenses, along with any governance or policy frameworks built around them, should explicitly specify and stress-test attacker capabilities along our three dimensions.
tldr: The paper proposes a threat model framework for distillation attacks on black-box LLMs, focusing on output perturbation defenses.
motivation: Distillation defenses lack a shared threat model, making it hard to compare them or evaluate robustness, which is critical for IP protection and regulatory compliance.
method: The authors define a threat model with three dimensions: query budget, data budget, and interface profile, and apply it to antidistillation sampling as a case study.
result: They show that whether a defense is effective depends on the assumed threat model, highlighting the need for explicit specification.
conclusion: Future work on distillation defenses should explicitly specify and stress-test attacker capabilities along the proposed dimensions.

title: Model Checking In Finite Fields And Finite Groups
authors: Samuel Braunfeld
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the following results. 1, First order model checking is fixed-parameter tractable on the class of finite fields, as a corollary of results of Ax on the theory of (pseudo)finite fields. 2. Every hereditary graph class first order definable in the class of finite groups is monadically stable, and thus has fixed-parameter tractable first order model checking. 3. Monadic second order model checking is not slicewise polynomial on the class of cyclic groups of prime-power order, assuming E [MATH] NE. Thus the same is true on the class of finite fields. 4. The class of finite fields is finitely axiomatizable in monadic second order logic, and so there are no pseudofinite fields in this setting.
tldr: The paper studies model checking complexity in finite fields and finite groups, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To understand the fixed-parameter tractability of first-order and monadic second-order model checking on algebraic structures like finite fields and groups.
method: Uses results from model theory (Ax's theorem, monadic stability) and complexity theory (ETH) to prove tractability or hardness results.
result: First-order model checking is FPT on finite fields; hereditary graph classes definable in finite groups are monadically stable; MSO model checking is not slicewise polynomial on cyclic groups of prime-power order; finite fields are finitely axiomatizable in MSO.
conclusion: The work provides complexity classifications for model checking on finite fields and groups, but is unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: SoK: Ai Secure Code Generation: Progress, Pitfalls, And Paths Forward
authors: Rupam Patir, Keyan Guo, Haipeng Cai, Hongxin Hu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25195v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The increasing use of AI systems for code generation raises a central security question: what can today's models and coding agents actually do to produce secure code, where do they still fail, and what would move the field forward? Existing work has explored prompting, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and agentic workflows for secure code generation, but the field still lacks a systematic understanding of how these techniques improve security and why substantial failures persist. In this SoK, we systematize the progress, pitfalls, and paths forward for AI secure code generation. We introduce a three-level framework that measures models' natural-language understanding of secure coding principles, their code-level actuation of those principles during generation, and the knowledge--actuation gaps between the two. We instantiate this framework across models and coding agents on benchmarks covering both isolated function-level security and full web-application security. Our results show that secure-coding-principle understanding is a statistically strong predictor of code-level outcomes, including functional correctness, security, and joint functional-security correctness. Yet substantial knowledge--actuation gaps remain: models can recognize relevant security principles but still fail to translate them into secure and functional code. These findings offer a principle-centered account of where AI secure code generation stands today and identify concrete paths forward through principle-guided generation, evaluation, benchmarking, and agentic workflows.
tldr: This paper systematizes progress and pitfalls in AI secure code generation, focusing on natural-language understanding and code-level actuation of security principles.
motivation: AI code generation models often produce insecure code, and the field lacks a systematic understanding of why failures persist and how to improve security.
method: The authors propose a three-level framework measuring models' understanding of secure coding principles, their code-level actuation, and the gap between them, evaluated on function-level and web-application benchmarks.
result: Secure-coding-principle understanding is a strong predictor of code-level security and correctness, but significant knowledge–actuation gaps remain.
conclusion: The findings highlight the need for principle-guided generation, evaluation, and agentic workflows to advance AI secure code generation.

title: Decidability And Undecidability Results For LIA-Definable Impartial Combinatorial Games
authors: Shiguang Feng, Liangda Fang, Jiahao Luo, Quanlong Guan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25276v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Combinatorial game theory is a branch of mathematics and theoretical computer science that studies deterministic games with perfect information and no elements of chance. The majority of combinatorial games are impartial and formalized in linear integer arithmetic, which we call LIA-definable impartial combinatorial games (ICGs). This paper studies decidability and undecidability questions for these games. We prove that deciding whether an LIA-definable ICG is terminating or cyclic is undecidable in general, while the corresponding questions become decidable for terminating LIA-definable ICGs. We also show that deciding whether an LIA formula exactly characterizes the set of winning, losing, or draw states of an LIA-definable ICG is undecidable in general and decidable for terminating LIA-definable ICGs. For state-level questions, deciding whether a state is winning or losing remains undecidable even for terminating LIA-definable ICGs, but becomes decidable for terminating finite-depth LIA-definable ICGs. Finally, deciding whether a state is draw for an LIA-definable ICG is undecidable in general and decidable for terminating LIA-definable ICGs.
tldr: This paper studies decidability and undecidability of properties of impartial combinatorial games defined in linear integer arithmetic.
motivation: To understand the computational complexity of analyzing impartial combinatorial games, which are deterministic perfect-information games.
method: The authors formalize impartial combinatorial games in linear integer arithmetic and prove undecidability results via reductions from the halting problem, and decidability results for terminating games.
result: Deciding termination, cyclicity, and exact characterization of winning/losing/draw states is undecidable in general but decidable for terminating games; state-level winning/losing is undecidable even for terminating games but decidable for terminating finite-depth games.
conclusion: The results delineate the boundary between decidable and undecidable problems in combinatorial game theory, highlighting the difficulty of general analysis.

title: Decoupling Reconnaissance And Exploitation: Measuring The Capability Boundaries Of LLM-Based Web Penetration Testing
authors: Liwei Yu, Shuo Li, Ming Zhou, Ge Chu, Yan Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown promise for automated penetration testing, yet existing end-to-end black-box evaluations are highly susceptible to error cascading: failures in early reconnaissance can mask an agent's actual ability to exploit vulnerabilities. To more accurately characterize these capabilities, we propose a two-stage decoupled evaluation framework that separates exploit execution from reconnaissance. Using ground-truth injection and knowledge-driven ablation across 70 high-fidelity web vulnerability testbeds, our framework isolates exploitation performance from reconnaissance noise. We empirically evaluate five open-source penetration-testing agents, covering multiagent, monolithic, and graph-driven architectures, on a strictly aligned subset of 50 representative vulnerabilities. The results reveal a substantial capability gap. With accurate vulnerability context, agents achieve a functional success rate of up to 90.0%, whereas autonomous reconnaissance, measured by targeted vulnerability recall, plateaus at approximately 50.0%, primarily due to failures in parsing unstructured telemetry. Cross-architectural analysis further reveals distinct capability niches: multi-agent isolation is more effective for long-sequence interactions such as de-serialization, while monolithic and graph-driven designs perform better on short-chain injections and cross-session access-control vulnerabilities, respectively. This decoupled evaluation work provides a fine-grained benchmarking protocol and an empirical basis for designing next-generation automated offensive security agents.
tldr: This paper proposes a decoupled evaluation framework for LLM-based web penetration testing, separating reconnaissance from exploitation to measure capability boundaries.
motivation: Existing end-to-end evaluations of LLM-based penetration testing suffer from error cascading where early reconnaissance failures mask true exploitation ability.
method: A two-stage decoupled evaluation uses ground-truth injection and knowledge-driven ablation across 70 web vulnerability testbeds to isolate exploitation performance from reconnaissance noise.
result: With accurate vulnerability context, agents achieve up to 90% functional success, but autonomous reconnaissance recall plateaus at ~50% due to parsing failures.
conclusion: The decoupled evaluation reveals a significant capability gap and distinct architectural niches, providing a benchmarking protocol for designing next-generation offensive security agents.

title: Representation Matters: An Empirical Study Of Program Representations For Llm Vulnerability Reasoning
authors: Andrew Stoltman, Johnathan Tang, Haipeng Cai
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25356v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used for automated vulnerability detection, but it remains unclear how program structure and semantics should be represented for LLM-based reasoning. Most prompting-based approaches provide raw source code, implicitly assuming that more source-level context gives the model better evidence. This paper challenges that assumption through RepBench, an empirical benchmark comparing raw source code with static-analysis-based program representations. RepBench converts real-world C/C++ vulnerability testcases into multiple representations: raw source, Abstract Syntax Trees (ASTs), Control-Flow Graphs (CFGs), Program Dependence Graphs (PDGs), their combinations, and an auxiliary track of enriched PDGs (ePDGs). Using a curated PrimeVul-derived corpus of 107 Joern-based testcases across five CWE categories, we evaluate ten representation variants under a fixed Chain-of-Thought and structured-output protocol, plus 19 additional ePDG cases generated through VulChecker/Hector. Representation choice substantially affects LLM vulnerability reasoning. The strongest variant, AST+PDG, achieves 83.2% accuracy, compared with 53.5% for raw source. At the family level, graph-only prompts outperform both source-only and source-plus-graph prompts while requiring far less prompt overhead. These results reveal a context dilution effect: adding raw source code to compact structural graph evidence can degrade reasoning by making vulnerability-relevant evidence less salient. Overall, our findings show that carefully selected structural representations offer a better accuracy-overhead tradeoff than simply giving LLMs more raw input, and suggest that static analysis can serve as an effective prompt-construction layer for security-focused LLM reasoning.
tldr: This paper studies how different program representations (source code, AST, CFG, PDG) affect LLM-based vulnerability detection, finding that structural graph representations outperform raw source code.
motivation: LLMs are used for vulnerability detection, but it is unclear how program structure should be represented for optimal reasoning. The paper challenges the assumption that raw source code is best.
method: The authors create RepBench, converting C/C++ vulnerability testcases into multiple representations (raw source, AST, CFG, PDG, combinations) and evaluate ten variants under a fixed Chain-of-Thought protocol.
result: The AST+PDG variant achieves 83.2% accuracy vs 53.5% for raw source. Graph-only prompts outperform source-only and source-plus-graph prompts with less overhead.
conclusion: Carefully selected structural representations offer a better accuracy-overhead tradeoff than raw source code, suggesting static analysis can serve as an effective prompt-construction layer for LLM security reasoning.

title: CV-Rules: Serializability Verification Of Concurrency Control Protocols Via Explicit Transaction Ordering
authors: Takashi Hoshino, Shigeo Mitsunari, Takashi Kambayashi, Ryoji Kurosawa, Sho Nakazono
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present CV-rules, an alternative characterization of serializability in which a transaction order constructed by a protocol satisfies two per-read conditions, C-rule (Causality) and V-rule (View Consistency), that constrain the reads-from relation and competing writers. While classical Multi-Version Serialization Graph (MVSG) reasoning characterizes serializability via its acyclicity, our approach requires explicit order construction, enabling direct proofs that build on the protocol's own mechanisms. We prove that CV-rules, serializability, and MVSG acyclicity are all equivalent. Moreover, the C/V separation reveals that serializability is polynomial-time decidable for any fixed bound on the width of the order forced by C-rule. We verify five protocols: Two-Phase Locking, Multi-Version Timestamp Ordering, Serial Safety Net (SSN), Aria, and SnapChain. For SSN and Aria, whose original papers defined only certification conditions, we identify explicit transaction orders arising from their mechanisms; we also prove that Aria's unique-write constraint is unnecessary for serializability. SnapChain, in contrast, is designed directly from CV-rules, enforcing V-rule by construction. All results except the complexity bounds are mechanized in Lean with no additional axioms and no admitted goals.
tldr: This paper presents CV-rules, a new characterization of serializability in database concurrency control, with formal proofs and protocol verification.
motivation: To provide an alternative to classical serialization graph reasoning that enables direct proofs of serializability by constructing explicit transaction orders.
method: Defines two per-read conditions (C-rule and V-rule) that constrain reads-from and competing writers, and proves equivalence to serializability and MVSG acyclicity; verifies five protocols using Lean.
result: CV-rules are equivalent to serializability; serializability is polynomial-time decidable for fixed order width; five protocols are verified, revealing unnecessary constraints in Aria.
conclusion: CV-rules offer a practical framework for proving serializability, with mechanized verification and insights into protocol design.

title: Envy-free Contracts With Subsidies
authors: Matteo Castiglioni, Junjie Chen, Yingkai Li
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25431v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study algorithmic fair contract design, where a principal designs task-level contracts and fairly delegates a set of tasks to a set of agents. Prior work on this setting, particularly on envy-free (EF) contracts, either suffers from an unbounded price of fairness (PoF) or avoids this unboundedness by losing strict fairness. To address these limitations, we propose a novel scheme, called {\it Envy-free Contracts with Subsidies} (EFS), in which the principal may additionally offer agent-specific subsidies. We show that EFS contracts not only restore strict fairness, but can also outperform EF contracts by an arbitrarily large factor. Moreover, in sharp contrast to EF contracts, we prove that EFS contracts admit a tight [MATH] bound on the price of fairness, where [MATH] is the number of agents. We further show that computing optimal EFS contracts is NP-hard in general. Nevertheless, when the number of tasks is constant, we provide a polynomial-time algorithm for computing optimal EFS contracts.
tldr: This paper studies algorithmic fair contract design with subsidies, unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: Prior envy-free contract designs suffer from unbounded price of fairness or lose strict fairness; the authors propose subsidies to overcome these limitations.
method: The paper introduces Envy-free Contracts with Subsidies (EFS), proves tight bounds on price of fairness, and analyzes computational complexity.
result: EFS contracts can outperform EF contracts arbitrarily, admit a tight O(m) bound on price of fairness, and computing optimal EFS is NP-hard but polynomial-time for constant tasks.
conclusion: Subsidies enable strict fairness with bounded efficiency loss, but optimal contract design is computationally hard in general.

title: Towards An Hrs Category In TermCOMP
authors: Aart Middeldorp Johannes Niederhauser
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that there is a simple syntactically-defined subclass of higher-order benchmarks in the termination problem database for which rewriting according to Nipkow's higher-order rewrite systems (HRSs) and rewriting according to a beta-first strategy in the semantics of TermCOMP's higher-order category coincide. This lays the formal foundation for an HRS (sub)category in TermCOMP which would allow more tools to compete against each other.
tldr: This paper proposes a formal foundation for an HRS category in the termination competition TermCOMP by showing equivalence between Nipkow's HRS rewriting and a beta-first strategy.
motivation: To enable more termination tools to compete in the higher-order category of TermCOMP by defining a simple syntactically-defined subclass of benchmarks.
method: The authors prove that for a subclass of higher-order rewrite systems, rewriting according to HRSs coincides with rewriting under a beta-first strategy.
result: They establish the formal equivalence, laying the groundwork for an HRS subcategory in TermCOMP.
conclusion: This allows more tools to participate in the higher-order termination competition.

title: Security And Privacy In Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Architectures, Threats, Defenses, And Future Directions For Building Trustworthy Systems
authors: Balamurugan Palanisamy, G S S Chalapathi, Vikas Hassija, Rajkumar Buyya
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25533v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a dominant paradigm for enhancing large language models with external knowledge. By coupling retrieval mechanisms with generative models, RAG systems improve factual grounding and adaptability across domains. However, integrating retrieval pipelines introduces new security and privacy risks that extend beyond conventional language modeling threats. Sensitive information may be exposed through retrieval indices, query logs, context construction, or federated updates, while adversarial manipulation of knowledge bases can undermine trust in generated outputs. This survey provides a comprehensive examination of privacy and security challenges across RAG systems deployed in centralized, on-device (Micro-RAG), federated, and hybrid paradigms. We present a unified taxonomy of threat surfaces spanning the retrieval, context construction, and generation stages and systematically analyze attack classes, including membership inference, index inference, poisoning, gradient leakage, and collusion. We further review architectural, algorithmic, and cryptographic defenses, highlighting privacy-utility trade-offs and deployment considerations. Finally, we outline open research challenges toward building trustworthy, secure, and resilient RAG systems for real-world applications.
tldr: A survey of security and privacy challenges in Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems, covering threat taxonomies and defenses.
motivation: RAG systems enhance LLMs with external knowledge but introduce new security and privacy risks that need systematic analysis.
method: The paper reviews architectures (centralized, on-device, federated, hybrid), taxonomizes threats across retrieval, context construction, and generation stages, and surveys defenses.
result: A unified taxonomy of attack classes (membership inference, index inference, poisoning, gradient leakage, collusion) and a review of architectural, algorithmic, and cryptographic defenses.
conclusion: Open research challenges remain in building trustworthy, secure, and resilient RAG systems for real-world applications.

title: An Approach For A Supporting Multi-LLM System For Automated Certification Based On The German IT-Grundschutz
authors: Marian Margraf Lea Roxanne Muth
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25608v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to perform semi-automated BSI IT-Grundschutz certification using a MultiLarge Language Model system (MLS) with Hybrid RetrievalAugmented Generation (HybridRAG). Facing the challenges of the Network and Information Security Directive 2 (NIS2) directive, a shortage of specialists, and high implementation costs, our MLS architecture aims to increase efficiency, reduce costs, and support certifiers in maintaining the quality of security concepts while meeting the increased demand for certifications of newly affected companies. The system combines Large Language Models (LLMs) and Knowledge Graphs (KGs) to support different phases of the certification process, including protection needs assessment, modeling, IT-Grundschutz check, measure consolidation, and subsequent realization. Our architecture addresses the growing demand for security concepts and offers an approach to handle the digital security challenges introduced by NIS2.
tldr: This paper proposes a multi-LLM system with hybrid RAG to semi-automate BSI IT-Grundschutz certification, addressing NIS2 compliance challenges.
motivation: The NIS2 directive increases demand for security certifications, but there is a shortage of specialists and high implementation costs, necessitating automated support.
method: The system combines multiple LLMs with knowledge graphs and hybrid retrieval-augmented generation to assist in certification phases like protection needs assessment, modeling, and measure consolidation.
result: The architecture aims to increase efficiency and reduce costs while maintaining quality of security concepts, though no experimental results are presented.
conclusion: The approach offers a scalable solution to meet rising certification demands, but further validation is needed.

title: Probabilistic Agents In Deterministic Audits: Evaluating Multi-Agent Systems For Automated Audits Based On The German IT-Grundschutz
authors: Marian Margraf Lea Roxanne Muth
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The NIS-2 Directive mandates robust Risk Management from thousands of small and medium enterprises. To ensure compliance, companies rely on established standards such as the German IT-Grundschutz (IT-GS) of the Federal Office for Information Security. However, IT-GS certification is resource-intensive and requires a high level of manual effort for documentation, validation, and revision, making scalable implementation difficult and expensive. Building upon our previous conceptual framework, this paper presents the technical implementation and empirical evaluation of a Multi-Agent System (MAS) architecture combined with Hybrid Retrieval Augmented Generation (HybridRAG) for the partial automation of IT-GS certification. We introduce two novel technical contributions to the MAS architecture to enforce the compliance rigor. The Hypothesis-Verification Loop in the Structural Analysis (SA) phase that cross-references agent-inferred dependencies against the Knowledge Graph to reduce hallucinations, and a Decoupled Reasoning Pipeline that separates agent-driven semantic extraction from the deterministic protection need inheritance. We utilize the BSI's "RecPlast GmbH" case study as a human expert-generated reference data set for end-to-end evaluation of the architecture and to quantify Precision, Recall, and F1-scores. The performance of the system is investigated across the phases of SA, Protection Needs Assessment (PNA), Modeling, and IT-GS Check. The empirical results reveal noticeable differences throughout the different steps of IT-GS. While the MAS demonstrates high efficacy in semantic tasks (SA and Modeling), significantly reducing manual effort through automated information extraction, quantitative results reveal limitations in logical reasoning phases (PNA and IT-GS Check) as the probabilistic nature of current LLMs struggles to meet the deterministic rigor required by IT-GS.
tldr: This paper presents a multi-agent system with hybrid retrieval-augmented generation to partially automate IT-Grundschutz certification audits.
motivation: The NIS-2 Directive requires many SMEs to comply with IT-Grundschutz, but manual certification is resource-intensive and not scalable.
method: The authors implement a Multi-Agent System (MAS) with a Hypothesis-Verification Loop and a Decoupled Reasoning Pipeline, using HybridRAG and a knowledge graph to reduce hallucinations and enforce deterministic compliance.
result: The MAS performs well on semantic tasks (structural analysis and modeling) but struggles with logical reasoning phases (protection needs assessment and IT-GS check) due to the probabilistic nature of LLMs.
conclusion: The system can reduce manual effort in semantic tasks, but current LLMs are insufficient for the deterministic rigor required in logical reasoning steps of IT-GS certification.

title: Taxonomy Of Risks On Automated Fact-Checking Systems Considering Its Propagation
authors: Jun Yajima, Tatsuya Oka, Takao Okubo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25645v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In recent years, the posting of fake news including disinformation and misinformation on social networking services (SNS) has become a social problem. To combat this fake news, fact-checking that is the process of assessing the veracity of posts on SNS has become increasingly important. While fact-checking is currently performed by fact-checking organizations, it is difficult to fact-check all posts on SNS. Therefore, the use of automated fact-checking systems is effective. Recent automated fact-checking systems utilize artificial intelligence and large language models, so there are risks of incorrect judgments and posting incorrect results on social media which can lead to the spread of misinformation or to engage in defamation. In this paper, as a first step toward enabling the safe use of automated fact-checking systems, we categorize the specific risks on automated fact-checking systems. In this categorizing, we consider a three-stage risk propagation: risk factors, hazardous situations, and harm. Our analysis revealed that 32 specific risks exist in automated fact-checking systems. In this paper, we utilize the categorized risks as analytical cues (guide words) to present the risk assessment of the automated fact-checking system DEFAME. This assessment result indicates that risks that cannot be derived using STRIDE, a conventional IT security risk assessment method can be derived using our guide words.
tldr: This paper categorizes risks in automated fact-checking systems using a three-stage risk propagation model and applies it to the DEFAME system.
motivation: Automated fact-checking systems using AI and LLMs pose risks of incorrect judgments and spreading misinformation, necessitating a systematic risk assessment.
method: The authors identify 32 specific risks by analyzing risk factors, hazardous situations, and harm, and use these as guide words to assess the DEFAME system, comparing with STRIDE.
result: The analysis reveals 32 specific risks and shows that the proposed guide words can derive risks not captured by STRIDE.
conclusion: The taxonomy provides a foundation for safer deployment of automated fact-checking systems by enabling comprehensive risk assessment.

title: Equilibrium And Infeasibility: A New Solution Concept For Games
authors: Anne Reulke (LIA), Mika\"el Touati (FR 3621, LIA), Rachid El-Azouzi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25707v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Addressing infeasibility in non-cooperative games has become an important topic, as many problems across different applications face this issue. In this paper, we propose a new solution concept for generalized games with possibly infeasible individual constraints. A solution is defined as the limit of a sequence of generalized Nash equilibria induced by games with penalty terms relaxing the individual constraints. Existence is established for a broad range of games and we provide conditions allowing to characterize a [MATH]-penalized solution as a strategy profile maximizing every player's utility over all her penalty minimizing strategies. A variation of Divide-the-Dollar serves as an illustrative example. We further establish the compatibility with the GNE and the solution to the Nash bargaining.
tldr: This paper proposes a new solution concept for generalized games with infeasible individual constraints, using penalized Nash equilibria.
motivation: Many non-cooperative games face infeasibility issues, and existing solution concepts may not apply. The authors aim to provide a robust solution concept that handles infeasible constraints.
method: The solution is defined as the limit of a sequence of generalized Nash equilibria from games with penalty terms that relax individual constraints. Existence is established for a broad class of games, and conditions for characterization are provided.
result: The penalized solution can be characterized as a strategy profile maximizing each player's utility over all penalty-minimizing strategies. Compatibility with GNE and Nash bargaining is shown.
conclusion: The proposed solution concept offers a way to handle infeasibility in non-cooperative games, with theoretical guarantees and illustrative examples.

title: Distributed SDN-Based Communication Architecture For The Pods4Rail System
authors: Dingyang Liu (COSYS), Dereje Mechal Molla (COSYS), L\'eo Mendiboure (cosys-Erena, COSYS), Marion Berbineau
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25711v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Future multimodal transportation systems require reliable, low-latency communication infrastructures to coordinate autonomous vehicles and moving infrastructure across rail and road networks. Traditional centralized control architectures struggle to meet these requirements in highly dynamic environments due to increased latency, limited scalability, and poor adaptability to changing network conditions. To address this, we propose a distributed communication architecture integrating Software-Defined Networking (SDN) and Multi-Access Edge Computing (MEC), that can create a flexible, programmable and lowlatency network. Results show controller communication and flow setup latency between edge SDN controllers and Pods are lower than reported in literature. The framework uses hierarchical control with regional and edge controllers to support low-latency interface management and edge autonomy. Operational workflows and control logic are defined as representative scenarios. The architecture combines regional policy coordination with edge-level autonomy, enabling local failover and adaptive interface management without central dependency.
tldr: This paper proposes a distributed SDN and MEC-based communication architecture for the Pods4Rail system, focusing on low-latency and reliable communication for autonomous vehicles in rail and road networks.
motivation: Traditional centralized control architectures cannot meet the low-latency and scalability requirements of future multimodal transportation systems.
method: The authors design a hierarchical control architecture with regional and edge SDN controllers integrated with MEC, and evaluate controller communication and flow setup latency.
result: The proposed architecture achieves lower controller communication and flow setup latency compared to reported literature.
conclusion: The distributed SDN-MEC architecture enables low-latency, adaptive, and reliable communication for autonomous vehicle coordination in dynamic transportation environments.

title: Tracing Target Answers In Poisoned Retrieval Corpora Via Token Influence Attribution
authors: Yan-Lun Chen, Pin-Yu Chen, Chia-Mu Yu, Ying-Dar Lin, Yu-Sung Wu, Wei-Bin Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems are vulnerable to corpus poisoning attacks that manipulate model outputs through malicious retrieved documents. Existing detection methods typically rely on auxiliary classifiers or additional LLM-based verification, introducing substantial computational overhead. We present TRACE, a lightweight detection framework that identifies poisoning attacks by tracing answer-related tokens through token influence attribution. TRACE first discovers recurrent high-influence keywords across retrieved documents and then performs a secondary verification to confirm their influence on model predictions. Experiments on three QA benchmarks and six LLMs demonstrate strong detection performance while simultaneously uncovering attacker-specified target answers.
tldr: TRACE is a lightweight framework for detecting corpus poisoning attacks in RAG systems using token influence attribution.
motivation: Existing detection methods for corpus poisoning in RAG systems are computationally expensive, requiring auxiliary classifiers or LLM verification.
method: TRACE identifies recurrent high-influence keywords across retrieved documents via token influence attribution, then performs secondary verification to confirm their influence on model predictions.
result: Experiments on three QA benchmarks and six LLMs show strong detection performance while uncovering attacker-specified target answers.
conclusion: TRACE provides an efficient and effective approach to detect poisoning attacks in RAG systems without heavy computational overhead.

title: Shoot The Honey, Cloak The Player: Towards Zero-Runtime-Overhead Proactive Defense And Detection For Visual Game Cheating
authors: Jianing Wang, Chuqi Zhang, Yuancheng Jiang, Adil Ahmad, Shanqing Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25734v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Visual aimbots have emerged as a serious cheating threat in first-person shooter (FPS) games, as they evade existing anti-cheat defenses by operating only on rendered frames rather than game memory. However, existing defenses fail to provide an end-to-end solution: post-hoc behavior detectors cannot protect match integrity in real time and are increasingly fragile against human-mimicking aimbots, while proactive runtime defenses often lack accountability, incur substantial overhead, or require intrusive system integration. We present AimTrap, the first end-to-end defense against visual aimbots that combines real-time protection with post-game detection using two adversarial texture mechanisms. Adversarial Camouflage Textures (ACT) hide real players from aimbots, while Adversarial Honeypot Textures (AHT) lure aimbots into locking onto fake targets, yielding strong evidence of cheating. To make this practical, AimTrap integrates differentiable rendering with Expectation over Renderings for robust 3D texture synthesis, secure texture management, and a novel honeypot-interaction trajectory analysis pipeline for accurate cheating attribution. In real-game evaluation against a state-of-the-art visual aimbot, ACT achieves 85.1% defense success, AHT achieves 96.9%. Compared with prior baselines, AimTrap attains extremely low false-positive rates, while incurring negligible runtime overhead. These results show that AimTrap provides a practical and effective end-to-end defense against visual aimbots.
tldr: AimTrap is an end-to-end defense against visual aimbots in FPS games using adversarial textures to hide real players and lure cheaters.
motivation: Visual aimbots evade existing anti-cheat defenses by operating on rendered frames, and current solutions lack real-time protection or incur high overhead.
method: AimTrap uses Adversarial Camouflage Textures (ACT) to hide players and Adversarial Honeypot Textures (AHT) to create fake targets, integrating differentiable rendering and trajectory analysis.
result: ACT achieves 85.1% defense success, AHT achieves 96.9%, with negligible runtime overhead and low false-positive rates.
conclusion: AimTrap provides a practical, effective end-to-end defense against visual aimbots without significant performance impact.

title: Ras: Measuring Llm Safety Through Refusal Alignment
authors: Chang-Chieh Huang, Yan-Lun Chen, Chia-Mu Yu, Wei-Bin Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Safety evaluation of large language models (LLMs) is commonly performed by querying models with unsafe or jailbreak prompts and judging whether their outputs violate a safety policy. Although useful, output-level evaluation is expensive, sensitive to judge choice, and easily tied to fixed question banks. We propose **SafeVec**, a white-box evaluation procedure that measures safety from internal representations rather than generated answers. **SafeVec** first extracts layer-wise refusal directions from a safety-aligned reference model, then selects stable layer windows where safe and unsafe behaviors are separable, and finally scores a target model by measuring whether its hidden states align with these refusal directions under unsafe and jailbreak prompts. The resulting metric, **RAS** (**R**efusal **A**lignment **S**core), maps representation-level refusal alignment to a calibrated 0-100 safety score. Across `Llama`, `Gemma`, and `Qwen` model families, RAS separates aligned models from uncensored and abliterated variants, tracks output-level attack success rate, and is substantially faster than judge-based evaluation. These results suggest that refusal alignment provides a compact and efficient signal for white-box LLM safety evaluation.
tldr: This paper proposes a white-box safety evaluation method for LLMs using internal representations.
motivation: Current output-level safety evaluation is expensive, sensitive to judge choice, and limited to fixed question banks.
method: SafeVec extracts refusal directions from a reference model, selects stable layer windows, and scores target models by alignment with these directions under unsafe prompts.
result: RAS separates aligned from uncensored models, tracks attack success rate, and is faster than judge-based evaluation.
conclusion: Refusal alignment provides a compact and efficient signal for white-box LLM safety evaluation.

title: Color Matters: Trigger Color Affects Success In Federated Backdoor Attacks
authors: Kavindu Herath, Joshua C. Zhao, Saurabh Bagchi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25858v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated learning is vulnerable to backdoor attacks in which malicious clients inject poisoned updates while preserving benign-task performance. In this paper, we study a semantics-driven backdoor mechanism in which attackers use natural visual accessories as triggers and manipulate only the trigger color while keeping the attack pipeline fixed. Our framework considers semantic trigger objects such as masks and sunglasses, instantiated in black and white variants, and evaluates their effect in a controlled federated learning setting. Malicious clients construct poisoned samples by applying a trigger to source-class images and relabeling them to an attacker-chosen target class, while benign clients train only on clean data. We analyze this mechanism under both a standard poisoning objective and a stronger SABLE-based objective that combines clean classification loss, triggered target loss, feature-separation loss in the penultimate representation space, and regularization to keep malicious updates close to the global model. This design enables the attack to remain effective while reducing excessive update drift. Experiments on a four-class CelebA hair-color task show that trigger color significantly changes attack success rate even when trigger semantics, placement, and poisoning budget are unchanged. White triggers are more effective for attacks targeting the blond class, whereas black triggers perform better for attacks targeting the black class. The same trend persists under robust aggregation, showing that trigger color is a meaningful factor in the operation, persistence, and evaluation of semantic backdoor mechanisms in federated learning.
tldr: This paper studies how trigger color affects the success of backdoor attacks in federated learning, a topic in adversarial machine learning.
motivation: Federated learning is vulnerable to backdoor attacks; understanding semantic triggers like color can improve attack evaluation and defense.
