method: The authors propose a semantics-driven backdoor mechanism using visual accessories (masks, sunglasses) in black/white, and test under standard and SABLE-based poisoning objectives on CelebA dataset.
result: White triggers are more effective for targeting the blond class, while black triggers work better for the black class, even under robust aggregation.
conclusion: Trigger color is a meaningful factor in semantic backdoor attacks and should be considered in attack design and defense evaluation.

title: Restoring Incentive Compatibility In Two-Stage Energy Markets With Prosumers
authors: Nikolas Koumpis, Koushik Kar, Leandros Tassiulas, Manolis Zampetakis
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A central challenge in modern energy market design is the formulation of a strategy-proof imbalance settlement layer that secures both the economic efficiency of the institution and the stability of the power grid. Public data reveals that the day-ahead market is strategically biased below actual consumer demand. Such empirical observations are explained by active prosumers which provide implementable incentives for demand under-reporting. Active prosumers buy energy in the day-ahead market and sell energy in the real-time market for balancing real-time energy deviations. By under-reporting their demand for the day ahead they inflate real-time imbalances and, under uniform pricing, they dispatch their generation assets more profitably. We model the two-stage institution under linear preferences and benchmark it against its associated competitive equilibria. We show that although consumers' incentives for demand under-reporting vanish when the day-ahead market scales, prosumers' incentives remain lower bounded by a positive gain which depends only on the real-time market generation stack and their shares over it. To restore incentive compatibility under the existing informational constraints, we design a leave-one-out contrastive scoring rule-based penalty that is implemented by the day-ahead market operator, incentivizes prosumers to report their demand truthfully and ensures small charges when participating honestly. We illustrate these results with numerical simulations on synthetic data and evaluate our mechanism on real-market data by first rationalizing demand reports as subjective equilibria of the induced game. Our mechanism demonstrates strong incentive alignment while retaining a low cost for honest participation.
tldr: This paper addresses incentive compatibility in two-stage energy markets with prosumers, using a scoring rule-based penalty mechanism.
motivation: Prosumers can exploit two-stage energy markets by under-reporting demand to profit from real-time imbalances, threatening market efficiency and grid stability.
method: The authors model the two-stage market with linear preferences, analyze strategic behavior, and design a leave-one-out contrastive scoring rule penalty to restore truthfulness.
result: The mechanism ensures incentive compatibility for prosumers with low honest participation cost, validated on synthetic and real market data.
conclusion: The proposed penalty mechanism effectively aligns prosumer incentives with truthful reporting while maintaining low costs for honest participants.

title: A Tattered Cloak Of Invisibility: Measuring Anonymity Loss In Railgun On Ethereum
authors: Kanan Huseynov, Ali Shahzaib, Istv\'an Andr\'as Seres, J\'anos Tapolcai
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: From a user's perspective, perhaps the most significant difference between traditional banking services and widely used blockchain-based financial systems is that, in the latter, transactions and, either directly or indirectly, account balances and transaction histories are publicly observable. Therefore, a growing number of cryptographic solutions have been proposed to add a privacy layer to such systems. However, the privacy that users actually obtain does not depend solely on the security of the underlying cryptographic protocol: user behavior, transaction amount patterns, and timing decisions can substantially reduce anonymity. In this work, we study behavioral leakage in cryptocurrency mixers, focusing on Railgun on Ethereum. We aim to heuristically estimate the probability that a given deposit and withdrawal transaction belong to the same user. We consider five sources of leakage: characteristic timing patterns, address reuse, proximity in the transaction graph induced by prior public transactions, amount fingerprints that preserve distinctive digit patterns across transaction values, and knapsack type matches in which groups of transaction amounts add up in revealing ways. Our results show that even cryptographically strong privacy systems may suffer substantial anonymity loss due to user behavior and transaction patterns. Our five heuristics are able to uniquely link 17.65% of Railgun withdraw transactions to deposit transactions. We also applied a knapsack solver algorithm that was able to produce a 3.42 bit median anonymity loss for withdraw transactions. This work contributes to a better understanding of the practical privacy limits of mixers and anonymity pools, and points toward safer usage practices and design principles.
tldr: This paper analyzes anonymity loss in the Railgun cryptocurrency mixer on Ethereum due to user behavior and transaction patterns.
motivation: To understand the practical privacy limits of cryptographic mixers, as user behavior can undermine theoretical privacy guarantees.
method: The authors develop five heuristics (timing patterns, address reuse, transaction graph proximity, amount fingerprints, knapsack matches) to link deposit and withdrawal transactions in Railgun.
result: The heuristics uniquely link 17.65% of withdrawals to deposits, and a knapsack solver yields a median anonymity loss of 3.42 bits.
conclusion: Even cryptographically strong privacy systems suffer substantial anonymity loss from behavioral leakage, suggesting the need for safer usage practices and design improvements.

title: Do (Not) Tell Me About My Insecurities: Assessing The Status Quo Of Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure In Germany Amid New Eu Cybersecurity Regulations
authors: Sebastian Neef, Cenk Schlunke, Anne Hennig
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In our increasingly interconnected world, good IT security practices are necessary to prevent vulnerabilities and data breaches. Providing security contacts, e.g., via Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure (CVD) programs or security.txt files, is an important practice for businesses to facilitate vulnerability reporting by external parties. As part of a longitudinal study, we analyzed the adoption of, as well as the challenges and experiences with, CVD programs among the 40 companies listed on Germany's DAX (the country's primary stock market index). In addition to monitoring publicly available information about their CVD programs, we sent out questionnaires via email and postal mail in 2023 and 2025, and received answers from 20\% of the companies. The adoption rates show a significant increase from 50\% (2023) to over 90\% (2025), with ten new CVD programs and 25 new security.txt files now available. The survey answers reveal that, for example, legal obligations (e.g., NIS2 and CRA) drive the adoption of CVD practices, but a lack of (human) resources and varying report quality are considered drawbacks. As the first study to survey 40 German stock market index (DAX) companies on their CVD practices, our results can help foster the adoption and understanding of security programs among SMEs and other companies, and provide policymakers with insights into practical challenges and industry experiences.
tldr: A study on the adoption of Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure programs among German DAX companies, driven by new EU cybersecurity regulations.
motivation: To assess the current state of CVD adoption and understand challenges faced by large companies in Germany, especially in light of upcoming EU regulations like NIS2 and CRA.
method: Longitudinal study combining monitoring of public CVD program information and surveys (email and postal) sent to 40 DAX companies in 2023 and 2025.
result: CVD adoption increased from 50% in 2023 to over 90% in 2025, with legal obligations being a key driver, but lack of resources and report quality remain challenges.
conclusion: The findings can help SMEs adopt CVD programs and provide policymakers with insights into practical industry challenges.

title: Variable Bound Tightening For Nash Equilibrium Computation In Multiplayer Imperfect-Information Games
authors: Sam Ganzfried
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25997v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: There has been significant recent progress in algorithms for approximation of Nash equilibrium in large two-player zero-sum imperfect-information games and exact computation of Nash equilibrium in multiplayer strategic-form games. While counterfactual regret minimization and fictitious play are scalable to large games and have convergence guarantees in two-player zero-sum games, they do not guarantee convergence to Nash equilibrium in multiplayer games. Recently, an approach has been presented for exact computation of Nash equilibrium in multiplayer imperfect-information games that solves a quadratically constrained program based on a nonlinear complementarity problem formulation derived from the sequence-form game representation. This formulation was solved using Gurobi's nonconvex quadratic solver, which employs spatial branch-and-bound to iteratively refine variable bounds by solving convex relaxations of bilinear terms via McCormick envelopes. During presolve, Gurobi introduces auxiliary variables and, in some cases, binary variables, leading to an internal MIQCP reformulation. This approach was demonstrated to outperform prior algorithms from the Gambit software suite and quickly solve three-player Kuhn poker after removal of dominated actions; however, the algorithm was not able to solve the full version of the game within 24 hours. In this paper, we derive finite bounds on slack and multiplier variables in the nonlinear complementarity formulation. These bounds strengthen the convex relaxations used within spatial branch-and-bound and lead to substantial computational improvements. We demonstrate the impact of the proposed bounds on exact Nash equilibrium computation in three-player Kuhn poker.
tldr: This paper improves variable bound tightening for exact Nash equilibrium computation in multiplayer imperfect-information games using a nonlinear complementarity formulation.
motivation: Existing algorithms for exact Nash equilibrium in multiplayer games are limited; prior work could not solve full three-player Kuhn poker within 24 hours.
method: The authors derive finite bounds on slack and multiplier variables in the nonlinear complementarity formulation to strengthen convex relaxations in spatial branch-and-bound.
result: The proposed bounds lead to substantial computational improvements, enabling faster solution of three-player Kuhn poker.
conclusion: Variable bound tightening is an effective technique for accelerating exact Nash equilibrium computation in multiplayer games.

title: BlowLive: Blow-Based Multi-Factor Biometrics With Liveness Detection And Revocability
authors: Eyasu Getahun Chekole, Howard Halim, Dani\"el Reijsbergen, Jianying Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2606.25998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Biometric authentication systems are increasingly deployed in security-critical applications, yet existing physiological and behavioral biometrics suffer from fundamental limitations: 1) they are vulnerable to spoofing attacks due to unreliable liveness detection, 2) biometric templates may leak privacy-sensitive information 3) intra-user variability results in accuracy degradation, and 4) it is difficult to revoke physiological biometrics and safeguard them over long-term use. To address these challenges, we propose BlowLive, a robust multi-factor biometric (MFB) framework that integrates blow-acoustic signals and facial biometrics as complementary behavioral and physiological modalities. BlowLive incorporates advanced spectral feature extraction and multimodal fusion techniques, achieving high authentication accuracy even for behavioral modalities. Instead of relying on conventional biometric approaches that utilize raw biometric templates for authentication, the proposed framework adopts a fuzzy-extractor-based biometric authentication scheme, wherein stable cryptographic keys are derived from inherently noisy biometric inputs and subsequently used for authentication. To defend against playback, synthetic, and deepfake attacks, BlowLive further integrates a novel Doppler shift-based liveness detection mechanism. We implement the complete BlowLive framework and experimentally evaluate its effectiveness using biometric data collected from 50 participants. The experimental results demonstrate high authentication accuracy (99.56% for blow-acoustics and 100% for facial and fusion modalities), robust liveness detection (99.42% accuracy), strong template protection and revocability, non-invasiveness, and high usability.
tldr: BlowLive is a multi-factor biometric authentication framework using blow-acoustic signals and facial biometrics with liveness detection and revocability.
motivation: Existing biometric systems suffer from spoofing, privacy leakage, accuracy degradation, and irreversibility.
method: The framework integrates blow-acoustic and facial modalities, uses spectral feature extraction and multimodal fusion, employs a fuzzy extractor for key derivation, and incorporates Doppler shift-based liveness detection.
result: Achieves 99.56% accuracy for blow-acoustics, 100% for facial and fusion, and 99.42% liveness detection accuracy on 50 participants.
conclusion: BlowLive provides a secure, accurate, and usable multi-factor biometric system with strong template protection and revocability.

In this work, we develop, in the Gurevich-Pitaevskii framework, an analytic theory for the evolution of localized pulses in the defocusing modified Korteweg–de Vries equation theory for situations when a dispersive shock does not eventually transform into a sequence of well-separated solitons. We fo…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064208] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an analytic theory for the evolution of localized pulses in the defocusing modified Korteweg–de Vries equation, focusing on dispersive shock waves and soliton dynamics.
motivation: To understand the evolution of localized pulses in nonlinear wave systems where dispersive shocks do not break into solitons, which is relevant to fluid dynamics and nonlinear optics.
method: The authors use the Gurevich-Pitaevskii framework and Whitham modulation theory to derive analytic solutions for the pulse evolution.
result: They obtain explicit formulas describing the pulse shape and dynamics, including the formation of dispersive shock waves.
conclusion: The analytic theory successfully describes the evolution of localized pulses in the defocusing mKdV equation, providing insights into nonlinear wave phenomena.

title: Unsteady Phase Waves In The One-dimensional Swarmalator Model With Inertia
authors: Kevin O'keeffe
abstract:
Author(s): Kevin O'Keeffe

We study a one-dimensional swarmalator model with inertia. Previous studies have focused almost exclusively on the overdamped limit. We find inertia introduces an unsteady collective state in which the rainbow order parameters undergo multiharmonic oscillations. This “thrashing” phase wave bifurcate…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064210] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a one-dimensional swarmalator model with inertia, discovering a new unsteady collective state called 'thrashing' phase waves.
motivation: Previous studies of swarmalator models focused on the overdamped limit; this work aims to understand the effect of inertia on collective dynamics.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional swarmalator model with inertia using numerical simulations and bifurcation analysis.
result: Inertia introduces multiharmonic oscillations in the rainbow order parameters, leading to a 'thrashing' phase wave state.
conclusion: Inertia can fundamentally alter the collective behavior of swarmalators, producing unsteady states not present in the overdamped regime.

title: Effect Of Temporary Lockdowns On Disease Extinction Risk In Assortative Networks
authors: Elad Korngut And Michael Assaf
abstract:

Changing environmental conditions can significantly affect the dynamics of disease spread. [Phys. Rev. E 113, 064309] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of temporary lockdowns on disease extinction in assortative networks using stochastic modeling.
motivation: Understanding how temporary lockdowns affect disease extinction risk is crucial for public health policy, especially in structured populations.
method: The authors develop a stochastic model of disease spread on assortative networks and analyze the probability of extinction under temporary lockdown scenarios.
result: They find that temporary lockdowns can significantly increase extinction probability, with the effect depending on network assortativity and lockdown timing.
conclusion: Temporary lockdowns can be an effective strategy for disease eradication, but their success is sensitive to network structure and implementation details.

result: The paper reveals unique dynamics of droplet motion and removal under low-pressure conditions.
conclusion: The findings provide insights for designing surfaces that promote droplet removal in low-pressure environments.

title: Spatial Correlations In Susceptible-infected-susceptible Processes On Random Regular Graphs
authors: Alexander Leibenzon, Samuel W. S. Johnson, Ruth E. Baker, And Michael Assaf
abstract:

In network-based susceptible-infected-susceptible (SIS) models of infectious disease transmission, infection can only occur between directly connected individuals. This constraint naturally gives rise to spatial correlations between the states of neighboring nodes, as the infection status of connect…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064307] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spatial correlations in SIS epidemic models on random regular graphs, a topic in statistical physics of networks.
motivation: Understanding how spatial correlations affect epidemic spread on networks is important for modeling infectious diseases.
method: The authors develop an analytical approximation for pair correlations in the SIS model on random regular graphs, using moment closure techniques.
result: They derive expressions for the steady-state density of infected nodes and the pair correlation function, showing how clustering influences epidemic thresholds.
conclusion: Spatial correlations significantly impact the dynamics of SIS processes on networks, and the analytical method captures these effects accurately.

result: They identify parameter regimes leading to multistability and characterize bifurcation structures.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the design principles of multistable gene circuits.

title: Influence Of Visual Field Offset On Collective Behavior: An Exploration Using The Two-dimensional Vicsek Model

result: Visual field offset alters the onset of collective motion and can lead to different phases of alignment.
conclusion: The offset angle is a key parameter controlling collective behavior, with implications for biological swarms and robotic systems.

title: Topological Enhancement Of Protein Kinetic Stability
authors: João N. C. Especial And Patrícia F. N. Faísca
abstract:

Knotted proteins embed a physical (i.e., open) knot within their native structures. For decades, significant effort has been devoted to elucidating the functional role of knots in proteins, yet no consensus has been reached. Here, using extensive Monte Carlo off-lattice simulations of a simple struc…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062402] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how topological knots in proteins enhance kinetic stability using Monte Carlo simulations, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To understand the functional role of knots in proteins, which has been debated for decades.
method: Extensive Monte Carlo off-lattice simulations of a simple structure-based model for knotted proteins.
result: Topological knots increase the kinetic stability of proteins by slowing down unfolding.
conclusion: Knots may serve a biological function by enhancing protein robustness against mechanical stress.

[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064206] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spiral wave chimeras in delay-coupled oscillators on a sphere, a topic in nonlinear dynamics with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Spiral wave chimeras are a fascinating pattern in coupled oscillator systems, but the work is purely classical nonlinear dynamics.
method: The authors analyze a model of nonlocally coupled phase oscillators on a sphere with time delay, using numerical simulations and theoretical analysis.
result: They observe switching between different spiral-phase kinks and characterize the dynamics.

The experiment indicates that the dominant electron ene…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023322] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.

title: Proof-of-principle Experiment Of A Beam Extraction Over Millions Of Turns Using Stable Resonance Islands And Bent Crystal
authors: D. E. Veres, P. Arrutia, S. Cettour Cave, B. H. F. Lindström, M. Giovannozzi, L. E. Pauwels, F. F. van der Veken, F. M. Velotti, And G. Franchetti
abstract:
Author(s): D. E. Veres, P. Arrutia, S. Cettour Cave, B. H. F. Lindström, M. Giovannozzi, L. E. Pauwels, F. F. Van der Veken, F. M. Velotti, and G. Franchetti

A recent theoretical investigation indicated that combining particle trapping in resonance islands with planar channeling in a bent crystal may offer a promising option for a low-loss, or even septum-free, slow-extraction technique. This work reports on the successful proof-of-principle experiment conducted at the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron, in which stable islands and a bent crystal were employed to split and channel a circulating beam onto an absorber, thereby emulating slow extraction.

tldr: This paper reports a proof-of-principle experiment on beam extraction using resonance islands and a bent crystal at CERN's Super Proton Synchrotron.
motivation: To demonstrate a low-loss, septum-free slow-extraction technique for particle accelerators by combining particle trapping in resonance islands with planar channeling in a bent crystal.
method: The experiment was conducted at the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron, where stable resonance islands and a bent crystal were used to split and channel a circulating beam onto an absorber, emulating slow extraction.
result: Successful proof-of-principle demonstration of beam extraction over millions of turns using the proposed technique.
conclusion: The technique shows promise for low-loss slow extraction in high-energy accelerators, but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

Combining experiments and theory, we find that facilitating compression yields effects anal…

tldr: This paper studies gas-liquid-grain displacement dynamics in confined granular systems, focusing on the role of gas compressibility.

method: Combined experiments and theoretical analysis to probe how gas compression affects morphodynamics.
result: Facilitating compression yields effects on displacement patterns.
conclusion: Gas compressibility is a key control parameter in granular displacement processes.

title: Leidenfrost Hydrogels: Elastic Surface-wave Instability And Sustained Bouncing
authors: Nathan C. J. Coombs, Peter Lewin-Jones, Mykyta V. Chubynsky, And James E. Sprittles
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan C. J. Coombs, Peter Lewin-Jones, Mykyta V. Chubynsky, and James E. Sprittles

This work investigates the oscillatory dynamics and subsequent sustained bouncing behavior of Leidenfrost hydrogels, a phenomenon that has received little theoretical attention to date. Building on previous approaches toward drop impacts and Leidenfrost drops, a computational model is developed to capture the oscillatory dynamics and analyze the mechanism of energy injection that leads to sustained bouncing.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022052] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the oscillatory dynamics and sustained bouncing of Leidenfrost hydrogels, a fluid dynamics phenomenon.
motivation: To understand the mechanism of energy injection that leads to sustained bouncing in Leidenfrost hydrogels, which has received little theoretical attention.
method: A computational model is developed to capture the oscillatory dynamics and analyze the energy injection mechanism.
result: The model reproduces the sustained bouncing behavior and reveals the role of elastic surface-wave instability.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for Leidenfrost hydrogels and their unique bouncing dynamics.

This work aims to study the resynchronization of CR flagella after a high light intensity stimulus, known as photoshock. The synchronization is estimated thanks to a qu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023294] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies flagellar synchronization in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii using time-frequency analysis to characterize photophobic response.
motivation: Understanding how microalgae coordinate flagella after light stimuli is important for biological physics but unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use time-frequency domain analysis to track phase synchronization between two flagella before and after a high-intensity light pulse.
result: They quantify resynchronization dynamics and identify characteristic timescales of the photophobic response.
conclusion: The work provides insights into biological synchronization but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: When Surface Dynamics Fakes Symmetry: Oxygen On Rh(100) Revisited
authors: Lutz Hammer, Tilman Kißlinger, Margareta Wagner, Reinhard B. Neder, Michael Schmid, Ulrike Diebold, And M. Alexander Schneider
abstract:
Author(s): Lutz Hammer, Tilman Kißlinger, Margareta Wagner, Reinhard B. Neder, Michael Schmid, Ulrike Diebold, and M. Alexander Schneider

Heating a long-range ordered adsorbate phase beyond its stability temperature does not necessarily result in a disordered phase; it can also break up into heavily fluctuating ordered domains. Temporal and/or spatial averaging over these fluctuations may give the impression of both a wrong periodicit…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023296] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies oxygen adsorption on Rh(100) surface, revealing that fluctuating ordered domains can mimic a wrong surface symmetry under thermal averaging.
motivation: To understand the behavior of adsorbate phases beyond their stability temperature and correct misinterpretations of surface symmetry from diffraction patterns.
method: Combined experimental techniques (STM, LEED) and simulations to analyze the structure and dynamics of oxygen on Rh(100) at elevated temperatures.
result: Heating the ordered phase leads to heavily fluctuating domains that, upon averaging, produce a diffraction pattern suggesting a different symmetry than the true local structure.
conclusion: Care must be taken in interpreting surface symmetries from averaged data, as dynamic fluctuations can create false impressions of periodicity.

title: Seeing New Depths: Three-Dimensional Flow Of A Free-Swimming Alga

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on surface defects, electrical stress, and plasma formation.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators and other high-voltage devices; understanding its mechanism can improve reliability and efficiency.
method: The authors synthesize recent experimental and computational studies to build a coherent mechanistic picture of vacuum breakdown.
result: A multi-step process involving surface defects, field emission, heating, and plasma formation is identified as the trigger for breakdown.
conclusion: Improved understanding can guide the design of more robust accelerator structures and other high-power technologies.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews experimental progress in hadron production from open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium spectroscopy and strong interaction mechanisms.
motivation: Understanding charmonium decays and searching for new hadrons are crucial for validating QCD and exploring quark confinement and gluon binding.
method: The paper reviews experimental results from BABAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII, highlighting recent high-precision data from BESIII.
result: The review summarizes current knowledge of hadron production in charm-meson pair systems and identifies BESIII as the leading facility for such measurements.
conclusion: Continued experimental studies of open-charm meson pairs will provide deeper insights into strong interaction dynamics and hadron spectroscopy.

title: Editorial: A Tribute To The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Véronique van Elewyck And Dietrich Belitz
abstract:

Three Colloquia honor the Arecibo Observatory’s legacy, exploring its revolutionary impact on planetary radar studies, radio astronomy, and geospace science.

[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 010001] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: An editorial tribute to the Arecibo Observatory, summarizing its impact on planetary radar, radio astronomy, and geospace science.
motivation: To honor the legacy of the Arecibo Observatory and its contributions to various scientific fields.
method: The paper is an editorial that reviews historical achievements and impacts of the observatory.
result: The editorial highlights three colloquia covering planetary radar studies, radio astronomy, and geospace science.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory had a revolutionary impact on multiple areas of science.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the scientific legacy of planetary radar observations at the Arecibo Observatory, focusing on Solar System bodies.
motivation: To document the unique contributions of Arecibo's planetary radar system to planetary science and its role in supporting space missions.
method: The paper provides a historical overview of radar techniques and summarizes key observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon, Saturn system, and near-Earth asteroids.
result: Arecibo's radar provided high-resolution surface and subsurface data, enabling characterization of planetary terrains and asteroid properties.
conclusion: The Arecibo radar system was a uniquely powerful tool for planetary science, and its loss leaves a gap in observational capabilities.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A historical review of the Arecibo radio telescope's contributions to radio astronomy and atmospheric science.
motivation: To document the legacy of the Arecibo Observatory and its scientific impact over five decades.
method: Historical narrative and review of key scientific results from Arecibo's upgrades and observations.
result: Summarizes Arecibo's major contributions in pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave detection.
conclusion: Arecibo was a transformative instrument in radio astronomy, and its loss is significant for the field.

title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars and their multimessenger connections.
motivation: Continuous gravitational waves are a key frontier in gravitational-wave astrophysics, and multimessenger observations could reveal physics of dense matter.
method: The paper surveys detection prospects with future gravitational-wave detectors and discusses simultaneous electromagnetic observations.
result: It outlines the potential for multimessenger astronomy with continuous waves and implications for nuclear and condensed matter physics.
conclusion: Multimessenger observations of continuous gravitational waves will enhance understanding of neutron star interiors and fundamental physics.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews convection-cloud chambers as a laboratory tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds.
motivation: The rapid transition from condensation to collision-coalescence in warm clouds is poorly understood; controlled experiments are needed.
method: The paper synthesizes experimental, theoretical, and computational studies of convection-cloud chambers that reproduce key cloud microphysics.
result: Convection-cloud chambers can generate turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation, bridging laboratory and atmospheric scales.
conclusion: These chambers offer a promising platform to address the long-standing bottleneck in cloud physics.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae and their detection in multimessenger astronomy.
motivation: Core collapse supernovae are rare, multimessenger events that can provide insights into the supernova engine and neutron star physics.
method: The paper summarizes latest supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, and discusses detection methods in ground-based laser interferometers.
result: It presents progress in predicting gravitational wave signatures and parameter estimation strategies.
conclusion: Gravitational wave detection from a Galactic supernova would be a landmark event for multimessenger astronomy.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, a cosmological observation that challenges the standard ΛCDM model.
motivation: To test the cosmological principle by comparing the dipole in the large-scale matter distribution with the CMB dipole.
method: Analysis of radio galaxy and quasar catalogs to measure the matter dipole and compare it to the CMB dipole.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the two dipoles, suggesting a possible violation of the cosmological principle.
conclusion: The anomaly may indicate new physics beyond ΛCDM or unknown systematic biases.

title: Astrophysical Tests Of Dark Matter Self-interactions
authors: Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, And Jesús Zavala
abstract:
Author(s): Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, and Jesús Zavala

Dark sectors, involving new particles that couple very weakly to the standard model ones, play an important role in current model-building efforts in particle physics, as they allow, for example, for new dark matter production and interaction mechanisms. This review focuses on self-interacting dark matter scenarios, their implications on the dynamics and distribution of dark matter halos in the Universe, and the related astrophysical tests and observations, from galaxies to large-scale structures. It is embedded in the framework of the Novel Probes Project, a forum connecting observers and theorists involved in the study of astrophysical tests of dark-sector interactions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045004] Published Mon Dec 08, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews astrophysical tests of dark matter self-interactions, focusing on dark sector models and their effects on galaxy and large-scale structure formation.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and test self-interacting dark matter scenarios using astrophysical observations.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes theoretical models of self-interacting dark matter with observational constraints from galaxies, clusters, and large-scale structure.
result: It summarizes current constraints on dark matter self-interaction cross-sections and discusses implications for halo dynamics and structure formation.
conclusion: Self-interacting dark matter remains a viable alternative to cold dark matter, with ongoing and future observations expected to further constrain the parameter space.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for beyond-Standard Model physics, and the HL-LHC offers new discovery potential.
method: The paper surveys current experimental constraints and theoretical developments, and projects discovery potential across multiple search channels.
result: Stringent bounds have been placed on supersymmetric parameter space, narrowing viable models.
conclusion: The HL-LHC may discover or further constrain supersymmetry, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion reactions and their astrophysical implications.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting solar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: The review summarizes theoretical models and experimental data from the last decade on nuclear reaction rates, plasma physics, and atomic effects in the solar interior.
result: Updated reaction rates and improved solar models are presented, with comparisons to neutrino and helioseismic observations.
conclusion: The new data and theory refine our understanding of solar fusion, but the paper is purely astrophysical and unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025001] Published Thu Apr 17, 2025.
tldr: This review covers the dynamics of gas bubbles in liquids, focusing on turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes.
motivation: Understanding gas bubble dynamics is important for natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The paper is a review summarizing advances over the past 20 years in bubble dynamics, including effects of turbulence, rheology, and surfactants.
result: Key advances in modeling bubble behavior in complex fluids and turbulent flows are highlighted.
conclusion: The review provides insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems, but has no relevance to the user's research interests.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in active matter systems, focusing on polar active particles that align their orientation with their velocity.
motivation: To understand how self-alignment, as opposed to neighbor imitation, leads to novel collective behaviors in active systems, with potential applications in biology, smart materials, and robotics.
method: The paper reviews existing models and experiments on self-aligning active particles, presenting a unified mathematical framework and exploring emergent phenomena from single-particle dynamics to collective motion.
result: Self-alignment enables a wide range of behaviors including orbiting in traps, synchronized motion in dense assemblies, and other transformative collective phenomena.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a fundamental mechanism in active matter that reshapes motion emergence and offers new avenues for designing active materials and robotic swarms.

title: Using Gravitational Waves To See The First Second Of The Universe
authors: Rishav Roshan And Graham White
abstract:
Author(s): Rishav Roshan and Graham White

Gravitational waves open a unique window on the earliest times in cosmology because the dense primordial plasma, impenetrable to light or neutrinos, is transparent to gravitational waves up to the instant of the birth of the Universe. This review discusses the possible signals from the phase transitions, topological defects, and other cosmological sources, as well as a range of strategies for detection of the stochastic gravitational waves produced by the earliest events in the history of the Universe.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015001] Published Wed Jan 08, 2025.
tldr: A review of using gravitational waves to probe the early universe, focusing on phase transitions and topological defects.
motivation: Gravitational waves can penetrate the early universe's opaque plasma, offering a unique window into the first second after the Big Bang.
method: The paper reviews theoretical signals from cosmological sources like phase transitions and topological defects, and discusses detection strategies for stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds.
result: It summarizes possible gravitational wave signatures from early universe events and outlines current and future detection methods.
conclusion: Gravitational waves are a promising tool for studying the earliest moments of the universe, complementing electromagnetic and neutrino observations.

title: Defect Approach To Giant Graviton Dynamics
authors: Yunfeng Jiang And Xinan Zhou Junding Chen
abstract: We develop a framework of zero dimensional defects for analyzing light–light–heavy–heavy (LLHH) correlators in conformal field theories. We specifically apply this formalism to correlators of giant gravitons in super Yang–Mills to probe the nontrivial physics beyond planarity. By combining this framework with bootstrap techniques, we compute all four-point functions at strong coupling involving two maximal giant gravitons and two supergravitons of arbitrary dimensions. We identify a partially broken, higher-dimensional hidden symmetry—a defect extension of 10d hidden conformal symmetry–present at both strong and weak coupling, which allows these correlators to be packaged into a single generating function. Furthermore, we perform a systematic OPE analysis of the strong-coupling correlators, extracting the complete spectrum of anomalous dimensions for the defect-channel double-particle operators. Finally, we argue that the defect perspective provides the natural nonperturbative description for any LLHH correlator by showing that four-point conformal blocks reduce to defect two-point blocks in the heavy limit.
tldr: This paper develops a defect framework for analyzing LLHH correlators in conformal field theories, applied to giant gravitons in super Yang-Mills, and uncovers a hidden symmetry.
motivation: To understand non-planar corrections in AdS/CFT by studying correlators involving heavy operators like giant gravitons.
method: Combines zero-dimensional defect formalism with bootstrap techniques to compute four-point functions at strong coupling.
result: All four-point functions with two maximal giant gravitons and two supergravitons are computed, revealing a defect extension of 10d hidden conformal symmetry.
conclusion: The defect perspective provides a natural nonperturbative description for LLHH correlators in the heavy limit.

SignificanceMdxmice lack Dp427 but still express shorter isoforms. Despite their widespread use in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) research, they exhibit a relatively mild phenotype that differs from the phenotype seen in patients. TheDMDgene encodes ...
tldr: This paper studies muscle weakness and regeneration in DMD-null mice, a model for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
motivation: To understand the role of dystrophin isoforms in muscle function and regeneration, as existing mdx mice have a mild phenotype.
method: Phenotypic analysis of DMD-null mice including muscle strength tests, regeneration assays, and satellite cell function studies.
result: DMD-null mice exhibit severe muscle weakness, impaired regeneration, and deficient satellite cell function.
conclusion: DMD-null mice more closely recapitulate human DMD pathology and are a better model for studying the disease.
